title: Scrutiny of v_c regressors: form is lossy (rank), going is a blind spot
author: modelling
summary: Audit of effective-v_c terms. (1) FORM is the dominant signal but coupled through a CENSORED rank proxy (relative-finish): winning by a nose vs 10 lengths both give pos=1, discarding the margin = the …
text: scrutiny of v_c regressors: form is lossy (rank), going is a blind spot scrutiny form speed-figure going critical-power methodology v_c audit of effective-v_c terms. (1) form is the dominant signal but coupled through a censored rank proxy (relative-finish): winning by a nose vs 10 lengths both give pos=1, discarding the margin = the velocity info. mechanistic upgrade: a speed figure from lbw (lengths behind winner) + finishtime -> velocity deficit in m/s, coefficient ~1 (kinematic), normalised to a going/distance/class par. data available in results_rich. highest-value, cleanest. (2) going is a real v_c modifier (soft ground raises locomotion cost, differentially by horse) that the residual diagnosis cannot see -- it's a race-level constant that vanishes under within-race renormalisation. systematic blind spot of the whole loop; needs a calibration-by-going instrument, not the residual regression. (3) v_c estimator is a one-race min-velocity heuristic; principled version is the critical-power hyperbola d=v_c*t+w' across multi-distance runs. (4) jockey is reduced-form + selection-confounded; a clean coupling would route it through trip geometry/policy not raw v_c -- leave for now. rating is well-incorporated (resid ~0). meta: the residual instrument is blind to race-level physics (going/distance/class/track) by construction -- it will keep finding within-race mechanisms and miss condition mechanisms.

title: Full power-balance EOM underperforms kinematic by ~1.4 nats/race (win-prob)
author: modelling
summary: Tried the most-fundamental mass coupling: run the power-balance EOM (hkjc.model.eom) in production so declared mass enters every term via Newton's law, with one allometric constant b. Built dynamics.w…
text: full power-balance eom underperforms kinematic by ~1.4 nats/race (win-prob) eom mass allometric negative-result physics-migration steady-state tried the most-fundamental mass coupling: run the power-balance eom (hkjc.model.eom) in production so declared mass enters every term via newton's law, with one allometric constant b. built dynamics.win_probs + a sim='eom' path in fit.py (kinematic-calibrated gains form_gain=4, w_prime_gain=2). result on a 42-race slice: eom winner-logp -3.68 to -4.38 vs kinematic -2.30. removing drag (cda=0) recovers only ~0.7; lowering tau/noise doesn't help. the eom's dynamics (accel phase, w'-depletion fade, power smoothing) compress the ability spread the kinematic sim preserves. key insight: the (m/m_field)^(b-1) v_c factor is not an arbitrary tack-on -- it is the eom's exact steady-state solution (v_c=p_c/(k_loco*m*g), p_c=k*m^b). it captures the win-determining mass->v_c physics at kinematic accuracy; the full integrated eom only adds second-order transients that are currently mis-calibrated and hurt. making the full eom competitive needs a from-scratch recalibration (gains up, noise down, fade/drag retuned) starting 1.4 nats behind, uncertain it matches. recommendation: bake the steady-state allometric law (first-principles, ready now); treat the full dynamic-eom migration as a separate greenlit project.

text: mass coupling parked -- real residual but low-leverage (b=1 isometric optimal) mass allometric parsimony low-leverage negative-result calibrated the steady-state allometric law v_c*(m/m_field)^(b-1) on the quick backtest. b=1.0 (no mass effect) is optimal; b=1.5->47%, b=2->-9%, monotone worse. fine check: b=1.05/1.10 also worse than 1.0. so despite the confirmed-real bodywt residual (t=+8.8, survives rating+class), coupling mass to v_c does not improve goodness-of-fit -- it is low-leverage on the winner's prob, the same lesson as draw. physical reading: b~1 = isometric (aerobic power and carrying-cost both scale ~linearly with mass, cancelling) => no net v_c effect. per parsimony (physics-plausible + real-residual is not sufficient; it must move the needle), mass is left out. the high-leverage lever remains w' (+1.4pp). eom/allometric_b/dynamics.win_probs kept as inert recorded infrastructure (default b=1). next: speed-figure form (velocity vs rank).

title: Noise framing resolved: velocity-mult (=log-normal proportional time-noise) wins; statistical model can't do interactions
author: modelling
summary: Tested finishing-time noise per the standard-theory reframing. FULL-SCALE: velocity-multiplicative constant sigma_v = 48.3% (best). Finishing-TIME ADDITIVE: Gumbel->Plackett-Luce closed form peaks 46.…
text: noise framing resolved: velocity-mult (=log-normal proportional time-noise) wins; statistical model can't do interactions noise-model finishing-time plackett-luce interactions architecture parsimony tested finishing-time noise per the standard-theory reframing. full-scale: velocity-multiplicative constant sigma_v = 48.3% (best). finishing-time additive: gumbel->plackett-luce closed form peaks 46.4% @sigma_t=5s; gaussian->probit 44.9% @8s -- both slightly worse. distance-dependent noise: exp=0 (flat) best; exp=0.5 (the diffusion/first-passage sqrt(d) law) 47.7%, worse -- so the calibration-by-condition distance gradient was small-sample/awt noise, not robust. parsimony: keep sigma_v flat. reconciliation: constant-sigma_v velocity model is a finishing-time model -- log-normal noise proportional to time (sigma_t ∝ mu), the standard model for positive performance quantities; data prefers proportional over additive. key caveat (user): the purely statistical framework (probit/pl/softmax) cannot mechanistically model interactions -- blocking, real-time tactics, jockey policy. that is the agent-based sim's reason to exist (the physics+game-theory core). corrected architecture conclusion: probit = fast dev surrogate for the win-calibration loop (35x, matches because interactions are low-leverage for win); the agent-based sim stays as the production substrate for interactions/policy/exotics. not a replacement. pl/time/probit kept as documented fit.py modes. noise + statistical-reformulation levers exhausted. remaining concrete lever: awt 1650m badly miscalibrated (13%).

title: FUTURE DIRECTION: stat-mech / condensed-matter machinery for the interaction layer
author: modelling
summary: User idea (later, not now). The race is a driven, interacting, non-equilibrium many-body system; condensed-matter / stat-mech gives the right tools to go from MICRO interactions to MACRO finishing-ord…
text:
future direction: stat-mech / condensed-matter machinery for the interaction layer future-direction stat-mech condensed-matter interactions mean-field-games tasep plackett-luce game-theory user idea (later, not now). the race is a driven, interacting, non-equilibrium many-body system; condensed-matter / stat-mech gives the right tools to go from micro interactions to macro finishing-order observables, potentially semi-analytically (vs brute-force monte-carlo). concrete mappings to explore:
- blocking -> exclusion processes (tasep / multi-lane asep): the car-following 'can't pass through' is hard-core exclusion -- the canonical solved model for traffic; gives current-density relations, jamming, and correlation functions analytically.
- drafting -> active matter / self-propelled particles with wake-attraction (peloton dynamics).
- jockey policy / tactics -> mean-field games (lasry-lions): the continuum limit of n agents optimising pace/position simultaneously = coupled hjb (optimal control) + fokker-planck (density). this is the rigorous mathematical home for the project's physics(plant)+game-theory(policy) thesis -- the 'best-response pace layer' is a mean-field game.
- quenched disorder (abilities) -> replica/cavity for the outcome distribution over ability disorder.
unifying picture: plackett-luce is the free (non-interacting) theory -- independent finishing times. interactions (exclusion/drafting/tactics) are couplings on top => an 'interacting plackett-luce' / effective field theory whose observables are the finishing-order probabilities; the agent-based sim is its monte-carlo, stat-mech could give analytic/perturbative (cluster/virial-expansion) results. this bridges the fast statistical model (free theory, great for win) and the interaction modelling (perturbations, matters for place/exotics/policy).

title: Diffusion law (Inverse-Gaussian first-passage) tested: ties the in-place log-normal noise
author: modelling
summary: Per the diffusion-law correction: finishing time = first-passage of dx=v·dt+sqrt(2D)·dW => INVERSE GAUSSIAN (Wald), strictly positive, Var(T)=2D·L/v^3. Implemented sim='wald' (one physical param, diff…
text: diffusion law (inverse-gaussian first-passage) tested: ties the in-place log-normal noise diffusion inverse-gaussian wald first-passage noise-model unification foundation per the diffusion-law correction: finishing time = first-passage of dx=v·dt+sqrt(2d)·dw => inverse gaussian (wald), strictly positive, var(t)=2d·l/v^3. implemented sim='wald' (one physical param, diffusion coef d). full-scale sweep: peaks d~160-180 -> 47.7%, vs velocity-multiplicative (=log-normal time) 48.2% -- a tie within noise. both are correct positive-time models, both one numpy call (equal efficiency); fit marginally favors the log-normal already in place. conclusion: the noise foundation is validated -- the principled diffusion law agrees with the in-place model to ~0.5pp, so adopting the diffusion framing later (for interactions) costs nothing. unifying picture: each horse = drift-diffusion particle (drift=ability, diffusion=d). non-interacting limit = independent inverse-gaussian finishing times (the fast win surrogate). with interactions (exclusion=blocking/tasep, coupling=drafting, policy=mean-field game) = the agent-based sim is the monte-carlo of the same many-body drift-diffusion. so the fast surrogate and the interacting sim are one model at different interaction orders -- the substrate for the stat-mech program. keep log-normal noise for now (marginally better, in place); diffusion is the principled foundation for the interaction layer. fit.py keeps probit/pl/time/wald as documented modes.

title: AWT fix in the diffusion framework: D_awt = 2x D_turf (no ad-hoc velocity knob)
author: modelling
summary: AWT (1650m) was 13% of market (over-confident + weak ability transfer). FIRST attempt used an ad-hoc multiplier on velocity speed_noise -- wrong framework (user). CORRECT: in the diffusion (Wald) mode…
text: awt fix in the diffusion framework: d_awt = 2x d_turf (no ad-hoc velocity knob) awt diffusion surface noise-model ability-transfer calibration awt (1650m) was 13% of market (over-confident + weak ability transfer). first attempt used an ad-hoc multiplier on velocity speed_noise -- wrong framework (user). correct: in the diffusion (wald) model the noise is the diffusion coefficient d; awt is simply a more diffusive surface (kickback, less reliable turf-trained signal) => larger d. calibrated (wald, d_turf=170): awt d = 2x turf d is optimal -> awt 16.7%->23.7% (vs 12.7% velocity baseline), overall 47.4->47.7%, turf unchanged 48.8%. a clean physical statement (awt 2x as diffusive), one surface-dependent physical parameter, not a tuned velocity knob. remaining: awt 23.7% << turf 48.8% is the genuine ability-transfer weakness (model ranks awt winners at percentile 0.59 vs 0.70 turf) -- the turf-dominated form/v_c doesn't apply to all-weather; surface-specific ability is the fix but data-starved (awt ~6% of races). timing: wald sampling 1.6x probit (inv-gaussian vs gaussian), both ~30-40s full-scale; closed-form pl is ~2000x faster (no sampling) -- the instant proxy for sweeps. architecture: this is the case for adopting diffusion as the noise model (physical, condition-dependence is real, interaction-ready); ~0.5pp turf cost vs velocity-mult. eventually the agent-based sim's integrator should use per-timestep sqrt(2d)dw (non-interacting limit = wald).

text: breakthrough: recency-weighted form (half-life ~2 races) lifts st 48% -> 56% of market (+7.8pp) recency form breakthrough ability shrinkage knob-scan knob scan found the biggest lever of the session. replacing the career expanding-mean form with an exp-weighted (recency) form, half-life ~2 races: career 48.1% -> recency 55.9%. half-life sweep is a clean smooth interior optimum (0.7->49.4, 1.0->53.4, 1.5->55.6, 2.0->55.9, 3.0->55.2, 5.0->53.6, 10->51.4, career->48.1) -- the signature of real signal. leak-verified: recency_form_table uses ewm_mean().shift(1).over(horse_id), strictly prior (first run null); manually confirmed prior-only. this overturns the old 'recency doesn't transfer to the abm' finding (that was the stale form_gain=2 abm). mechanism: career-average form is stale over hk's long careers (horses improve/decline, change class); recency tracks current ability and aligns with how the market weights recent runs -> big %market jump. action: make recency form (hl~2) the production form; re-calibrate form_gain and re-confirm w_prime_gain/jockey_gain/shrink_mult under it (the form spread changed). also found this scan: eb shrink_mult on the sectional v_c residual is over-trusted -- 0.5 (48.8%) and even 0.0 (48.5%) beat 1.0 (48.1%); the sectional energetics barely earns its keep for win. trainer parked (+0.2pp, redundant with jockey+rating).

title: Model lineup: drop probit (velocity-mult); Wald (diffusion) is production, PL the fast probe
author: modelling
summary: Per the first-principles mindframe, dropped the probit (velocity-multiplicative) win model -- an odd in-between: noise on velocity not the physical finishing-time observable, and a one-shot draw not a…
text: model lineup: drop probit (velocity-mult); wald (diffusion) is production, pl the fast probe wald diffusion probit plackett-luce model-lineup jax n_samples first-principles per the first-principles mindframe, dropped the probit (velocity-multiplicative) win model -- an odd in-between: noise on velocity not the physical finishing-time observable, and a one-shot draw not a diffusion. also dropped the additive-gaussian 'time' mode (allows t<0). lineup now: sim='wald' (default, the production win model -- drift-diffusion first-passage / inverse-gaussian, the principled noise law, one physical d, surface-dependent awt 2x, ~55.5% of market); sim='pl' (closed-form plackett-luce, instant, the fast-and-dirty probe); sim='kinematic' (jax traffic sim, for interactions/exotics only -- traffic low-leverage for win); sim='eom' (inert infra). wald speedup (user asked, jax available): jax only 1.2x on cpu (no gpu; the ig sampling is memory-bound; a single batched (races,ns,n) call is worse, 195s). the real quick win is n_samples: 4000->55.3%, 8000->55.5%, 20000->55.5% -- ~3x faster at 4k for <0.2pp. production n_samples=6000 already fine. further option (not done): the ig is near-gaussian here (mu/lam~0.02), so a sampling-free gaussian-approx probit with the diffusion variance could be ~instant -- an approximation to verify. studies repointed probit->wald; model_state + sim constant updated.

text: re-diagnosis at the recency (56%) baseline rebalanced the ability gains: form_gain 4->5, w_prime_gain 2->1 recalibration form-gain w-prime-gain re-diagnosis recency wald parsimony the recency-form switch changed the residual regime, so the gains baked for career form went stale. fresh market-residual diagnosis (sim=wald): form flipped to under-weighted (t=+11.4 at fg=4) because recency form is a sharper, higher-variance signal than the career mean; w_prime flipped to over-weighted (t=-8.95) because recency form absorbed the reserve signal. recalibrated: form_gain 4->5 (clean interior optimum, +0.9pp full scale; 6-7 fall off a cliff); w_prime_gain 2->1 (win-prob impact flat over 0-2 -- w' is a finishing-margin effect, low-leverage on who wins -- so parsimony + the residual sign both say revert the amplification we added in the career era). diff_coef d=170 already optimal (sharper hurts, so v_c_eb's under-trust is not a global-confidence problem). re-diagnosis confirms: form neutralised (->-8.7, the fg optimum edge), v_c_eb +14.5->-4.0, w_prime ->+1.4. method note: speed_noise is a no-op under wald (wald uses diff_coef, not speed_noise) -- don't sweep it for the production model. also fixed quick_eval determinism: polars unique() is not order-stable, so the test_cap subsample jittered ~1.7pp run-to-run; sorted the ids.

title: BREAKTHROUGH: re-added bend ground-loss to the wald drift (DRAW_GAIN=0.003) -> ST 56->58% of market
author: modelling
summary: The #1 residual at 56% was draw (t=-26.5). ROOT CAUSE: production wald (and pl) had NO draw term at all -- draw/bend_curvature lived ONLY in the kinematic geometry sim, and was silently DROPPED when w…
text: breakthrough: re-added bend ground-loss to the wald drift (draw_gain=0.003) -> st 56->58% of market draw bend-ground-loss wald breakthrough interaction abm re-diagnosis first-principles the #1 residual at 56% was draw (t=-26.5). root cause: production wald (and pl) had no draw term at all -- draw/bend_curvature lived only in the kinematic geometry sim, and was silently dropped when wald became production. (the naive 'over-weights' label was wrong: the model had zero draw signal while the market prices the inside-draw advantage.) fix (physics, not a regressor): a horse drawn k lanes off the rail runs a longer arc round the turns -> larger effective distance -> longer first-passage time. l_eff = dist*(1+draw_gain*(draw-1)) in the wald/pl drift. geometry fixes the sign; the magnitude is calibrated and absorbs jockeys steering toward the rail. clean monotone sweep, broad peak 0.003-0.004; baked 0.003 -> +1.9pp full scale (56.2->58.1%), residual collapsed t=-26.5->-1.5, model ece 0.0060 (better than market's 0.0069). sanity check: 0.003/lane => draw-14 vs draw-1 runs ~3.9% (~62m) longer over 1600m -- the right order for the extra arc of being ~13 lanes wider round the turns, so the calibrated magnitude lands in the geometric ballpark (physical, not a fudge). interaction (per user: draw is a proxy for geometry and collision -- horses are not collisionless, the abm's original motivation): the residual has a field-size gradient (small fields over-penalised, crowded under) -- the collision fingerprint. but a mean-field field-size modulation (draw_fs_gain, wired+unbaked) recovers only ~0.1pp; the full draw x crowding / boxed-in / draw x pace structure is genuinely the agent-based sim's job (place/exotics). lesson: a 'parked / low-leverage' verdict can go stale when the production sim changes -- always re-check parked items against the current production path. bodywt (t=+9.6) is the next such re-check.

text: bodywt re-checked on the production wald path: real but small (~0.8pp) -- not a needle-mover, parked bodywt mass wald parked low-leverage structural ability-model next-direction bodywt was the #1 residual at 58% (t=+9.6). like draw, production wald had no mass term (the allometric v_c law lived only in the kinematic/eom path). re-checked on wald with two untested channels: (1) mass->drift (heavier = higher effective v_c, additive z-coupling) peaks ~+0.8pp at mass_vc_gain~0.1 then collapses past 0.2; (2) mass->noise (heavier = sharper, smaller d) is falsified -- monotonically hurts. so the drift channel is real and physical (heavier = more muscle = more sustainable power, b slightly >1) but only ~0.8pp -- below the user's 5%-move bar. not baked (parsimony + anti-bloat); probe code reverted, no params left in fit.py. broader read: the diagnose->recalibrate loop on the current feature set is at diminishing returns -- remaining residuals are all <1pp (bodywt 0.8, actwt smaller). the big session wins were structural (recency form +7.8, re-added draw +1.9 -- missing mechanisms, not gain tweaks). the path to 70% is a structurally better ability estimate (opponent-strength-adjusted form / a coherent latent rating; distance-aptitude curves), not more residual whack-a-mole. confirmed: the additive ability composite is the next thing to revamp.

title: Research round (6 parallel dimension probes): HV is broken (#1 lever, ~10pp); pace + rest-days are real medium leads
author: modelling
summary: Dispatched 6 read-only subagents across the THEORY dimensions to measure market-residual headroom at the 58% (ST) baseline. Findings, ranked by leverage: [BIG, >=5pp] PER-VENUE CALIBRATION — HV is bro…
text:
research round (6 parallel dimension probes): hv is broken (#1 lever, ~10pp); pace + rest-days are real medium leads research-round per-venue hv draw pace lone-leader days-since-run opponent-adjusted interactions sectionals headroom dispatched 6 read-only subagents across the theory dimensions to measure market-residual headroom at the 58% (st) baseline. findings, ranked by leverage:
[big, >=5pp] per-venue calibration — hv is broken. hv = 47.6% of market vs st 57.9% (-10.3pp). two agents converged: (a) the st-calibrated global draw_gain=0.003 massively over-penalises draw at hv (hv draw residual t=-31.9 vs st t=-1.4; slope 25x larger, uniform across hv courses); hv form also over-weighted (t=-13.7 vs -8.4). (b) the kinematic abm beats wald by +2-3pp at hv (matched samples) but loses ~4pp on st — divergence is draw-driven (kinematic better on wide draws in large fields, worse on inside draws via a rail-blocking artefact). so hv wants its own draw_gain (~0) + form_gain, and the abm may be the right hv win model. also: st 1000m straight chute has the draw sign wrong (inner draws disadvantaged at the chute, model penalises wide) -> distance-conditional draw fix (152 races, 46% bucket). small st fields/sprints over-confident.
[medium, 1-3pp] pace — front-runner/lone-leader residual is real (fr t~9-13 both venues, survives form; lone-leader market-model gap +1.3pp at hv; packedfront contested-pace hv-specific). crucial: the old pace falsification was for the `style` feature (corr only 0.12 with the positional proxy trail_early_pos_norm), so a lone-leader / early-position coupling in wald is genuinely untested and physically grounded (lone leader saves energy, controls pace).
[small, 0.5-1.5pp] condition — days-since-run rest premium (28-60d t=+5.9, survives 7-covariate multivariate; >120d penalty t=-3.3). body-weight delta = noise. gear = data-limited (not in results_rich). mechanism: muscle recovery peaks 4-8wk.
[small, ~0.3pp] sectionals — dense mean-velocity as speedfig adds ~+0.3pp over the existing parked speedfig; market is largely efficient w.r.t. sectionals; the cp-w' across-runs hyperbola is noise here (too few trip-varied prior runs). cv trajectories unlikely to help win (maybe draw geometry).
[not a lever now] opponent-adjusted ability — residual correlation real (t~4.6, leak-safe, control-stable) but does not convert to %market in any leak-free test (collinear ~0.70 with own rtg; the rating channel already prices it). the proper test is a self-consistent fixed-point rating (elo/bt) replacing form, not a bolt-on add-on — a bigger build, uncertain payoff.
[not a lever on st] interactions for win — kinematic abm net negative on st (~-4pp, over-penalises inside draws); its value is hv win + exotics/place, not st win.
meta-lesson: the production model was calibrated entirely on st and applied globally -> hv and st-1000m are mis-served. same 'parked verdict goes stale when the production path changes' lesson, now at the venue/distance level. next step is the user's call (no changes made; all probes read-only).

title: Research round 2 (4 agents): pace POSITIONAL-FADE is the next clean lever; data-mining goldmine (weather/formline/vet); going=noise; drone=defer
author: modelling
summary: PER-VENUE calibration DONE (committed): HV 47.6->52.5% (+4.9pp). Four more read-only agents returned: [STRATEGY — the next clean lever] Pace mechanistic probe REFRAMED the pace signal. The lone-leader…
text:
research round 2 (4 agents): pace positional-fade is the next clean lever; data-mining goldmine (weather/formline/vet); going=noise; drone=defer research-round-2 per-venue hv pace positional-fade data-mining weather wind formline veterinary going drone cv competition game-theory theory-first per-venue calibration done (committed): hv 47.6->52.5% (+4.9pp). four more read-only agents returned:
[strategy — the next clean lever] pace mechanistic probe reframed the pace signal. the lone-leader bonus is not robust (threshold-fragile, n~70, sign flips). the robust, both-venue, ground-truth-confirmed signal is a positional fade: the wald model over-rates early-front horses and under-rates closers (front horses win ~1pp less than the model says; closers ~1pp more; market already partly corrects this). trail_early_pos_norm residual t=-7.0 st / -6.5 hv controlling for form+v_c+w_prime. recommended coupling: v_c_eff = v_c*(1 - pos_fade_gain*(proj_early_pos - field_mean)), pos_fade_gain>0 (front=>higher mu=slower; closer=>bonus), proj_early_pos = eb-shrunk mean of prior trail_early_pos_norm. physics: front-runners burn w' against air with no draft; closers conserve. one scalar gain on v_c, mirrors draw_gain. ~1-1.7pp, mean-field (both venues same sign). hold per user: deepen the strategy/game-theory theory first before wiring.
[data-mining goldmine — browser+http] (1) new graphql `weather` op on the same endpoint: per-section wind vectors (4 anemometers/venue) + soil volumetric water content / moisture-loss / rain — fills the environment cell (wind term + a continuous going/firmness proxy far better than the categorical going string). (2) `formline` = hkjc-precomputed opponent-linkage (collateral form: which of today's rivals met before, with weight/rating deltas) — the raw material for the competition axis. (3) `exceptionalfactors` (gear/bit/new-trainer/conghua-return + trainer multi-entries), `veterinaryrecord`/`overecord` (dated lameness/surgery/eiph -> the health cell), `localtrackwork` (timed gallops + conghua/st location), `btresult` (barrier-trial times/sectionals). (4) graphql `trainerpreference` (stable's own-runner rank) + `trumpcard` (confidence flag) are already in our query body, just unextracted. (5) doc fix: the pre-race angle pages are ssr-fetchable with requests but only in the pre-race window (populated for the imminent meeting, cleared after). penetrometer/hammer unreliable -> use weather soil-moisture instead. -> update docs/hkjc_data.md.
[going] noise-level lever. no systematic turf miscalibration by going (firm/good and soft buckets both ~57% of market). going-affinity collapses to t=0.74 once >=2 prior same-going runs required (the t=2.6 was 1-sample noise). bounded by soft-going sparsity (40% of soft runners have any prior soft run; <1% have >=5). revisit only with continuous firmness (the weather soil-moisture feed!) or many more seasons.
[drone/cv] defer. the only win-relevant target dense paths would touch is draw/bend ground-loss + traffic (not speed — market efficient there), but the mean draw effect is already priced by draw_gain, the cv output is currently unusable (poc: 0 tracks >19 frames, identity unsolved, homography broken), and the no-cv queue (hv, pace, rest-days) is cheaper and bigger. build cv only for place/exotics later, if ever.
competition-axis reframe (per user): the opponent/competition axis is not dead — only the simplistic treatments (elo, relative form) failed. the deeper game-theoretic mechanics (jockeys observe rivals' running styles and best-respond; pace equilibrium; the handicap as adversarial design) are unexplored. general principle: a dead first attempt != a dead axis; we may just not understand the mechanics yet. next per user: develop theoretical depth on strategy/competition/game-theory before rushing implementation.

title: Three-front push: kinematic-ABM-dead premise overturned, DRAW_FS (HV +0.3pp) banked, pace-interaction + debut-RTG refuted; barrier-trial backfill underway
author: modelling
summary: Three-front push (ABM revamp + new-data + debut). Net model change: HV 53.8->54.1% (+0.3pp), ST 60.0% unchanged. The real value was decisive INTELLIGENCE. ABM FRONT -- premise OVERTURNED (CORRECTS 002…
text:
three-front push: kinematic-abm-dead premise overturned, draw_fs (hv +0.3pp) banked, pace-interaction + debut-rtg refuted; barrier-trial backfill underway abm interaction draw-fs crowding pace-pressure refuted conversion-test paired-seed method debut prior-starts barrier-trials new-data saturation hv three-front push (abm revamp + new-data + debut). net model change: hv 53.8->54.1% (+0.3pp), st 60.0% unchanged. the real value was decisive intelligence.

abm front -- premise overturned (corrects 0025). the 'kinematic abm beats wald at hv +2-3pp' claim was stale -- it predated the per-venue wald bakes. at the current baseline the kinematic sim loses to wald at hv by -4.1pp (48.8 vs 52.9, paired quick_eval); its uncalibrated emergent-geometry draw is now worse than wald's tuned per-venue draw 0.008. do not promote the slow jax sim to production. the interaction axis instead pays as mean-field shadow terms on the fast wald path (the abm = theory generator, like pos_fade):
  * baked draw_fs_gain (crowding x draw): dg = draw_g*max(0,1+gain*(n-12)), a wide draw costs more in a crowded field (boxed-in), clamped >=0. per-venue hv-only (hv 0.25 -> +0.3pp; st flat). the clamp matters: the linear form reversed the penalty into a wide-draw bonus in small fields.
  * refuted relational pace-pressure (theory 3b #1): front-runner w'-burn scaling with rival front-runner count, driven by the converting early_pos signal, as a clean symmetric interaction (contested->fade, lone leader steals it, closers boosted). hv +0.12pp (noise), st flat. the 4th flat result on the pace axis (pace_gain, contestedness, eom, pace_press). pos_fade already absorbs the convertible pace signal. pace axis closed.

method lesson (important): the 150-race quick_eval wildly over-states a knob -- draw_fs read +1-1.6pp on quick_eval, +0.3pp hv/0.0 st at full scale (~4x). and the full-backtest mc seed is hash(race_id), pythonhashseed-salted -> +-0.3-0.5pp run-to-run. fix baked into method: confirm every candidate with a paired full-scale test at pythonhashseed=0 (base+candidate share per-race seeds; delta is pure mechanism). quick_eval is for scouting sign only.

debut front -- rtg-suppression quick-win does not convert (built+tested e2e). premise real (fab. rtg corr -0.04, anti-predictive) but: the v_c rating slope is tiny (~0.04 m/s over the debut spread vs form's ~2 m/s), the model is already calibrated on debuts (mean p 0.065 vs actual win 0.068), and ~35% of 'debutants' carry a real handicapper rating (hk rates first-timers off trials/breeding) so uniform suppression discards signal. a debut-jockey gain hurt (hv 33->28%). kept the leak-free prior_starts feature (committed) as the debut flag for the real fix. the market is efficient on debuts via existing signal -- debuts need new signal, not reweighting.

data front -- barrier trials are the genuine next lever (verified live). btresult (ssr html, ?date=dd/mm/yyyy): clean horse_id join, history to 2018, inherently pre-race, trial field dominated by debutants (11/19 sample = unraced foals). trial_time + 3 sectionals + lbw = a real v_c/w' velocity prior for first-timers (same energetics machinery). prototype studies/newdata_probe.py + samples. a 2022-2026 historical backfill is running -> data_cache/barrier_trials.parquet; next: a leak-free trial-form feature + conversion test (esp. debut subset). secondary: weather (continuous soil-moisture going proxy, graphql weather op, poll-and-log) and formline (reconstruct collateral-form graph from our localresults).

convergent conclusion: the mean-field/interaction terms on existing data are saturated (one hv +0.3pp term from a whole pass; pace axis closed). the next real % gain requires new data -- barrier trials first.

title: Draw & the interaction axis are DEFERRED not rejected: draw is geometry × CONTROL coupled (needs a joint jockey-policy game, not a regression term)
author: modelling
summary: User steer (important framing correction): the draw effect — and the pace/competition interaction axis generally — must be DEFERRED, not REJECTED. WHY the simple treatments fail: draw is not a static …
text:
draw & the interaction axis are deferred not rejected: draw is geometry × control coupled (needs a joint jockey-policy game, not a regression term) draw control geometry interaction deferred theory game-theory jockey-policy competition mean-field abm-deprecation user steer (important framing correction): the draw effect — and the pace/competition interaction axis generally — must be deferred, not rejected.

why the simple treatments fail: draw is not a static geometric covariate. it is deeply coupled to the control dimension — the jockey's policy (how the gate is used to take up position, when to commit, how the trip is navigated). a regression / mean-field term (draw_gain, draw_fs_gain, a scalar contestedness×pos_fade, the relational pace-pressure term) can only capture the first-order geometric shadow of a fundamentally geometry × control phenomenon. that is why those probes don't convert — the mechanism is real, we just haven't modelled it deeply enough. the first-attempt abm did reproduce the qualitative draw/trip characteristics (a point in favour of the picture), even though its hand-tuned implementation was low-leverage for win and was deprecated from the codebase.

direction: the proper treatment is a joint differential / mean-field game of jockeys navigating the geometry (the theory §3b competition game), with draw as a boundary condition on that game — geometry + control modelled together. until that theory exists, treat draw_gain/draw_fs_gain as interim stopgaps and keep the axis open. this is the most promising piece of deep theory-building left — a theory build, not a regression probe.

action taken: re-framed theory.md (appendix), model_state (section a + a deferred-not-refuted note), and the draw_fs_gain constant comment from 'interaction axis closed / refuted' to 'deferred pending a geometry×control theory'. the abm-sim code deprecation stands (greenlit; physics preserved in theory.md), but the axis is open.

title: MILESTONE: ST 62.6% / HV 59.3% — new-data + structural fan-out (barrier trials, collateral-form, rating-peakgap, fade) breaks the mean-field saturation
author: modelling
summary: MILESTONE: ST 60.0->62.6%, HV 54.1->59.3% (+2.6 / +5.2pp) — driven ENTIRELY by NEW DATA + NEW STRUCTURE from a 6-agent theory-dimension fan-out, none of it a reweighting of priced features. The HV-ST …
text:
milestone: st 62.6% / hv 59.3% — new-data + structural fan-out (barrier trials, collateral-form, rating-peakgap, fade) breaks the mean-field saturation milestone barrier-trials new-data collateral-form competition massey peakgap process-feature trajectory fade fan-out conversion-test coherent-bayes training-load 70-percent-push milestone: st 60.0->62.6%, hv 54.1->59.3% (+2.6 / +5.2pp) — driven entirely by new data + new structure from a 6-agent theory-dimension fan-out, none of it a reweighting of priced features. the hv-st gap closed from ~6 to ~3pp.

banked (all committed, conversion-gated by paired fixed-seed full-scale; ablation-confirmed to stack):
- barrier trials (trial_gain per-venue): the first new-data lever. full 4-yr backfill (27,909 trials, 94.8% debut coverage) -> st +1.9pp. a debutant's only on-track form; market efficient on debuts via the rating, so genuinely new.
- collateral-form (collat_gain): the competition axis cracked. a relational massey opponent-strength velocity rating (credits margins vs strong fields), not scalar elo (which failed, collinear w/ rtg). hv +2.3pp, ece improves.
- rating-peakgap (peakgap_gain): a process feature (own rtg - own prior peak). hv +2.4pp. lesson: trajectory pays only where it adds an absolute landmark the point can't express; rating velocity/accel did not convert (restate form).
- trajectory fade (fade_gain): late-velocity hold (w' signature), +0.2/0.1pp.

refuted as simple terms (but several alive with new data): physiology-from-race-history (layoff/banister/own-weight all ~0 partial corr — a race outcome is a coarse training proxy; alive only via real training-load), sustained-speed (priced), rating velocity/accel (restate form).

generalizable lessons (both user-framed): (1) process features (sequence/trajectory) beat point features only where they carry an absolute landmark recency-form doesn't already price (peak-deficit yes; velocity no). (2) the path past the mean-field 'saturation' is new data the market sees but the model doesn't + structural signals (relational opponent-strength, career landmarks) — not more per-horse residual terms.

theory: integrated §3c (geometry x control game; draw as a boundary condition on jockey policy; o1-o5 testable obs).

forward (user-steered): (1) coherent bayesian fusion — fold trials, then training gallops, into the same eb ability posterior as races (down-weighted), replacing the additive trial_gain proxy so shrinkage handles the green->established gradient and the denser prior helps non-debutees. (2) training-load (localtrackwork daily gallops + vet records — confirmed historically scrapeable & leak-free) as the densest prior. (3) cv video/gait. (4) geometry x control o1.

title: Queue #33: CV(T) ∝ 1/√L CONFIRMED on turf; D roughly constant (no L-term needed); AWT carries a real variance floor
author: modelling
summary: DESCRIPTIVE population study (not a predictive feature → no as-of/leak-free constraint; within-race de-meaning removes field-strength + going, leaving the residual stochastic spread). Panel: data_cach…
text:
queue #33: cv(t) ∝ 1/√l confirmed on turf; d roughly constant (no l-term needed); awt carries a real variance floor theory variance distance-law queue-33 diffusion d-floor cv descriptive population study (not a predictive feature → no as-of/leak-free constraint; within-race
de-meaning removes field-strength + going, leaving the residual stochastic spread). panel:
data_cache/results_rich.parquet (39,428 runners, 3,248 races, 2022-09 → 2026-05, per-horse finishtime
in seconds — clean, monotone with pla, no dnf sentinels). study + plot:
studies/cv_distance_law.py → studies/out/cv_distance_law.png.

method. within-race cv(t) = sd(finishtime)/mean(finishtime) per race (the sd de-means the race →
strips field strength/going), aggregated per bucket l × venue × surface (turf vs all-weather from
course). scaling test: regress log cv on log l. floor test: regress log d on log l and fit the
time-floor model var(t) = 2·d0·l/v³ + σ0² (σ0² = a distance-independent variance chunk).

=== does 1/√l hold? yes — strongly, on turf. ===
fitted slope of log cv on log l (theory predicts −0.5):
  • bucket-level (each l×venue×surface a point, n≥30):  slope = −0.507, 95% ci [−0.84, −0.17], r²=0.45
  • turf pooled-by-distance (9 cells):                  slope = −0.39,  95% ci [−0.58, −0.20], r²=0.71
  • per-race turf (n=2933):                             slope = −0.62,  95% ci [−0.72, −0.53], r²=0.054
  • per-race st turf −0.72 / hv turf −0.54 / awt −0.47.
the −0.5 prediction sits inside every ci. cv falls cleanly 1000m→1650/1800m (turf 0.92%→0.66%),
i.e. longer races are intrinsically more predictable, parameter-free, exactly as theory §3e predicts.
(the per-race slope reads slightly steeper than −0.5 but its r² is tiny — it's noise-dominated; the
bucket means, where the signal lives, land on −0.5.)

=== the d(l) floor — is d constant? on turf, yes. ===
back-out d from cv²=2d/(l·v), v=l/mean(t):
  log d on log l (turf):  slope = +0.12, 95% ci [−0.27, +0.50] — indistinguishable from 0.
  ⇒ theory's simplest form (d constant in l) holds on turf. d ≈ 0.6–0.8 m²/s across the middle
    distances; the implied-d table is flat with a faint u (mild lift at the 1400m and 2400m cells,
    the latter only 12 races — small-sample, not a trend).
the time-floor fit on turf: d0 ≈ 0.70 m²/s, σ0 ≈ 0.15 s — the distance-independent chunk is only
~10% of the variance at 1000m and ~3% at 2200m. so on turf there is no material sprint over-dispersion
beyond 1/√l: a d(l) floor term is not warranted.

=== the one exception — all-weather track. ===
awt is both more diffusive and floored:  d0 ≈ 0.94 m²/s (vs turf 0.70 — consistent with the baked
awt_diff_mult=2.0 surface-d), and a large time-floor σ0 ≈ 0.46 s = ~36% of the variance in awt
sprints (1200m) vs ~26% at 1800m. awt sprints carry a big distance-independent variance pile — the
kickback/dirt "bad-break/check costs the same seconds at any l" mechanism §3e names. if any d(l)
floor is ever added, it belongs on awt, not turf.

=== venue structure (consistent with the model's priors). ===
hv turf cv sits systematically below st turf at every shared distance (e.g. 1200m hv 0.79% vs st
0.94%); implied d_hv ≈ 0.58–0.80 vs d_st ≈ 0.69–0.92. hv's smaller fields + tighter handicap blanket
finishes → lower residual spread. this is the descriptive backdrop to the evt field-size argument
(§3e): st runs the big fields where d has the most order-statistic leverage — the same split that
made draw→d (draw_var_gain) convert st-only.

=== modelling implications ===
1. the production homogeneous-wald variance law (var ∝ l, cv ∝ 1/√l) is empirically vindicated on
   turf — the slope is −0.5 and d shows no l-trend. the parameter-free §3e prediction passes a direct
   data check (theory-confirms-data).
2. a distance-dependent d(l) floor is not needed on turf (the queue's open "distance-floor d(l)" item
   can be closed for turf — the sprint cells are not under-dispersed relative to 1/√l). keep it open
   only for awt, where σ0≈0.46s is real; an awt-specific additive d floor (var += σ0²) is the correct
   structure there, and awt is already the surface flagged as extra-diffusive.
3. supports draw→d rather than complicating it. the variance knob is well-behaved (constant d in l on
   turf) so the draw→d lever sits on a stable base; and because d has the most leverage in big fields
   (st) and cv is largest in the short/awt cells, the §3e prioritisation rule is reinforced: pursue
   per-horse d_i (#28) and variance levers in st big fields / sprints first. for per-horse d_i (#28):
   the within-race cv floor (~0.6–0.9% turf) is the population baseline a horse's own figure-spread
   should modulate around — d_i should scale the bucket d, not replace it.
4. caveat: this is a population/descriptive study (within-race spread, all runners) — it validates the
   law's l-scaling and the d-constancy, not the per-horse d_i heterogeneity, which is #28's job.

title: "Queue #28: per-horse D_i from a horse's own figure-spread — converts ST (+0.19% +ECE, BAKE), fails HV ECE gate (DON'T-BAKE)"
author: modelling
summary: HYPOTHESIS (THEORY §3d/§3e — the D-heterogeneity knob, the variance third knob applied PER HORSE). Every banked signal moves the MEAN drift; the only variance lever so far (DRAW_VAR_GAIN) is a geometr…
text:
"queue #28: per-horse d_i from a horse's own figure-spread — converts st (+0.19% +ece, bake), fails hv ece gate (don't-bake)" theory variance diffusion d-heterogeneity queue-28 figure-spread speed-figure conversion-test third-knob evt field-size draft hypothesis (theory §3d/§3e — the d-heterogeneity knob, the variance third knob applied per horse).
every banked signal moves the mean drift; the only variance lever so far (draw_var_gain) is a
geometry/field effect, not the horse's own consistency. a horse whose past speed figures are tightly
clustered is a low-variance runner; one whose figures swing wildly is genuinely less predictable, so
its diffusion d_i should scale with the spread of its own prior figures. because the winner is an
order statistic, variance is as load-bearing as the mean — a high-d horse upsets more than its drift
implies. queue #29 (the cv∝1/√l study) established d is constant in l on turf, so this is
heterogeneity across horses around that stable population baseline, not a distance effect.

construction.
- feature `features.speed_figure_dispersion_table` (mirrors `speed_figure_table`): per-run figure
  `sf = v_run − par(going,dist)` (m/s vs a condition standard), then the per-horse trait = the
  strictly-prior standard deviation of `sf` over the horse's prior runs (expanding std shifted by one,
  computed welford-style from lagged running sums of `sf` and `sf²`). shrinkage toward the population
  dispersion σ_pop (panel mean of the per-horse stds, ≈0.147 m/s) with weight `n/(n+3)`; a horse with
  ≤1 prior run gets σ_pop exactly (neutral). population: mean 0.148, iqr 0.120–0.159, fat tail to 2.2
  m/s — real per-horse heterogeneity in figure-consistency.
- knob `fit.fit_predict_traffic(figvar_gain=)` wired into the wald variance beside `draw_var_gain`:
  `d_i = d·(1 + gain·(disp_i/disp̄ − 1))`, field-mean-normalised so the population-average horse keeps
  the baseline d — a pure redistribution of variance, conserving the field-mean d (so global
  calibration is preserved). clamped ≥0.05·d. swept param, default `figvar_gain=0.0` ⇒ no-op. baked
  default off at both venues (`figvar_gain_by_venue={"st":0,"hv":0}`) — production untouched.

leak-free proof. direct check (pythonhashseed=0): for a 56-run career horse, the emitted `fig_disp`
at each run equals the hand-computed shrunk std over exactly that run's strictly-prior figures (match
to 1e-6; n≤1 → σ_pop). `par` is a race-condition constant (not the horse's own outcome) ⇒ leak-free,
same discipline as the baked speed_figure / collateral channels. the feature joins on
(date,venue,race_no,runner); the population σ_pop is computed over the full panel but is a dispersion
constant (the shrink target), not a per-horse outcome — identical to how `par` uses the full panel.
population component carries no per-fold future leakage into the per-horse std (which is strictly
prior). the gate below trains the energetics population on each walk-forward fold's train window only.

the gate (paired fixed-seed, pythonhashseed=0, full scale, both venues; %market | ece):

  st (1952 races, 24433 runners)            base 65.25% | 0.0066
    figvar_gain=0.10                              65.42% | 0.0064   (δ% +0.17, δece −0.0002)  pass
    figvar_gain=0.15                              65.44% | 0.0058   (δ% +0.19, δece −0.0008)  pass *best*
    figvar_gain=0.20                              65.42% | 0.0058   (δ% +0.17, δece −0.0008)  pass
    figvar_gain=0.25                              65.38% | 0.0058   (δ% +0.13, δece −0.0008)  pass
    figvar_gain=0.30                              65.28% | 0.0059   (δ% +0.03, δece −0.0007)  pass
    figvar_gain=0.40                              65.04% | 0.0052   (δ% −0.21, δece −0.0014)  %market down
    figvar_gain=1.00                              61.04% | 0.0061   (δ% −4.21)                overshoot
    figvar_gain=−0.40                             62.08% | 0.0065   (δ% −3.17)                wrong sign craters

  hv (1296 races, 14823 runners)            base 59.69% | 0.0046
    figvar_gain=0.05                              59.99% | 0.0050   (δ% +0.30, δece +0.0004)  ece worse
    figvar_gain=0.10                              60.23% | 0.0049   (δ% +0.54, δece +0.0003)  ece worse
    figvar_gain=0.15                              60.43% | 0.0049   (δ% +0.74, δece +0.0003)  ece worse
    figvar_gain=0.20                              60.48% | 0.0056   (δ% +0.79, δece +0.0009)  ece worse
    figvar_gain=0.40                              60.20% | 0.0055   (δ% +0.51, δece +0.0009)  ece worse
    figvar_gain=−0.40                             54.03% | 0.0043   (δ% −5.66)                wrong sign craters

evt field-size breakout (st, split at field_size 12; band by scoring, gain=0.15; %market | ece):
    big  (≥12, ~20440 runners)   base 66.06% | 0.0064   cand 66.14% | 0.0064   (δ% +0.09, δece ~0)
    small(<12,  ~3747 runners)   base 62.00% | 0.0183   cand 62.37% | 0.0175   (δ% +0.36, δece −0.0008)
  the st gain is broad-based, not confined to big fields. naively the evt order-statistic argument
  (§3e) predicts d-heterogeneity pays most in big fields; here the %market lift is actually a touch
  larger in st small fields, though they start from a much worse-calibrated base (ece 0.0183 vs 0.0064
  — small st fields are the under-served calibration cell), so the term is partly fixing that. big
  fields still improve on both metrics. reading: the per-horse-d redistribution helps st broadly, with
  the cleanest calibration repair in the poorly-calibrated small-st cell — consistent with "variance
  is load-bearing in the order statistic" without being a pure big-field effect. (caveat: the band is
  by scoring only; the fit trains on full fields. a field-size interaction of the gain is untested.)

interpretation.
- the mechanism is real and the sign is unambiguous at both venues: positive gain (erratic horses get
  more d_i) helps %market; negative gain craters both. the market does not already fully price
  figure-consistency into the win prob — there is a recoverable per-horse variance signal.
- st: a clean, stable interior optimum — gains 0.10–0.30 all pass the dual gate (both %market and ece
  improve), a plateau peaking ≈0.15 (+0.19% %market, ece −0.0008). small in %market but a real, paired,
  full-scale dual-metric improvement on a broad plateau — the signature of a genuine lever, not noise.
- hv: fails the dual gate at every positive gain. %market wants the term (up to +0.8%) but ece
  degrades monotonically (+0.0003 to +0.0009) even at gain=0.05. hv's smaller fields + tighter handicap
  blanket finishes mean the population already sits at a lower residual spread (queue #29: hv cv below
  st at every shared distance), so redistributing variance per-horse over-disperses hv and breaks its
  (already tighter, ece 0.0046) calibration. this is the same st-converts / hv-null venue split the evt
  field-size argument predicts for variance levers (cf. draw_var_gain, st-only), here sharpened to
  "hv actively mis-calibrates."

recommendation.
- st: **bake-candidate** `figvar_gain_by_venue["st"] = 0.15` (range 0.10–0.20 equivalent; passes the
  paired full-scale dual gate). defer to the orchestrator (serializes all bakes). note it stacks on top
  of the live st base (65.25%) which already carries draw_var_gain=0.5 — the two d-knobs (geometry/draw
  and own-figure-spread) co-exist and the figure-spread term still adds, so they are not redundant.
- hv: **don't-bake.** keep `figvar_gain_by_venue["hv"] = 0.0`. the dual gate fails on ece at all gains.
- production stays no-op as shipped (both venues 0.0); nothing in constants.py baked-defaults changed.

what to try next if a fuller variance lever is wanted.
1. couple to the figure-residual-after-class/rating (regress sf on rtg-band, take the residual std) so
   the dispersion is not confounded with a horse simply moving up/down in class — the §spec's suggested
   refinement; may sharpen the st gain and possibly rescue an hv variant.
2. field-size interaction of the gain (figvar_gain × field_size) rather than the by-scoring band — to
   test the evt prediction properly inside the fit, and possibly let hv's small fields opt out.
3. awt-specific d_i: queue #29 found awt carries a real distance-independent variance floor (σ0≈0.46s);
   per-horse d_i may pay most on awt (big fields + intrinsic extra diffusion) — untested here (the
   per-venue st/hv split folds awt into st's surface branch via awt_diff_mult, but a dedicated awt gain
   is unexplored).

title: "Queue #31: START-phase gate-break trait — drift channel DON'T-BAKE (priced/collinear); D channel ST-sprint BOTH↑ but sub-noise, HV ECE-worse"
author: modelling
summary: DRAFT — orchestrator serializes any bake + MODEL_STATE update. Production left a NO-OP (all GATE_BREAK_* gains default 0.0). Recommendation: DON'T-BAKE both channels as-is. ## HYPOTHESIS (THEORY §3e —…
text:
"queue #31: start-phase gate-break trait — drift channel don't-bake (priced/collinear); d channel st-sprint both↑ but sub-noise, hv ece-worse" theory phase-structure queue-31 gate-break start-phase draw-residual diffusion d-knob collinearity dont-bake draft draft — orchestrator serializes any bake + model_state update. production left a no-op
(all gate_break_* gains default 0.0). recommendation: don't-bake both channels as-is.

## hypothesis (theory §3e — the start phase as a distinct regime)
the homogeneous wald law treats the trip as one drift-diffusion gun-to-wire. the start is a
distinct phase: a horse that breaks well and secures early position gains a real, repeatable
edge — it should reach v_c sooner (shorter effective l / higher early drift) and a clean break
is low-variance while a troubled break injects variance d. this should matter most where the
start is a bigger fraction of l (sprints) and where traffic at the break is worst (big fields).
the trait must be the horse's break skill, not a draw restatement — so early position
residualised against draw.

## construction (leak-free) — features.gate_break_table(run_policy, wpq)
per run: gate_break_run = early_pos_norm − e[early_pos_norm | draw_norm], draw_norm =
(draw−1)/(field_size−1), and e[·|draw_norm] = a + b·draw_norm a single population affine fit
over the full panel. then the strictly-prior expanding mean per horse (sorted by date) =
gate_break, with prior-run count gate_break_n for eb shrinkage. in fit.py the trait is
shrunk n/(n+3) toward 0 (= field-average break) and within-race centred.

leak-free proof: (1) per-horse trait is the expanding mean of strictly prior runs only (shift
discipline, like form/early_pos/trajectory tables). (2) the draw→position affine is a population
constant over a random, pre-race-public boundary condition (draw) — not the horse's outcome —
same leak status as the trial `par` and the trajectory within-race z-score. (3) mechanical
check: `assert_no_lookahead` on the full gate-break fit path (both channels active) returns max
prediction drift = 0.0 (predictions invariant to corrupting test outcomes). (4) population eb
fit is train-only per walk-forward fold (backtest_st loader, unchanged discipline).

## the collinearity finding (the key result, §3e-predicted)
draw explains almost none of hkjc rank-normalised early position: corr(early_pos_norm,
draw_norm) = 0.06; the per-band draw→early-pos slope is ~+0.03–0.08 (and weakly positive — wide
horses sit fractionally more forward, a style/selection artifact, not a break penalty). the bend
ground-loss, not the break, is the dominant draw mechanism in this data. consequence:
residualising against draw removes essentially nothing, so gate_break ≈ centred early_pos
(corr(gate_break_run, early_pos_norm) = 0.998). the break trait is therefore highly collinear
with the existing positional-fade `early_pos` term and with the form channel — it can only earn
its keep through a different mechanism/channel (early-phase drift or d), not as new ability info.

## the paired gate (pythonhashseed=0, full-scale walk-forward, shared per-race mc seeds)
channel (a) — effective-l / drift bonus (good break ⇒ shorter l, scaled by start_frac=min(1,
1200/l) so it bites in sprints):

  st full    base 65.25% | ece 0.0066 →  gain 0.05/0.1/0.2/0.4 = 64.96/64.14/61.32/51.03%
             (δ% −0.29/−1.11/−3.93/−14.22), ece all worse. negative gains also cost %market
             (−0.15/−0.84/−3.65) though they improve ece (0.0066→0.0050 at −0.1).
  st sprint  base 69.12% → all gains lower %market (−0.12…−16.24). st route same.
  hv full    base 59.69% → gain 0.05/0.1 = 58.58/56.75% (δ −1.11/−2.94). decisively negative.
  ⇒ drift channel don't-bake on both venues, both signs (monotone away from base in %market).

channel (b) — diffusion d modulation (good break ⇒ lower d / more predictable):

  st full    base 65.25% | ece 0.0066 →  gain 0.1/0.25/0.5 = 65.31/65.38/65.34% | 0.0064/0.0062/
             0.0058  (δ% +0.06/+0.13/+0.09, δece −0.0001/−0.0004/−0.0008) — both↑ at every gain.
  st sprint  base 69.12% | 0.0087 →  gain 0.5 = 69.34% | 0.0086  (δ% +0.22, δece −0.00004) both↑.
  st route   base 61.73% | 0.0080 →  +0.1–0.13% %market but ece worsens (+0.0004) — fails both.
  hv full    base 59.69% | 0.0046 →  gain 0.25/0.5 = 60.01/60.08% | 0.0053/0.0052  (δ% +0.32/+0.39,
             δece +0.0007/+0.0006) — %market up but ece worse ⇒ fails the both gate. negative gain
             (−0.25) improves ece (−0.0007) but costs %market (−0.31).
  ⇒ d channel: st passes both gates (sprint-led, +0.13% full / +0.22% sprint, ece flat-to-better);
    hv fails (ece worsens). the split is exactly the §3e/evt field-size prediction (the d-knob
    pays in big-field st, null/wrong at small-field hv — same signature as the baked draw_var_gain
    st-only split, and consistent with journal 0029: hv has the lowest cv already).

## interpretation
- §3e gets a partial theory-confirms-data: the start-phase signal lives on the variance knob
  (clean break = lower d), not the drift — putting it on drift double-counts the already-priced
  forward-position/form channel and craters %market. and it pays where §3e says (st sprints /
  big fields), null at hv. the drift no-op + d-sprint-positive pattern is the §3e
  "mean→drift, temperament→d" decomposition resolving in favour of the d half.
- but the st d gain is sub-noise: +0.13% full / +0.22% sprint is well inside the ±0.3–0.5pp mc
  band the methodology caveat names (and quick_eval over-states ~4×; this is the full-scale gate,
  so it is not inflated — it is simply tiny). ece moves are 1e-4. not a confident bake.

## recommendation: don't-bake (both channels), keep the axis open.
- drift channel: reject this structure (priced/collinear — the break adds nothing as new drift).
- d channel: st-only is directionally right and §3e-consistent but the magnitude is sub-noise;
  not worth a bake on its own. hv explicitly fails (ece). park as "real mechanism, marginal
  leverage on win" pending a sharper trait.

## what to try next (if the axis is revisited)
1. the trait is a near-restatement of early_pos because draw barely moves hkjc early position.
   a sharper break signal needs the actual gate-to-first-call position change, not the settled
   early level — i.e. the §3e "first-call rank minus draw" using the raw runningposition call
   points (results_rich.runningposition) rather than run_policy's already-settled early_pos_norm.
   that would decouple it from the positional-fade term.
2. break×field-size interaction on the d channel only, st big fields (the evt corollary): the
   gate_break_fs_gain hook exists but was left at 0.0 here — sweep it on st sprints with large n.
3. break → d only on awt (journal 0029: awt carries a real distance-independent variance floor =
   the "bad-break costs the same seconds at any l" mechanism §3e names) — the d channel's natural
   home if any.
4. interaction with the positional-fade w′ term (posfade_w_gain): the break is the early control
   decision whose cost is paid late (the §3e intertemporal coupling) — a break×pos_fade cell, not
   a standalone gate trait.

## artifacts (production untouched — all gains default 0.0)
- features.gate_break_table — leak-free draw-residualised break trait + eb count.
- fit.fit_predict_traffic gate_break_gain (drift, start_frac×field-size scaled) +
  gate_break_d_gain (diffusion) + gate_break_fs_gain — all no-op at 0.0.
- constants gate_break_gain[_by_venue]/fs_gain/d_gain/lref — all 0.0.
- studies/gate_break_probe.py — paired fixed-seed probe, st distance-band breakout.

title: "Queue #29 (T3+T4): peak-gap mean-reversion ASYMMETRY (HV passes thin, ST flat) + unified allometric b (split is load-bearing — DON'T unify)"
author: modelling
summary: Two independent sub-parts, gated separately. Both paired fixed-seed (PYTHONHASHSEED=0), full scale, both venues, %market | ECE. Base for each gate is the CURRENT production path (not zero). ==========…
text:
"queue #29 (t3+t4): peak-gap mean-reversion asymmetry (hv passes thin, st flat) + unified allometric b (split is load-bearing — don't unify)" peakgap mean-reversion asymmetry career-landmark process-feature allometric mass allometric-b parsimony venue-split conversion-test queue-29 ece draft two independent sub-parts, gated separately. both paired fixed-seed (pythonhashseed=0), full scale,
both venues, %market | ece. base for each gate is the current production path (not zero).

=============================================================================================
## t3 — peak-gap as career mean-reversion (not a static deficit)

hypothesis (theory §3d career-phase / mean-reversion). the baked peakgap_gain enters the own-peak
rating deficit (rtg − own prior peak, ≤0) as a flat linear coupling — a static handicap. the refinement:
a deficit is a mean-reversion signal. a horse far below its career peak is often an improving/returning
horse the market under-rates (reversion up toward peak); a horse at a fresh peak may be over-bet
(regression down). so the coupling may be asymmetric around the career landmark, or the rating's recent
trend/velocity (recovering vs declining) may carry the signal instead of the raw gap level. per the
model_state refuted list, raw rating velocity/accel was refuted as generic velocity (restates form);
only the peak landmark converts — so the live hypothesis is the asymmetry structure around the landmark,
not generic velocity.

construction (additive, leak-free, default no-op).
- two new knobs on `fit.fit_predict_traffic`, both stacking on top of the live static peakgap term:
  - `rtg_peakgap_asym_gain` (a) — an extra coupling on the below-peak (raw ≤0) portion only,
    within-race centred: `v_c += gain·(min(rtg_peakgap,0) − field_mean)`. a non-zero gain ⇒ the
    below-peak slope differs from the at-peak (flat) slope = the asymmetry around the landmark.
  - `rtg_peakgap_vel_gain` (b) — the rating velocity toward/away from peak (`rtg_vel` = δrtg/k),
    within-race centred, on v_c (the reversion trend rather than the gap level).
- constants `peakgap_asym_gain[_by_venue]`, `peakgap_vel_gain[_by_venue]`, default 0.0 ⇒ production
  untouched. both columns (`rtg_peakgap`, `rtg_vel`) are the existing strictly-prior as-of feature
  (`features.rating_trajectory_table` → `attach_rating_trajectory`, backward join
  `allow_exact_matches=false`, same one already baked for the static term). the new knobs only
  re-weight that leak-free column (min/centre/velocity) — no new data path, no new join. eb population
  stays train-only per fold. determinism confirmed (pythonhashseed=0 reproduces to the digit).

the gate (paired fixed-seed, full scale; base = current static peakgap; %market | ece):

  st (1952 races, 24433 runners; 24.2% below-peak)   base 65.25% | 0.0066
    (a) asym=-0.03                                         64.90% | 0.0055   (δ% -0.35, δece -0.0011)
    (a) asym=-0.02                                         65.19% | 0.0060   (δ% -0.06, δece -0.0006)
    (a) asym=-0.01                                         65.30% | 0.0063   (δ% +0.05, δece -0.0003)  pass (marginal)
    (a) asym=+0.01                                         65.01% | 0.0065   (δ% -0.24, δece -0.0001)
    (a) asym=+0.02                                         64.64% | 0.0063   (δ% -0.61, δece -0.0003)
    (b) vel=-0.02                                          65.31% | 0.0070   (δ% +0.06, δece +0.0004)  ece worse
    (b) vel=-0.01                                          65.28% | 0.0069   (δ% +0.03, δece +0.0003)  ece worse
    (b) vel=+0.01/+0.02                                    ~65.2  | ~0.0066   (δ% ≤0)
  → st: flat. asymmetry buys at most +0.05% (noise); velocity is null/ece-worse. clean confirmation
    that the st static term is already sufficient — exactly what the refuted-list note predicts.

  hv (1296 races, 14823 runners; 27.1% below-peak)   base 59.69% | 0.0046
    (a) asym=-0.05                                         59.72% | 0.0055   (δ% +0.03, δece +0.0009)  ece worse
    (a) asym=-0.04                                         60.33% | 0.0052   (δ% +0.64, δece +0.0006)  ece worse
    (a) asym=-0.035                                        60.52% | 0.0045   (δ% +0.84, δece -0.0002)  pass
    (a) asym=-0.03                                         60.63% | 0.0039   (δ% +0.94, δece -0.0007)  pass (best ece)
    (a) asym=-0.025                                        60.64% | 0.0047   (δ% +0.95, δece +0.0000)  pass (best %)
    (a) asym=-0.02                                         60.61% | 0.0056   (δ% +0.92, δece +0.0010)  ece worse
    (a) asym=-0.01                                         60.28% | 0.0047   (δ% +0.59, δece +0.0001)  ece worse
    (a) asym=+0.01                                         58.93% | 0.0049   (δ% -0.76, δece +0.0002)  ece worse
    (b) vel=-0.02                                          60.06% | 0.0045   (δ% +0.37, δece -0.0001)  pass (weaker)
    (b) vel=-0.01                                          59.87% | 0.0045   (δ% +0.18, δece -0.0001)  pass (weaker)
    (b) vel=+0.01/+0.02                                    <base  | worse                              wrong sign

  → hv: a real but thin signal. steeper below-peak coupling (asym<0 = more reversion-up credit) lifts
    %market ~+0.9% with ece neutral-to-better at asym∈[-0.035,-0.025]. sign is right and consistent
    (negative asym = credit the below-peak horse as reverting up). but the ece is jumpy across the grid
    (−0.0007 at −0.03, but +0.0010 at −0.02 and +0.0009 at −0.05), i.e. the dual-gate pass sits on a
    narrow ece knife-edge near the ±0.0003–0.0005 sampling floor.

the decisive control — is it asymmetry, or just "hv's static gain is under-tuned?"
rtg_peakgap is ≤0, so a steeper below-peak slope is nearly a steeper overall slope (73% of hv runners
are at-peak=0 and carry no gap signal). so i swept the symmetric plain `peakgap_gain` at hv:
    peakgap_gain=-0.025 (baked)   59.7% | 0.0046
    peakgap_gain=-0.035           60.3% | (—)
    peakgap_gain=-0.045           60.6% | 0.0056   ← same +0.9% %market as the asym term…
    peakgap_gain=-0.055           60.6% | (—)
  a symmetric larger hv gain reaches the same +0.9% %market — but at ece 0.0056 (+0.0010, fails the
  dual gate). the asymmetry term reaches the same %market at ece 0.0039 (−0.0007, passes). so the
  asymmetry is not a different %market story — the *market lift is just "hv peakgap is under-coupled"* —
  but the asymmetric structure achieves that lift with materially better calibration than steepening
  everything symmetrically. reading: hv genuinely wants more below-peak (reversion-up) coupling, and
  loading it asymmetrically (not also steepening the at-peak/regression-down side) is what keeps the
  calibration clean. that is a (weak) vindication of the mean-reversion structure over the static term
  at hv — but it is thin and ece-fragile.

recommendation (t3).
- st: **don't-bake.** flat for both asymmetry and velocity — the static term is sufficient (confirms
  the refuted-list note: only the landmark converts; no asymmetry/velocity structure to add at st).
- hv: **don't-bake (lean), candidate-if-pushed.** `peakgap_asym_gain_by_venue["hv"] = -0.03` passes the
  paired dual gate (+0.94% %market, ece −0.0007) and beats a symmetric retune on calibration — a real
  but marginal, ece-knife-edge result. i would not bake it on the strength of one ece-jumpy grid: the
  +0.9% is mostly "hv static peakgap is under-tuned" and the asymmetry's only clean advantage is the
  ece, which is grid-fragile. defer to the orchestrator; if anything, the cleaner first move is to
  re-examine the hv static peakgap_gain tune (it may simply want to be slightly larger with an ece
  guard), and only adopt the asymmetric form if it survives a finer/independent-seed ece check.
- production stays no-op (both knobs 0.0 at both venues); constants baked-defaults unchanged.

what to try next (t3).
1. decompose at-peak vs below-peak as two independent gains (full two-slope fit) to measure the
   regression-down (at/near-peak, over-bet) side directly — here it's folded into the static term;
   the asym knob only touches the below-peak side.
2. residualise rtg_peakgap against recency-form before coupling, to be sure the hv below-peak lift is
   the landmark and not form leaking back in (the refuted-list worry).
3. an independent-seed ece replication of hv asym=-0.03 before any bake — the dual-gate pass is on a
   ±0.0005 ece margin.

=============================================================================================
## t4 — unify the allometric exponent b across venues

hypothesis (theory §3d allometric mass + constants note "venue-invariant physiology, st-only by
leverage"). `allometric_b_by_venue={st:1.1, hv:1.0}` couples declared mass to v_c via v_c ∝ m^(b−1).
the note claims the physiological exponent b is one number and the venue split is an artifact of where
mass-leverage bites (hv's other channels already price mass), not real physiology. so a single unified
b should hold both venues — a parsimony win (one fewer free constant). test candidate unified b ∈ {1.0,
1.05, 1.1} applied to both venues vs the {st:1.1, hv:1.0} baseline.

construction. no new code — `fit.fit_predict_traffic(allometric_b=)` already overrides the per-venue
dict when not none (mass is leak-free: declared weight is published pre-race; field-relative to the
geometric-mean mass on the wald path). `studies/allometric_b_probe.py` runs the paired gate per venue:
base = `allometric_b=none` (the per-venue split), candidate = a single b for both.

the gate (paired fixed-seed, full scale; %market | ece):

  st (baked b=1.1)    base (split) 65.25% | 0.0066
    unified b=1.0                  64.75% | 0.0071   (δ% -0.50, δece +0.0005)  worse both
    unified b=1.05                 65.13% | 0.0073   (δ% -0.12, δece +0.0007)  worse both
    unified b=1.1                  65.25% | 0.0066   (== base; b=1.1 is st's value)

  hv (baked b=1.0)    base (split) 59.69% | 0.0046
    unified b=1.0                  59.69% | 0.0046   (== base; b=1.0 is hv's value)
    unified b=1.05                 59.97% | 0.0047   (δ% +0.28, δece +0.0000)  %market up, ece ~flat
    unified b=1.1                  60.02% | 0.0055   (δ% +0.33, δece +0.0009)  %market up but ece worse

the verdict — the split is load-bearing; do not unify.
- to unify at a single b you must pick one value for both venues:
  - b=1.0 unified → st loses −0.50% %market (ece +0.0005). fails at st.
  - b=1.1 unified → hv gains +0.33% %market but ece worsens +0.0009. fails the dual gate at hv.
  - b=1.05 unified → st −0.12%/ece worse and hv ece essentially flat; a compromise that improves
    neither venue on the dual gate (st worse both metrics).
- there is no single b that holds both venues on the dual %market+ece gate. b=1.1 helps hv's %market
  but breaks hv's (tighter, 0.0046) calibration; b=1.0 protects hv's calibration but costs st. the
  venue split is doing real work.

interesting nuance: hv's %market actually wants more mass (b=1.1: +0.33%), echoing the st direction —
consistent with the "venue-invariant physiology" idea at the level of the drift. what kills unification
is hv calibration: pushing hv mass to b=1.1 over-disperses the win prob (ece +0.0009), the same
"variance lever over-disperses the already-tighter hv field" failure mode seen for the per-horse-d
knobs (queue #28 figvar, draw_var_gain). so the constants-note story is half right: the *drift*
physiology may indeed be venue-invariant (hv's mean wants b>1 too), but the venue split is not a pure
leverage artifact you can drop — it is the calibration guard that keeps hv from over-dispersing. the b
exponent is doing double duty (drift physiology + an implicit hv dispersion control), and the two pull
apart at hv.

recommendation (t4).
- **don't-bake a unified b. keep `allometric_b_by_venue={st:1.1, hv:1.0}`.** the split is load-bearing:
  no single b passes the dual gate at both venues. documented above with the gate numbers.
- parsimony is not free here — unifying costs ≥−0.5% at st (b=1.0) or +0.0009 ece at hv (b=1.1).
- what to try next if the parsimony win is still wanted: absorb hv's mass-leverage shortfall elsewhere
  (field-size or distance leverage, per the note's hypothesis) and re-test a unified b=1.1 — i.e. give
  hv a mass×field-size or mass×distance term so the venue difference is explained by leverage, then see
  if b can unify without the hv ece break. that is the real test of "venue-invariant physiology, split
  is leverage" and is the only path to the parsimony win; the flat-unify tested here rejects it.

=============================================================================================
leak-free caveats (both sub-parts). all features are the existing strictly-prior as-of columns
(`rtg_peakgap`/`rtg_vel` via backward `allow_exact_matches=false`; declared mass is a pre-race public
boundary condition). the new knobs only re-weight those columns — no new join, no new data path. the
eb energetics population is fit on each walk-forward fold's train window only (unchanged). all gates are
paired fixed-seed (pythonhashseed=0, shared per-race mc seeds), full scale, both venues; verified
deterministic on re-run. no bakes performed — both new knobs default 0.0 (production untouched); the
orchestrator serializes any bake.

title: "Queue #32: finishing-sectional v_c fusion channel — DON'T BAKE (collinear with whole-race v_c; the closing read IS the existing v_c)"
author: modelling
summary: HYPOTHESIS (THEORY §3e phase structure). The CLOSING phase (final ≈400 m) is the least tactically-contaminated read of raw aerobic capacity — every horse maximally extended, W′ emptying, nobody holdin…
text:
"queue #32: finishing-sectional v_c fusion channel — don't bake (collinear with whole-race v_c; the closing read is the existing v_c)" queue-32 finishing-sectional phase-structure theory-3e fusion precision-fusion v_c collinear dont-bake closing-phase conversion-test hypothesis (theory §3e phase structure). the closing phase (final ≈400 m) is the least
tactically-contaminated read of raw aerobic capacity — every horse maximally extended, w′ emptying,
nobody holding back — so the finishing-sectional velocity should be the highest-precision single read
of v_c, sharper than the trip-average. fold a horse's strictly-prior finishing-sectional v_c reads
into the eb v_c posterior at their own precision π_fin=ρ_fin·π_race, the temporal analogue of the
baked trial/gallop fusion (give each phase its own precision).

construction (leak-free). `features.finishing_sectional_vc_table(trajectory, mode, going)` on
`trajectory_dataset_full` (per-section velocity, 39,256 runs, full 4-yr, st 82.9% / hv 90.4% runner
coverage). per run: closing-section velocity = velocity at `section == n_sections` (the final 400 m).
two modes: `raw` = the closing velocity itself; `kick` = the pace-adjusted residual
`v_close − v_mean_run` (the closing kick net of the run's own average). par-normalise on
(going, distance) — a panel-level condition constant, not the horse's outcome ⇒ leak-free — re-centre
onto the race-v_c mean (the closing velocity mean 16.90 ≈ race v_c mean 16.82, so it lands on the race
scale by construction). then the strictly-prior expanding mean per horse (cum-sum shifted by one) +
prior count `finsec_m`. fused in `fit.fit_predict_traffic` as a 4th channel exactly like gallops: a
train-only affine map (`fit_trial_vc_map`, signal=finsec_vc) puts the race-scale signal on the v_c
residual scale; `finsec_m` precision mass enters the shared posterior denominator with trials+gallops;
weight clamped ≤1. `finsec_pi_ratio` defaults 0.0 — production untouched (no-op).

leak-free proof. (i) finsec_vc is null exactly where finsec_m==0 (no prior closing read) — the
shift-by-one expanding mean. (ii) the study attaches it with a strict backward as-of join
(`allow_exact_matches=false`), so a race never sees its own or any later closing sectional. (iii) par
is a contemporaneous condition constant. (iv) decisive: ρ_fin=0 reproduces the base bit-for-bit
(st 65.25%/0.0066, δ +0.00%) under the paired fixed-seed — the channel is a clean no-op when off, so
the on-deltas are pure mechanism on shared per-race mc seeds.

the paired gate (pythonhashseed=0, full-scale, 5-fold walk-forward, % of market | ece):

  st (1,952 races):  base 65.25% | 0.0066
    raw  ρ=0.5 / 1 / 2:  65.42 / 65.46 / 65.30   ece +0.0003 / +0.0004 / +0.0008   (ece worse — fail)
    kick ρ=0.5 / 1 / 2:  65.47 / 65.49 / 65.31   ece −0.0001 / +0.0001 / +0.0007
       → only kick ρ=0.5 nominally passes both (+0.22pp, ece −0.0001) — inside mc noise.
  hv (1,296 races):  base 59.69% | 0.0046
    raw  ρ=0.5 / 1 / 2:  59.64 / 59.64 / 59.64   ece −0.0004 (flat-to-negative on %market — fail)
    kick ρ=0.5 / 1 / 2:  59.64 / 59.64 / 59.64   ece −0.0003 (flat-to-negative on %market — fail)

verdict: **don't bake.** leave finsec_pi_ratio = 0.0 at both venues (production no-op, already so).
- hv is dead-flat (−0.05pp %market both modes) — the channel adds nothing.
- st's best cell (kick ρ=0.5: +0.22pp, ece −0.0001) is a single non-robust gate-pass sitting inside
  the ±0.3–0.5pp mc-noise band the methodology warns of; the adjacent ρ=1.0 already flips ece positive,
  and `raw` worsens ece at every ρ. not a real, robust both-margin improvement on both venues.

why (the collinearity, with evidence — a flat result is the valuable finding here). the whole-race v_c
already in the posterior is essentially the closing read: `energetics.estimate_run_energetics` defines
`v_c = min` of the final two sections, so per-run corr(closing-section velocity, race v_c) = **0.96**.
the "finishing sectional as a high-precision v_c channel" is therefore not a new axis — it is the
channel the model already shrinks into v_c. folding it back in is near-redundant, hence the flat gate.
the one genuinely independent sub-axis is the pace-adjusted closing kick (`v_close − v_mean_run`), which
is ~orthogonal to whole-race average velocity (corr 0.09); that is why `kick` is the only mode showing
any st flicker — but the flicker is sub-noise. a dead term, not a dead axis.

what to try next (the axis stays open; this rejects the structure, not the phase mechanism):
1. closing-kick residual on the w′ knob, not v_c. the clean closing kick is the late anaerobic
   reserve emptying (theory §3d/§3e), the same phenomenon as the baked fade_w_gain (fade on w′). the
   finishing kick likely belongs on w′ (distance-aware via w′/l), where it is not collinear with the
   v_c the closing split already feeds — and where the existing fade term shows it converts. the raw
   v_c channel here double-counts v_c; the residual-on-w′ is the non-redundant home.
2. phase-specific precision / a true 3-phase wald (start/cruise/closing drifts) rather than one channel
   bolted on a homogeneous law — the §3e program proper. the single-channel fusion can't express that
   the closing read should displace (not supplement) the cruise-contaminated v_c.
3. pace-context-adjusted closing velocity: normalise the closing split by the pace it was run into
   (the field's mid-race tempo), isolating the horse's closing ability from the race shape — a sharper
   read than the own-run mean used in `kick`.

implementation note (caught a real bug — relevant to the gallop channel). the first gate run was
catastrophic (st 65→−187%) because the per-horse fusion term applied the affine map to the raw
race-scale finsec_vc (~16.85) instead of the rating-band residual — `fit_trial_vc_map` residualises x
internally (`x = x − fixed`) for non-`trial_fig` signals, so the prediction must subtract the same
per-horse fixed effect; passing raw injected a spurious ≈+5 m/s v_c bump. fixed:
`fmap_a + fmap_b·(finsec_vc − pop.v_c.fixed(band, rtg))`, term clamped ≤1 (finsec_m is a large per-horse
