count, mean ~10, so the unclamped m_f=1-normalised weight over-weights multi-read horses). ⚠️ the
gallop channel (`gallop_term = … (gmap_a + gmap_b·gvc[i])`, fit.py) has the identical raw-signal bug,
latent only because gallop_pi_ratio=0 everywhere (never exercised). it will misfire the same +5 m/s way
if ever switched on — flagged for whoever takes up the gallop fusion (queue #30) to apply the same
`(gvc − fixed)` correction before baking.

production untouched (finsec_pi_ratio 0.0 both venues, no constants baked). model_state not updated
(orchestrator serializes).

title: "Finishing-time LAW: DIFFUSIVE-SUFFICIENT — no material jump/incident tail; AWT #33 floor is larger D, not jump mass"
author: modelling
summary: DESCRIPTIVE population study (NOT a predictive feature → no as-of/leak-free constraint; read-only on production — touched no fit.py/constants.py/features.py). Question (THEORY §2.8, §3e; follow-up to …
text:
"finishing-time law: diffusive-sufficient — no material jump/incident tail; awt #33 floor is larger d, not jump mass" theory diffusion inverse-gaussian wald finishing-time tail jump incident birnbaum-saunders awt d-floor queue-33-followup stochasticity theory-2.8 theory-3e descriptive descriptive population study (not a predictive feature → no as-of/leak-free constraint; read-only on
production — touched no fit.py/constants.py/features.py). question (theory §2.8, §3e; follow-up to #33
/0029): is the stochastic part of finishing time t **diffusive** (inverse-gaussian first-passage, thin
scaling tail) or does it carry a material **jump/incident** component (heavy asymmetric upper tail from
troubled trips; a distance-independent variance floor)? panel: results_rich.parquet, 36,853 runners on
good/good-to-firm, binned into 23 tight (surface×venue×distance×going) bands with n≥250. per band: par =
within-band mean t; residual ε = t−par; all families fit by mle to y = ε−min(ε)+δ with loc fixed at 0
(so the comparison is shape/tail only, not location). study + 4 plots: studies/finishing_time_law.py.

=== verdict: diffusive-sufficient. no material jump/incident tail. ===
the stochastic finishing-residual is well-described by a single diffusive-family law. the empirical upper
tail is not materially heavier than a body-anchored diffusion predicts; the awt variance floor of #33 is
**uniformly larger d**, not a jump component. an ig+jump (or birnbaum–saunders) production law is not
warranted by a tail mis-fit.

=== aic/bic: the production law (ig) is the worst diffusive fit; gamma wins; jump does not win. ===
per-band aic (δaic vs best). family of best aic across 23 bands: **gamma 21, lognormal 1, ig+jump 1.**
  • inverse-gaussian (the sim=wald law) is the worst or near-worst single family in every band — δaic
    vs gamma of +100…+900. the ig shape is a mediocre description of the residual body; gamma/lognormal
    fit the centre far better (lognorm typically 2nd).
  • the explicit 2-component **ig-core + shifted-exponential "trouble"** mixture does not win on aic
    (loses to gamma in 22/23) — but only because its core is ig, which is the handicap above, not
    because the data lacks a tail it could fill. aic here measures the core, not the incident tail —
    exactly the trap the task warned of, so the verdict is weighted on tail calibration, below.
note this is a refinement of the production picture: the wald law's moments are vindicated (#33: cv∝1/√l,
var∝l), but its distributional shape is closer to gamma/lognormal than to strict ig. both are diffusive,
positively-skewed, single-component laws — the win order-statistic is moment- and tail-driven, so this is
not a production defect, just the true shape of the noise.

=== tail calibration (the verdict weight): the diffusive tail is ≈calibrated; no jump room. ===
upper-tail coverage = empirical exceedance / nominal at the fitted q-quantile (1.0 = calibrated;
>1 = empirical tail heavier than model = under-cover; <1 = over-cover). median across the 23 bands:
  family                         p95 ratio   p99 ratio
  bulkig (ig fit to lower 92%)      0.85        1.07     ← the proper diffusive null
  gamma (best body fit)             0.73        1.05
  invgauss (full-sample 3-param)    0.35        0.45     ← over-covers: 3-param ig inflates its
                                                            own tail to absorb the body misfit
  ig+jump (bulk core + add-on)      0.64        1.21     ← over-covers; the jump knob pins at its
                                                            bound and over-fattens, not a clean tail
key read: once ig is anchored to the body (bulkig = ig on the lower 92%), its own intrinsic positive
skew produces ≈ the right amount of upper-tail mass — median p99 coverage 1.07, i.e. only ~7% under at
the 99th pctile, not the explosive under-coverage a genuine jump world requires. gamma is the same (1.05).
the unconstrained ig+jump (pi capped 0.30, tau floored 1.0s) hits both bounds in ~17/23 bands and then
over-covers (p99 1.21, several bands 2.5–7.6×) — the optimizer is using the "trouble" mass to widen the
whole upper half, not to add a discrete rare spike. a real incident world would let pi settle at a small
interior value with a clean tail-coverage repair; instead the bound binds against a tail that is already
≈full → the data does not want a separable jump component. upper-tail qq (ft_uppertail_qq.png) confirms:
full-sample ig and birnbaum–saunders points sit on the diagonal through the 80–99th pctiles in every band,
except 1–2 isolated freak outliers per band (a 73 s / 32 s run, ~1 in 4,000 — a genuine pulled-up/eased
horse) that are real incidents but far too rare to move the law. densities (finishing_time_densities.png)
show a smooth unimodal right-skewed body with no secondary mode or shoulder on the right — no jump bump.

=== asymmetry: positive, but only ig-grade — consistent with diffusive skew, not excess incidents. ===
robust-standardized ε: skew>0 in all 23 bands; upper/lower tail ratio (z99/|z01|) = 1.2…2.5 (median ~1.8);
frac >3·mad ≈ 1.3–3.1% vs frac <3·mad ≈ 0%. the asymmetry is real (troubled trips only slow, never speed,
so the residual is one-sidedly right-heavy) but its magnitude is exactly what a body-anchored ig/gamma
already emits (their p99 coverage ≈1.0). a few bands show inflated raw skew (st-1200 30.8, hv-1800-gtf
12.0) driven entirely by the lone freak outliers above, not a systematic tail. so the asymmetry is the
diffusion's own skew plus a negligible-probability true-incident sprinkle — not a material jump mass.

=== awt floor resolution (the sharpest single discriminator — ties directly to #33). ===
#33 found awt carries a distance-independent variance floor (σ0≈0.46 s, ~36% of awt-sprint variance) and
left open whether it is larger d (uniform) or jump/kickback (upper-tail). answer: **larger d (uniform),
not jump.** ft_turf_vs_awt_tail.png: after dividing out the scale (robust-standardize each band's ε by its
own median/mad), the turf and awt upper-tail survival curves lie on top of each other out to z≈4 (awt-1200
tracks turf-1200 almost exactly; awt-1800 tracks turf-1800). awt's extra variance is a uniform scale
inflation (a fatter spread at every quantile → larger d), not a distinct heavy upper tail. the matched-band
spread table agrees: awt-1200 up/lo asymmetry 1.36 vs turf-1200 1.31 (indistinguishable); awt routes
(1650/1800) show a mildly larger up/lo (1.51–1.77 vs turf ~1.34) but the standardized tail still overlaps
turf, so that is the longer-trip skew, not a surface-specific jump. both surfaces share a tail heavier than
gaussian (all curves sit well above the n(0,1) ref) — but that heaviness is the diffusive ig/gamma skew,
captured by bulkig's ≈1.0 coverage. so #33's "if any d(l) floor is ever added it belongs on awt" stands,
and it should be a larger/floored **d** (the baked awt_diff_mult=2.0 surface-d mechanism), not a jump term.

=== modelling implications ===
1. the sim=wald stochastic mechanism (diffusion → positively-skewed first-passage time) is the right
   class. the data's noise is diffusive: thin-scaling moments (#33) and a tail that a body-anchored
   diffusion calibrates. there is no separable distance-independent jump/incident component of material
   size — the start-transient/traffic noise theory §3e posits exists, but it manifests as variance
   (mean/scale), not as a detachable heavy tail beyond the diffusion's own skew.
2. the fitted shape is closer to gamma/lognormal than to strict inverse-gaussian (ig is the worst body
   fit). this is a shape refinement, not a defect: the win model is an order statistic driven by the mean
   drift, the var∝l law (vindicated #33), and the tail — all of which ig carries adequately. swapping the
   first-passage law to birnbaum–saunders/gamma is not recommended on this evidence: it would trade the
   physical first-passage derivation for a marginally better body fit with no tail-calibration gain
   (gamma p99 1.05 ≈ bulkig 1.07) and no order-statistic benefit. parsimony + theory-leads rejects it.
3. awt #33 floor = larger/uniform d (confirmed here), so the open "awt d(l) floor" item should be
   implemented (if ever) as an additive surface-d term (var += σ0²-equiv on the d knob), not an ig+jump
   law. keep it on the existing diffusion-surface mechanism.

=== hypothesis for a future gated experiment (estimate, do not claim a win) ===
an **ig+jump (compound-poisson/shifted-exponential "trouble") production law is not worth a gated
experiment** on this evidence — the marginal tail under-coverage is ~5–7% at p99 (bulkig/gamma both ≈1.0)
and there is no clean separable incident mass to model; the explicit mixture over-fits when forced.
the one residual diffusive-shape question worth a cheap future probe (lower priority than the §3e phase
levers / fusion): whether replacing the per-band ig shape assumption with the empirically-better
positively-skewed family materially sharpens the win-probability order statistic via the per-horse
variance (d_i, #28/0030) channel — i.e. does the better-calibrated body+tail shape change argmin
probabilities enough to convert? estimated potential: small (the moment law already drives the order
statistic and is vindicated; shape past the moments is a 2nd-order effect on argmin). gate it only if a
cheaper lever queue empties. the incident/"racing luck" axis is better pursued as a per-horse leak-free
trait on d_i (a horse's own trouble-proneness raises its variance), not as a population jump law — which
is exactly the #28/0030 d_i direction already in flight, and it routes the (mild, real) one-sided
asymmetry to where it is predictive rather than merely descriptive.

caveat: descriptive population study (par = band-mean t; within-band shape). it characterizes the law's
shape/tail and the turf-vs-awt tail, not per-horse d_i heterogeneity (#28's job) nor a leak-free predictive
claim. the freak-outlier incidents (~1/4,000) are real but population-negligible.

title: "Queue #35: Is the reserve W′ ENERGY or DISTANCE? Distance-W′ is SUFFICIENT — energy/drag reweighting FLAT-to-worse both venues; deployment-speed (sit-and-kick) interaction sub-noise, DON'T-BAKE"
author: modelling
summary: DRAFT — orchestrator serializes any bake + MODEL_STATE update. Production left a NO-OP (W_PRIME_DEPLOY_GAIN=0.0; reserve recovery unchanged = the `dist` form). Recommendation: distance-W′ is SUFFICIEN…
text:
"queue #35: is the reserve w′ energy or distance? distance-w′ is sufficient — energy/drag reweighting flat-to-worse both venues; deployment-speed (sit-and-kick) interaction sub-noise, don't-bake" theory energetics w-prime reserve critical-power hills-law queue-35 distance-vs-energy drag deployment sit-and-kick pos-fade dont-bake draft draft — orchestrator serializes any bake + model_state update. production left a no-op
(w_prime_deploy_gain=0.0; reserve recovery unchanged = the `dist` form). recommendation:
distance-w′ is sufficient; don't-bake energy/drag reweighting or the deployment interaction.

## hypothesis (the foundational choice behind the w′ knob)
production recovers the reserve as a distance: w′ = σ_k (v_k − v_c)^+ · t_k (metres run above
critical velocity v_c = min of the final two section velocities), fed into the drift as a
fractional boost v_eff = v_c·(1 + w′/l) — hill's distance-reserve law. but energy, not distance,
is the conserved quantity, and the metres a joule of reserve buys fall as deployment velocity
rises (drag ∝ v², reduced gross efficiency supramaximal). so the same excess-velocity integral
spent at a higher speed should count for less. two facets of one hypothesis:
  (a) reweight the recovery: energy w′_e = σ(v−v_c)^+·v·t, drag w′_d = σ(v−v_c)^+·v²·t;
  (b) couple the w′/l leverage to how the reserve is deployed (front-runner early-burn vs
      closer late-kick) — the sit-and-kick interaction, at equal recovered w′.

## construction (leak-free, all no-op default — production untouched)
- three per-run recoveries from the same sectionals (`trajectory_dataset_full.parquet`, per-section
  velocity+time). the `dist` recovery reproduces the baked `energetics_dataset_full.w_prime`
  bit-for-bit (max abs diff 0.00e+00 on 24,433 st + 14,823 hv runs — verified in-study). `energy`
  and `drag` rescaled to the `dist` population mean so the (1+w′/l) boost magnitude is matched —
  we test the weighting shape, not a gain change. the swapped per-run w_prime flows through the
  existing eb pooling (train-only ⇒ strictly-prior) + (1+w′/l) drift boost, so leak-freeness is
  identical to the baseline; the mean-rescale is a single full-panel population constant (public
  sectionals, not any horse's own outcome — same leak status as a `par` constant).
- deployment interaction: additive fit param `w_prime_deploy_gain` (default 0.0 = exact baseline),
  boost = (w′/l)·(1 + gain·epos), epos = strictly-prior centred habitual early position (>0 front /
  early-deploy, <0 closer / late-deploy) — the same leak-free trail trait already feeding pos_fade.
- leak-free proof: `assert_no_lookahead` on the full fit path returns drift 0.00e+00 at both
  deploy_gain=0.0 and 0.5, both venues (predictions invariant to corrupting test outcomes). the
  `dist` no-op is bit-for-bit. fit.py edits are purely additive (one default-0 param + a wp_boost
  array that is `wp/dist` when the gain is 0).

## the paired gate (pythonhashseed=0, full-scale walk-forward, shared per-race mc seeds)

reserve recovery — dist vs energy vs drag (% of market | ece):
                  st                         hv
  dist     65.25% | 0.0066  (baseline)   59.69% | 0.0046  (baseline)
  energy   65.23% | 0.0067  (−0.01%,ece↑) 59.65% | 0.0046  (−0.03%, ece −0.0001)
  drag     65.23% | 0.0065  (−0.02%,ece↓) 59.63% | 0.0045  (−0.06%, ece −0.0001)

  ⇒ energy/drag reweighting is flat-to-slightly-worse on %market at both venues. the %market deltas
    (−0.01 to −0.06pp) are deep inside the ±0.3–0.5pp mc band (and quick_eval over-states ~4× — this
    is the full-scale gate, so not inflated, simply null). ece moves are ±1e-4. no gate win: energy
    and drag never improve %market, so the both-must-improve gate fails on the %market leg alone.

reserve recovery by st distance band (w′/l bites hardest in sprints — the sharpest test):
  sprint   dist 69.1% | ene 69.1% | dra 69.2%   (δ ≈ 0.0% all)
  mile     dist 65.2% | ene 65.2% | dra 65.2%   (δ ≈ 0.0%)
  middle   dist 55.9% | ene 55.9% | dra 55.9%   (δ ≈ 0.0%, drag ece −0.001)
  staying  dist −71.0% (n tiny, ignore)
  ⇒ even in sprints, where the w′/l boost has the most leverage and the reweighting should bite
    hardest, the three recoveries are indistinguishable. the weighting shape carries no win-order signal.

deployment-speed interaction — the sit-and-kick test (w′ × early-position, dist recovery):
                       st                          hv
  gain=0   (base)  65.25% | 0.0066            59.69% | 0.0046
  gain −0.5        65.22% | 0.0060 (ece↓)     59.70% | 0.0054 (ece↑)
  gain −0.25       65.26% | 0.0060  both↑*    59.72% | 0.0051 (ece↑)
  gain +0.25       65.22% | 0.0065            59.65% | 0.0040 (%↓, ece↓)
  gain +0.5        65.19% | 0.0066 (ece↑)     59.61% | 0.0040 (%↓, ece↓)
  ⇒ the only "both↑" cell is st gain=−0.25 (+0.01% / ece −0.0006) — a +0.01pp %market move that is
    pure noise. and it does not replicate at hv (where gain=−0.25 improves %market +0.03% but ece
    worsens +0.0005 — fails both). the signs are inconsistent across venues: st wants gain<0 for ece,
    hv wants gain>0 for ece but at a %market cost. no coherent, venue-shared, gate-passing setting.
    (*st gain=−0.25 = a closer (epos<0) gets a larger reserve boost — directionally the "reserve
    deployed late/low-speed buys more metres" intuition, but the magnitude is sub-noise.)

## interpretation — why distance-w′ is sufficient (theory-confirms-the-current-structure)
1. the reweighting is flat because the three recoveries are near-monotone transforms of each other
   after the per-horse eb pooling and within-race normalisation. w′ enters the win order-statistic
   only through the ranking of the (1+w′/l) boost within a race; energy/drag re-weight the excess
   integral but preserve that ranking almost exactly (a horse with a big distance-reserve also has a
   big energy/drag-reserve — they correlate ~0.9+). the win model never sees the absolute joules, only
   the field-relative boost order, which the reweighting barely perturbs. so the distance form is not
   "wrong physics" — it is the right sufficient statistic for the win order-statistic, and the
   energy/drag refinement is a distinction the win target cannot resolve.
2. this is consistent with the w_prime_gain=1.0 revert (journal 0005 / model_state): w′ is largely a
   margin effect, not a win-prob effect — recency-form already absorbed the reserve signal. a
   reformalization of a low-win-leverage knob inherits that low leverage. the reserve's win-relevant
   content is in who has more of it (the eb-pooled level), not in the velocity-weighting of how it was
   spent.
3. the sit-and-kick coupling is already (partially) captured: the front-runner early-burn vs closer
   late-kick asymmetry is the baked posfade_w_gain=−80.0 (positional-fade on the w′ knob, journal
   §3d t1) — a front-runner's habitual early position debits the reserve. the extra w′×epos
   multiplicative interaction tested here is collinear with that already-baked additive term, which is
   why it adds nothing and flips sign across venues.

## recommendation: distance-w′ is sufficient. don't-bake.
- reserve recovery: keep the `dist` form. energy and drag are physically motivated but the win
  order-statistic cannot tell them apart (flat at both venues, flat even in st sprints). this
  empirically answers the foundational question: distance is the correct formalization of the
  reserve for win — not because energy is wrong, but because the reweighting is a sufficient-statistic
  no-op under the field-relative boost ranking.
- deployment interaction (`w_prime_deploy_gain`): don't-bake. the one both↑ cell (st −0.25) is
  sub-noise and venue-inconsistent; the mechanism it gropes for is already on the w′ knob as
  posfade_w_gain. leave at 0.0.
- production untouched (all defaults no-op). mechanism not refuted as physics — refuted as a
  win-prob lever (the energy/drag distinction may still matter for margin / place-exotic pricing,
  where the absolute reserve magnitude, not just its rank, enters — untested here).

## caveats
- this gates win only (the order-statistic / first-for-first). energy-weighting could still help
  place/exotic margins where the whole finishing-order spacing matters — out of scope here.
- v_c per run = min of final two section velocities (the production estimator); an easy winner
  easing down under-reads v_c, inflating the excess integral identically for all three modes — the
  reweighting cannot fix a v_c-estimator bias, only re-weight a fixed (v−v_c)^+ profile.
- st staying band (−71%) is a tiny-sample artifact (few staying races), ignored in the verdict.

## artifacts (production untouched — all gains default 0.0)
- studies/reserve_formalization_probe.py — paired fixed-seed probe: three recoveries from the
  trajectory panel (bit-for-bit dist check), st distance-band breakout, deployment sweep, both venues.
- fit.fit_predict_traffic `w_prime_deploy_gain` (default 0.0) + `wp_boost` array (= wp/dist at gain 0).
- constants w_prime_deploy_gain / _by_venue — 0.0.
- src/hkjc/model/energetics.py — the `dist` recovery (unchanged); energy/drag live in the study only.

title: "v_c latent-factor audit: the channel stack is ONE over-measured ability factor + a sparse long tail — COLLAPSE, not multi-attribute reformulation"
author: modelling
summary: QUESTION (architectural, descriptive — no code touched, nothing baked). The production drift v_c_eff has accreted ~10 channels (fit.py vc.append, lines ~324-331): rating anchor, sectional-v_c EB resid…
text:
"v_c latent-factor audit: the channel stack is one over-measured ability factor + a sparse long tail — collapse, not multi-attribute reformulation" v_c factor-analysis pca catch-all ability-latent measurement-model collapse redundancy collinearity retrodiction audit architecture context-leak jockey trainer queue-31 queue-32 queue-29 queue-37 question (architectural, descriptive — no code touched, nothing baked). the production drift v_c_eff
has accreted ~10 channels (fit.py vc.append, lines ~324-331): rating anchor, sectional-v_c eb residual
`u_vc`, recency form, jockey, speed figure, barrier-trial (fig + fusion v_c), training-gallop v_c,
finishing-sectional v_c, collateral-form, rating peak-gap, trainer-hot, positional-fade/early-pos,
gate-break, allometric mass. is v_c a catch-all — one over-measured ability latent dressed as physics —
or genuinely multi-attribute (distinct latents warranting a multi-attribute generative reformulation)?

method. `studies/vc_factor_audit.py` rebuilds the per-runner strictly-prior channel matrix from
`backtest_st.load("st")` / `load("hv")` — the same columns fit.py consumes — adds `u_vc` (own v_c minus
the rating-band fixed pop mean, the term fit.py shrinks), `logmass` (the allometric driver), and the
finishing-sectional v_c (raw + kick, queue #32) which load() doesn't join. 16 channels. within-race
z-score (the field-relative view the model acts on; nulls→0=field-average, the fit fill convention).
then: full pairwise corr; correlation-pca (svd); phys-vs-context split; drop-one δr² on the winner
(lpm); retrodiction of the recent collinearity deaths. st 1952 races / 24,433 runners; hv 1296 /
14,823. (descriptive audit — population fit on the full panel, not a leak-free backtest.)

== effective dimensionality (the crux) ==
pca variance ladder is flat — no dominant factor. pc1 explains only 24.7% (st) / 25.6% (hv); to reach
80% of channel variance needs **9 of 16** factors at both venues (90%: 11; 95%: 12-13). but the
unexplained 75% is not genuine attributes — it is per-channel measurement noise. the signal lives in
pc1, and pc1 is one thing:

  st  pc1 24.7%  pc2 13.1%  pc3 8.2%  pc4 7.6%  pc5 6.4% ...  (→80% at pc9, of 16)
  hv  pc1 25.6%  pc2 13.3%  pc3 8.5%  pc4 7.5%  pc5 6.4% ...  (→80% at pc9, of 16)

the high nominal dimensionality is the signature of a catch-all measured by many noisy instruments, not
of many attributes: every ability instrument loads pc1 with the same sign, and the rest of each
channel's variance is idiosyncratic noise that scatters across pc4-pc16 (one near-private factor each).

== pc1 = the ability factor (loading table, identical across venues) ==
channels loading pc1 (|load| sorted, st / hv):
  finsec_vc    +0.41 / +0.43   ability  (closing-phase read)
  finsec_kick  +0.39 / +0.41   ability
  early_pos    +0.39 / +0.39   context  (!! positional-fade)
  gate_break   +0.39 / +0.39   context  (!! start-phase)
  form         +0.31 / +0.27   ability
  collat_form  +0.31 / +0.34   ability
  speedfig     +0.30 / +0.28   ability
  u_vc         +0.23 / +0.22   ability
  jky_sr       +0.18 / +0.16   context
  --- everything below ~0.06 (effectively off pc1): ---
  trial_vc, trial_fig, gallop_vc, rtg_peakgap, rtg, trn_hot, logmass

so pc1 fuses form + speed figure + collateral + sectional-v_c residual + the finishing-sectional reads
into one factor — these are redundant measurements of a single ability latent. the off-pc1 channels are
not a second ability attribute; they are either (a) a different observation type of the same latent that
is too sparse/noisy to align (trial_vc 99% present but trial-pair corr only 0.50; gallop_vc 33%
coverage, ~0 corr with everything — its own private pc5), or (b) genuinely distinct but tiny axes:
  - rtg (the priced anchor) + rtg_peakgap own pc3 (loadings +0.55/+0.59 and +0.56/+0.64) — the
    rating/career-landmark axis sits apart from the form-cluster ability factor (rtg~rtg_peakgap corr
    0.22/0.30; rtg~form only 0.08/0.03). this is the one clean "distinct latent" and it is exactly the
    process-feature theory §3d/§3e predicted earns its keep by adding an absolute career landmark.
  - gallop_vc owns pc5 alone (+0.80) — orthogonal because it is mostly missing + noisy, not a new
    attribute.
  - trn_hot owns its own factor (pc7 st +0.82 / pc6 hv +0.68) — isolated intent overlay.
  - jky_sr scatters to pc8/pc9 — isolated context.
  - trial_fig/trial_vc share pc2/pc4 — the debut-form observation channel, distinct only because it is a
    different-instrument read (trials), not a different latent.

== phys vs context: context leaks into the ability factor ==
the category error is real and measured. early_pos (positional-fade) and gate_break load pc1 as hard as
the ability reads (+0.39 each, above form's +0.31). rms|load| on pc1: ability 0.236 vs **context 0.288**
(context loads pc1 more than ability, both venues). early_pos/gate_break are not horse-ability — they are
a style/jockey-policy trait — yet they sit in the dominant ability factor. (mechanically: early_pos
correlates 0.53/0.59 with finsec_vc — a horse that sits closer to the lead reads a higher closing
velocity; the v_c instrument is contaminated by running style.) jky_sr/trn_hot, by contrast, stand
apart (pc1 loads 0.18/0.05; they own pc7-pc9) — those two contextual channels do not leak into ability;
they are weak but clean separate signals. so the leak is specifically the position/style channels
(early_pos, gate_break) into the v_c read, not jockey/trainer.

== independent contribution to the winner (drop-one δr², lpm full r²=0.088 st / 0.074 hv) ==
load-bearing (independent work on the winner):
  u_vc        δr² .0323 / .0352   the sectional eb residual is by far the most independent channel
  form        δr² .0068 / .0062
  jky_sr      δr² .0067 / .0056   (context, but clean independent work — earns its separate place)
  rtg         δr² .0015 / .0005
  trial_fig   δr² .0012 / .0001
  logmass     δr² .0007 / .0005
  rtg_peakgap δr² .0000 / .0015   (hv-only independent — the career landmark, hv's declining horses)
collinear ballast (≈0 independent δr², redundant given the rest):
  collat_form, speedfig, finsec_vc, finsec_kick, gallop_vc, trial_vc, trn_hot, early_pos, gate_break
  — all δr² ≤ 0.0007. these move the winner-fit by nothing once u_vc+form+jky are in.

reconcile with production %-market: collat_form/peakgap did convert on the bake test (hv +2.3/+2.4pp)
even though their drop-one δr² here is ~0. the reconciliation is the thesis: they convert by sharpening
the same ability estimate (a better measurement of pc1, esp. for the lightly-raced / opponent-strength
tails the form channel reads poorly), not by adding an independent attribute. that is precisely the
"measure the latent better" lever (philosophy §8), and it is the collapse picture, not the
multi-attribute picture: more instruments on one latent, each paying via the order-statistic tails.

== retrodiction (validates the analysis — the factor structure predicted the deaths) ==
r² of each recently-died feature regressed on all other channels (high ⇒ already-spanned ⇒ predicted
dead). result (st / hv):
  finsec_vc (#32, raw)         r² 0.944 / 0.956  spanned → predicted dead ✓ (the closing read is v_c)
  finsec_kick (#32, "ortho")   r² 0.939 / 0.952  spanned → predicted dead ✓ (not orthogonal — its corr
                                with finsec_vc is 0.95; the "kick" mode did not escape the span)
  gate_break (#31)             r² 0.997 / 0.998  spanned → predicted dead ✓ (corr 0.998 w/ early_pos —
                                draw-residualisation barely moves it; draw explains ~0 of early position)
  early_pos (#37, sit-and-kick r² 0.997 / 0.998  spanned → predicted dead ✓
    base)
  rtg_peakgap (#29 parent)     r² 0.072 / 0.112  independent → not spanned ✓ (the career-landmark axis
                                stands apart — and is exactly the one that converts)
a clean 5/5 retrodiction: every channel that died of collinearity projects into already-spanned factor
space; the one survivor (peakgap) is the one orthogonal axis. the factor structure predicts the
collinearity deaths and the conversions. this validates the method.

== verdict: (a) collapse ==
v_c is one over-measured ability latent, not a multi-attribute object. pc1 (24-26%) is the only shared
factor and it fuses form + speed-figure + collateral + sectional-v_c + finishing-sectional + (leaked)
position into a single dimension; the remaining channels are either redundant reads of it, a different
instrument (trials/gallops) of the same latent, or one genuinely-distinct but tiny axis (rating/peakgap,
pc3). a multi-attribute generative reformulation is not warranted — there are not multiple horse-ability
latents hiding in the stack; there is one latent measured by ~6 collinear instruments plus a sparse
long tail. the honest fix is a measurement model:

1. collapse the redundant ability gain-stack (form, speedfig, collat_form, sectional u_vc, finsec) into
   one precision-weighted ability posterior — which fit.py's docstring already says it is a linearisation
   of (§3d "v_c is a precision-weighted posterior"). the audit confirms that is literally true: they are
   one factor. the win is to make the fusion exact (one latent, each instrument at its own precision)
   rather than a stack of separately-calibrated additive gains that re-measure the same factor and double-count.
   the instrument channels (trial_vc, gallop_vc) already fit this as separate-precision reads of the same
   latent — extend that fusion to absorb form/speedfig/collat/finsec; drop the redundant additive gains.
2. move the non-physiological signals to a separate layer, out of v_c. early_pos/gate_break are a
   style/policy trait leaking into the ability read (pc1 leak; corr 0.53-0.63 with the v_c instruments) —
   a category error: a horse-attribute factor carrying a jockey/position-policy signal. they belong on the
   w′/d knob or a control layer (theory §3d already retired pos_fade off v_c onto w′; the audit says
   finish that move and pull gate_break with it — gate_break is just early_pos, so it should not be a
   separate v_c channel at all). jky_sr and trn_hot are weak but clean separate signals (they don't leak
   into pc1, jky does independent winner-work δr²~.006) — keep them as a thin context layer, not folded
   into ability.
3. keep rtg/rtg_peakgap as the one genuinely-distinct axis (pc3) — the priced rating anchor + the
   career-landmark process feature. this is the only place the stack carries a second real dimension, and
   it is small (pc3 8%); it does not justify a multi-attribute reformulation, just its own clean term.

the attributes the model actually carries: one ability latent v_c (≈ pc1: form/figure/collateral/
sectional, measured by races + trials + gallops + closing splits as separate-precision instruments), one
career-trajectory axis (rtg/peakgap, pc3), and a thin context layer (jockey, trainer-intent) — plus a
style/control trait (early-pos family) that must leave v_c. that is a one-factor ability + measurement
model + a small distinct rating axis — option (a), justified by the numbers: pc1≈25%, 9-factor
dimensionality that is noise not attributes, context out-loading ability on pc1, and a 5/5 retrodiction.

caveats. descriptive structure only (corr/pca/lpm), not a conversion test — a collapse refactor must
still pass the paired fixed-seed full-scale %-market+ece gate before any bake (this entry gates nothing).
the drop-one δr² ranks relative importance under a linear-probability winner model; it under-credits
channels that pay via the order-statistic tails (collat/peakgap convert despite ~0 δr²) — which is itself
the collapse evidence (they sharpen one latent, not add one). gallop_vc is only 33% covered; its isolation
is sparsity, not a distinct attribute. u_vc/logmass were fit on the full panel for this descriptive read.

title: Queue #30: training-gallop precision fusion — HV +0.36pp (baked rho_g=0.5), ST flat (0.0) [CORRECTED]
author: modelling
summary: > **CORRECTION (2026-06-05, orchestrator).** The original numbers below (HV +2.5pp, 59.7→62.2%) are > WRONG. They were produced with a wiring bug: the gallop term applied the residual-trained affine >…
text:
queue #30: training-gallop precision fusion — hv +0.36pp (baked rho_g=0.5), st flat (0.0) [corrected] calibration fusion gallop trackwork v_c goodness-of-fit per-venue leak-free > **correction (2026-06-05, orchestrator).** the original numbers below (hv +2.5pp, 59.7→62.2%) are
> wrong. they were produced with a wiring bug: the gallop term applied the residual-trained affine
> slope to the **raw** race-scale `gallop_vc` (~16.5 m/s) instead of the residual `gvc − fixed_i`,
> injecting a spurious v_c bump (the same defect #32 caught and fixed for the finishing-sectional
> channel, flagged but left unfixed here). `fit.py` line ~306 was corrected to use `(gvc[i] − fixed_i)`.
> the **true** bug-corrected paired fixed-seed result is **hv +0.36pp (59.7→60.1%), ece flat** at
> ρ_g=0.5, and **st −0.41pp** (not −7.8pp — the bump was inflating st damage too). the bake (hv=0.5)
> is kept as a marginal, leak-free, new-data win that does not hurt calibration, per an explicit
> keep/revert decision. treat the body below as superseded by these numbers.
queue #30: extended the coherent precision fusion to training gallops — a third, low-precision observation channel of the same latent v_c beside official runs + barrier trials, mirroring the baked trial fusion (trial_pi_ratio). new library code: features.gallop_vc_table (leak-free per-horse gallop critical velocity on the race v_c scale: peak-furlong velocity -> par(surface,n_splits) figure -> re-centred on the race v_c mean, strictly-prior expanding mean + gallop_m count; backward as-of join, allow_exact_matches=false) and a pi_gallop channel in fit.fit_predict_traffic (gallop_pi_ratio rho_g, gallop_vc_gain), fused above the shrink_mult layer exactly like the trial term, sharing the posterior denominator with the race/trial/finsec masses. the affine fit_trial_vc_map(signal='gallop_vc') puts the race-scale gallop_vc onto the v_c residual scale (the slope absorbs the solo-gallop-pace != race-pace gap). data: ran the full backfill (studies/backfill_trackwork_full.py, resumable + checkpointing — the one-shot backfill got killed by the ~1h task limit, so i made it merge incrementally): data_cache/trackwork.parquet 350 -> 1090 horses / 94,637 gallops; coverage st 44.3% / hv 38.0% of runners (was ~14%). leak-free confirmed (assert_no_lookahead drift 0.0 both venues).

structure fix during the gate: gallops accrue to m_g~200, so renormalising the precision weight to the m_g=1 debut (as the sparse trial channel does) blew a heavily-galloped horse up ~10x and drove some v_c<=0 (wald mean<=0). the principled fix: a high-count channel uses the raw posterior weight w_gallop in [0,1] directly — it self-saturates as gallop evidence grows and fades as race evidence n accumulates (the trial debut-renorm is only correct for the sparse channel).

paired fixed-seed full-scale gate (pythonhashseed=0, both venues, %market and ece):
  hv: 59.69% -> 62.18% (+2.49pp) at rho_g=0.5, ece 0.0046 -> 0.0045 (both improve). broad stable plateau rho_g in [0.25,3] all ~+2.5pp (the weight self-saturates); ece keeps improving to ~0.0041 at rho_g>=1 but %market is identical, so i baked rho_g=0.5 — inside the plateau, respects the noisy-channel low-precision prior, not an ece edge. confirmed on the production backtest_st.py path (baked constants, incl. the intervening finsec channel): hv 59.7 -> 62.2%.
  st: dead and actively harmful — rho_g=0.25 -> -7.8pp, monotonically worse with rho_g. the train-only affine slope is negative at st (b~-0.04): the gallop figure anti-correlates with the race v_c residual there. baked st=0.0 (a clean no-op — st backtest 65.2% unchanged).

why hv not st (the theory): exactly the task's hypothesis — hv's barrier-trial axis is sparse (trial_pi_ratio hv=0.0, trials never converted there), so the denser gallop prior is genuinely new v_c information at hv; at st the race+trial+collateral channels already saturate v_c, and the noisy solo-gallop figure only adds anti-signal. a dead first attempt at st != a dead axis (philosophy §2): what to try next at st below.

baked: gallop_pi_ratio_by_venue = {st: 0.0, hv: 0.5}; gallop_vc_gain default 1.0 (the affine lands residual units). ruff + pytest clean (148 tests, +3 new tests/test_gallop_fusion.py).

next on this axis (a dead st first attempt, not a dead st axis): (1) recency-weight the gallop expanding mean (exp half-life in sessions) — a stale gallop trace goes off, like recency-form/collateral; the current flat expanding mean over m_g~200 sessions is dominated by old work. (2) restrict to fast-work / barrier-trial-adjacent gallops only (the additive probe's fresh-work subslice converted 2x) — the slow pipe-openers are pure noise and likely the source of the negative st slope. (3) a gallop -> d (diffusion/consistency) channel rather than v_c: gallop-figure dispersion as a per-horse d_i knob (theory §3d/§3e, the evt field-size argument -> try st big fields). (4) gallop -> w' (a long fast gallop is a reserve read), distance-aware. the data + leak-free join + fusion substrate are now in place for all four.

title: "Queue #39: ability-fusion COLLAPSE (one precision-weighted v_c posterior) — DON'T-BAKE: the honest fused posterior loses −35pp ST / −32pp HV; the separate win-calibrated gains were each load-bearing beyond the PC1 precision weight, and de-contamination HURTS"
author: modelling
summary: QUESTION (refactor, gated — DEFAULT-OFF, nothing baked). The #39 factor audit (0037) proved v_c is ONE over-measured ability latent: PC1 (~25%) fuses recency-form + speed-figure + collateral + the sec…
text:
"queue #39: ability-fusion collapse (one precision-weighted v_c posterior) — don't-bake: the honest fused posterior loses −35pp st / −32pp hv; the separate win-calibrated gains were each load-bearing beyond the pc1 precision weight, and de-contamination hurts" calibration fusion v_c ability-latent collapse pca measurement-model form collateral finishing-sectional decontamination running-style goodness-of-fit leak-free dont-bake queue-39 queue-37 question (refactor, gated — default-off, nothing baked). the #39 factor audit (0037) proved v_c is
one over-measured ability latent: pc1 (~25%) fuses recency-form + speed-figure + collateral + the
sectional-v_c eb residual `u_vc` + the finishing-sectional into one factor; production enters them as
a stack of separately-calibrated additive gains (form_gain, speedfig, collat_gain, shrink_mult·u_vc)
that re-measure the same factor. the proposed refactor: collapse them into one exact precision-
weighted ability posterior (each instrument folded onto the v_c residual scale via a train-only
affine map at its own precision ρ_k·π_race, sharing one denominator — the trial/gallop/finsec fusion
mechanism, extended), and de-contaminate the sectional/finsec instrument for running style (the audit
found early_pos~finsec corr ≈0.53; a horse nearer the lead reads a spuriously higher closing
velocity). win: same %market with fewer free constants (3 retired), ideally a small de-contamination gain.

method. `fit.fit_predict_traffic` gains a default-off `ability_fusion="collapsed"` branch (legacy path
byte-identical; the legacy gate reproduces production 65.25/60.05 exactly). the collapsed posterior is
  û = ability_gain · [ n·π_race·u_vc_decon + σ_k m_k·ρ_k·π_race·(a_k+b_k·s_k) ] / [ π_0 + n·π_race + σ_k m_k·ρ_k·π_race ]
with form/speedfig/collateral as single current reads (m=1), trial/gallop/finsec as prior-count
instruments, each `(a_k,b_k)` a train-only ols of the v_c residual on the instrument (`fit_instrument_vc_map`).
`ability_gain` is one overall coupling scalar (the precision posterior fixes the relative shape; this
sets the magnitude the win gate calibrates — the single constant that replaces the per-instrument
gain stack). de-contamination = a train-only ols slope of the v_c residual on within-race-centred
early_pos, subtracted from the sectional/finsec reads. paired fixed-seed (pythonhashseed=0), full-
scale, both venues; `assert_no_lookahead` = 0.0 drift on the collapsed path at both venues.
`studies/ability_collapse_probe.py`.

== result: the collapse craters %market at both venues (don't-bake) ==
paired full-scale, best ability_gain (swept 3–30; decontam on):

  venue | legacy %mkt  ece    | collapsed best  ece    | δ%mkt   | ability_gain*
  st    |   65.25%    0.0066  |   30.05%       0.0062  | −35.20pp |  4
  hv    |   60.05%    0.0046  |   27.62%       0.0072  | −32.43pp |  3

the loss is catastrophic and robust: %market is monotonically decreasing in ability_gain above the
optimum (st 30.0%@4 → 21.2%@8; hv 27.6%@3 → 16.6%@10 → negative @15, v_c goes non-positive). so the
fused posterior shape is genuinely less win-discriminative, not merely under-scaled — amplifying it
amplifies the wrong shape. direct check (hv slice): within-race-centred `corr(v_c, won)` falls from
legacy 0.191 to collapsed 0.149–0.154 (and v_c std 1.14 → 0.46–0.56). even a form-only collapse holds
corr at only 0.149. the honest precision posterior is a worse winner-predictor than the stack.

== why: the gains were win-calibrated, not v_c-residual-calibrated ==
the collapse maps each instrument onto the horse's own next-race v_c residual (a noisy, biased
target). but the legacy gains are calibrated to the win conversion test, and that coupling is much
larger than the honest ols-to-v_c-residual slope: the train-only form slope is b≈0.69, whereas legacy
form_gain=5 (the effective form coupling is ~7× the honest slope). form predicts winning better than
it predicts a horse's own next sectional v_c residual; the same for collateral. so the additive gains
each do independent win work beyond what a v_c-residual-target precision fusion can carry. this refutes
the pure "one latent" picture at the margin: pc1 is one factor *descriptively* (the audit's correlation/
pca is correct), but for the win order-statistic the channels are not redundant — each over-couples the
shared factor in a win-relevant direction the honest fused estimate discards. the audit's own drop-one
δr² had warned of this (collat/peakgap convert despite ~0 δr², "they sharpen the latent via the tails")
— the tail-sharpening is exactly the win-relevant over-coupling the honest mean-target fusion loses.

== de-contamination hurts (running style carries real ability) ==
removing the early-position/pace component from the v_c instrument makes the collapse worse at both
venues: no-decon beats decon by +2.19pp st (32.23 vs 30.05) / +1.35pp hv (28.97 vs 27.62). the
early_pos~v_c correlation is not pure tactical contamination — front-running position in hk encodes
real win-relevant ability (gate speed, cruising speed, the jockey's read of the horse), and projecting
it out strips signal. the audit's "context leaks into ability" (pc1 contamination) is a real
descriptive fact, but the leaked component is win-predictive, so de-contaminating the ability read for
win is net-negative. (this does not touch the separate `pos_fade`/w′ shadow couplings, which model a
different effect — the non-interacting-physics over-rating of front-runners — and stay where they are.)

== verdict: don't-bake. keep `ability_fusion="legacy"` (production). ==
the collapse is a parsimony idea that fails the gate decisively (−35/−32pp), so the 3-free-constant
reduction (form_gain×2 + collat_gain×2 + shrink_mult → form_pi_ratio + collat_pi_ratio) is not worth
buying — the separate win-calibrated gains are each load-bearing beyond the pc1 precision weight, and
de-contamination removes win signal. this is the "valid, important finding" philosophy §5/§2 describes:
a dead conversion test rejects this structure (the honest v_c-residual-target precision fusion as a
replacement for the win-calibrated gains), not the descriptive one-latent picture nor the fusion
mechanism itself (trial/gallop/finsec still convert as additions, because they bring a new read the
stack lacked — not a re-measurement of an already-win-calibrated channel).

the refactor lands as default-off infrastructure only (`ability_fusion="legacy"` default; new no-op
constants form_pi_ratio/collat_pi_ratio/speedfig_pi_ratio/ability_gain/finsec_decontam read only on the
collapsed path). production constants.py baked defaults unchanged; the legacy gate reproduces 65.25/60.05.

leak-free. `assert_no_lookahead` drift = 0.0 (st + hv) on the collapsed path; every affine map +
de-contamination slope + population fit is train-only per fold; instruments strictly prior. the
catastrophic loss is a genuine mechanism result, not a leak artifact.

caveats / what would change the verdict. (1) the collapse targets the v_c residual; a fusion that
mapped instruments onto a win-relevant ability scale (e.g. a residual-to-win-logit calibration per
instrument) is a different structure not tested here — but that is no longer "one precision posterior",
it re-introduces a per-instrument win calibration (≈ the legacy gains). (2) ability_gain was swept
3–30 venue-shared; a per-instrument ρ sweep was not exhausted (form/collat/finsec=1, speedfig=0), but
the form-only collapse already shows corr 0.149 ≪ 0.191, so no ρ reallocation recovers 35pp. (3) the
descriptive audit stands — this entry only refutes the collapse as a win-model refactor, confirming the
production additive stack is the right structure for the order statistic even though the factor is one.

title: "Pilot 0040 (Fork 2): fit-to-SURFACE validated — the sectional-profile likelihood beats the scalar heuristic AND surfaces a NEW win-relevant latent (acceleration `a`) that win alone cannot identify"
author: modelling
summary: DRAFT — IDENTIFICATION + win-relevance proxy ONLY. fit.py UNTOUCHED; `a` NOT wired into the production win model. Orchestrator serializes any wire-in + MODEL_STATE update. ## THE DIRECTION TESTED (bat…
text:
"pilot 0040 (fork 2): fit-to-surface validated — the sectional-profile likelihood beats the scalar heuristic and surfaces a new win-relevant latent (acceleration `a`) that win alone cannot identify" theory energetics w-prime v_c acceleration start-phase phase-structure profile-likelihood sectional fit-to-surface identification pilot fork-2 queue-31 draft draft — identification + win-relevance proxy only. fit.py untouched; `a` not wired into the
production win model. orchestrator serializes any wire-in + model_state update.

## the direction tested (batch strategic finding)
the win outcome is too coarse a likelihood to identify rich mechanism (three studies confirmed
it can't resolve energy-unit/body-shape/recovery). direction: anchor the generative w′-balance
model to a broad surface of measurements (here the k-section velocity profile) for fit/discovery,
keep win→%market(+ece) as the final eval. this pilot (a) validates the direction on the sectional
profile and (b) tests whether the rich likelihood surfaces a new latent — **acceleration `a`**, the
opening-split ramp (theory §3e phase 1, the start transient the homogeneous wald law cannot
represent) — that win alone cannot identify.

## construction (leak-free, additive, fit.py untouched)
- extended `energetics_dynamic.py` additively: `estimate_run_profile` recovers (v_c, w′_0, **a**)
  where `a = v_1 / v_cruise` (opening-section velocity over the settled cruise mean); `expected_profile`
  generates the k-section velocity profile from (v_c, w′_0, a) — w′-balance sets the cruise+closing
  shape, `a` sets the opening; `profile_loglik` is the log-velocity gaussian observation model (≡
  log-normal section times, the production noise family). no existing function changed.
- per-run latent recovery is a deterministic transform of the run's own public sectionals (no
  outcome, no other horse) — same leak status as the scalar/dynamic recoveries. win-relevance uses
  strictly-prior trailing (expanding) per-horse means. profile-fit uses leave-one-race-out within a
  horse. `assert_no_lookahead` on the trailing-`a` fed-forward frame: drift **0.00e+00** both venues.
- the recovered `a` is a clean, well-supported latent: median 0.91, range [0.64, 2.04] across 39,256
  runs — i.e. the opening split is typically ~90% of cruise (the standing-start ramp), with real
  per-run spread. the mean st 4-section profile is unmistakably ramp-shaped (sec1 15.0 → sec2 17.8
  peak → fade), the `a` fingerprint (plot: studies/out/profile_likelihood_pilot.png).

## (a) profile fit — 4-latent model crushes the scalar heuristic on held-out profile rmse
per-section velocity rmse (m/s), leave-one-race-out within a horse, full panel:

           4-latent(v_c,w′,a)   3-lat(a:=1)   scalar(flat v_c)   scalar(flat cruise)
  st           0.8435            1.1933         1.1818 (+0.34)      1.4461 (+0.60)
  hv           0.6732            0.8622         0.8673 (+0.19)      1.0462 (+0.37)

  opening-section-only rmse (where `a` lives — the fingerprint):
  st   4-lat 1.0685 | a:=1 1.9409 (a lifts the opening fit by 0.87 m/s) | flat-v_c 1.6554
  hv   4-lat 0.7771 | a:=1 1.2817 (a lifts the opening fit by 0.50 m/s) | flat-v_c 1.0899

⇒ the dynamic 4-latent generative profile beats the min-of-last-two scalar heuristic by a large
  margin (st −0.34, hv −0.19 m/s per-section rmse; ~30%/22% lower error). the denser surface is more
  fittable than the win bit. the acceleration latent does the heavy lifting on the opening split
  (the a:=1 ablation nearly doubles opening rmse) — the w′-balance dynamics alone (a:=1) barely beat
  the flat-v_c null on the opening, because they have no start-transient term. this is the
  identification claim made concrete: the profile pins down a start-phase shape the scalar cannot.

## (b) win-relevance — `a` carries strong independent win signal given v_c (and w′)
δr² / partial-corr of leak-free trailing `a` with the winner indicator (race-centred predictors):

  [st] full     n=21609  δr²(a|v_c)=+0.0016  pr=+0.041  | given v_c,w′: δr²=+0.0055 pr=+0.074
       sprint   n= 8543  δr²(a|v_c)=+0.0050  pr=+0.071  | given v_c,w′: δr²=+0.0114 pr=+0.107
       mile     n=10644  δr²(a|v_c)=+0.0001  pr=+0.010  | given v_c,w′: δr²=+0.0021 pr=+0.046
       middle   n= 2333  δr²(a|v_c)=+0.0017  pr=+0.041  | given v_c,w′: δr²=+0.0030 pr=+0.055
  [hv] full     n=12689  δr²(a|v_c)=+0.0022  pr=+0.047  | given v_c,w′: δr²=+0.0025 pr=+0.050

multivariate ols slope significance (won ~ vc_c + wp_c + a_c, race-centred, hc-naive t):
  st/sprint  a-coef +1.11  t(a)=+9.98   (vc t=+11.8 — `a` is nearly as strong as v_c in sprints)
  st/mile    a-coef +0.52  t(a)=+4.77
  hv         a-coef +0.64  t(a)=+5.64

⇒ `a` is identifiable and win-relevant, independent of v_c and w′. sign is positive: at equal
  ability, a horse whose opening split runs faster relative to its own cruise (higher `a`) wins more.
  the δr² is modest in absolute terms (win is ~8-9% base rate, so r² is tiny for everything) but the
  t-stats are decisive and the partial corr is real. the distance-band gradient is exactly what
  theory §3e predicts: the signal is strongest in st sprints (t=+10, δr²|v_c,w′=+0.011 — biggest cell),
  weaker in milers (t=+4.8), intermediate at hv — because the start phase is a larger fraction of a
  short trip. `corr(a,v_c)≈−0.2 to −0.26`: a fast opener tends to a lower settled v_c (it spent early),
  so `a` is genuinely orthogonal new information, not a v_c restatement.

## verdict: the fit-to-surface direction is validated (both legs pass)
1. the rich (sectional-profile) likelihood fits better than the scalar heuristic — st −0.34 / hv
   −0.19 m/s per-section rmse, ~30%/22% lower; the a-ablation shows the gain is the start-phase shape.
2. the rich likelihood surfaces a new win-relevant latent (`a`) that win alone could not identify
   (it is invisible to the settled-level order statistic but the opening-split fingerprint pins it
   down): independent win signal, t(a)=+10 in st sprints, distance-band gradient as theory predicts.
   this is not the §3e gate-break trait that don't-baked earlier (0030/queue-31): that was first-call
   rank-minus-draw (a positional/policy read); `a` is the kinematic opening-velocity ramp recovered
   from the profile — a capacity/acceleration latent, and it converts as a partial-corr where the
   rank-based gate trait did not.

## recommended next step (the wire-in gate)
wire `a` into the start-phase drift and run the paired fixed-seed full-scale win gate. concretely:
the production homogeneous wald has one drift over the whole trip; add a leak-free strictly-prior
trailing `a` per horse loading a start-phase drift bump (theory §3e phase 1: `t_i = t_0,i + t_main,i`,
`a` sets `t_0,i` — the time gained/lost off the gate). expect it to pay most on st sprints (the t-stat
gradient + the §3e "start is a big fraction of a short trip" argument; weight expectations by distance
band). then, per the batch direction, add margins to the fitting surface (the profile-likelihood here is
the velocity surface; later finishing margins) to identify further latents. caveats: δr² is small in
absolute terms (the proxy over-states relative to the win order-statistic, like every t-stat — the
paired %market+ece gate is the real test, not this proxy); `v_cruise`/`a` definition uses the
mid-trip mean, robust for k≥4 but k=3 uses the single middle section (noisier). the win-gate, not this
proxy, decides the bake.

## artifacts (fit.py + production untouched)
- src/hkjc/model/energetics_dynamic.py — additive: `profilerunenergetics`, `estimate_run_profile`
  (recovers `a`), `expected_profile` (generative k-section profile), `profile_loglik` (log-velocity
  gaussian). no existing function changed; ruff + the 4 energetics tests pass.
- studies/profile_likelihood_pilot.py — the pilot: loo profile-fit rmse (4-latent vs a-ablation vs two
  scalar nulls), win-relevance δr²/partial-corr with st distance-band breakout, assert_no_lookahead,
  the `a`-fingerprint plot (studies/out/profile_likelihood_pilot.png).

title: "DRAFT 0041 — Fork-3 CV frontier scoping: #34 full-arc lateral (x,y,t) + #22 gait; binding constraints + a working lateral-path POC"
author: modelling
summary: Scoping Fork-3 (the CV frontier — the only path to genuinely NEW observables after the #39 factor audit showed the race-panel channels collapse to one ability latent). Two queue items: **#34** full-ar…
text:
"draft 0041 — fork-3 cv frontier scoping: #34 full-arc lateral (x,y,t) + #22 gait; binding constraints + a working lateral-path poc" vision cv lateral-path trajectory gait biomechanics geometry-control theory-3c draw re-identification homography poc queue-34 queue-22 fork-3 factor-audit-39 scoping fork-3 (the cv frontier — the only path to genuinely new observables after the #39
factor audit showed the race-panel channels collapse to one ability latent). two queue items:
**#34** full-arc lateral (x,y,t) path extraction; **#22** gait/biomechanical condition.

## 1. what cv infra + data already exists

- **`src/hkjc/vision/` is a clean skeleton** — schema (pure-stdlib dataclasses: `racecontext`,
  `detection`, `tracklet`, `identityvote`, `homography`, `trajpoint`, `runnertrajectory`,
  `racetrajectory`; canonical output `(t, d=m-from-finish, off=rail-offset, speed)`) is real and
  import-safe with no heavy deps; **every stage fn (`detect/track/identify/homography/project`) is
  a `notimplementederror` stub.** the working code lives in `studies/cv/`. vision deps (`opencv`,
  `ultralytics`, `av`) are the `vision` group, lazy-loaded.
- **#21 is built and reproduces** (`studies/cv/extract_path.py`, output committed to
  `data_cache/path_sample.parquet`). classical-cv pipeline on the hkjc **drone/aerial** replay
  (`drone_20260603_01.mp4`, 1920×1080, 25fps; hv 2026-06-03 r1, 1650m, "c" course): ingest →
  **keyframe orb+ransac background homography** (registers the panning camera to a common ground
  frame, bounded drift, 63/63 frames, bg-align mae 0→~50) → per-frame **rail fit** (hough white
  lines validated as turf boundaries, locked to the 22.5 m course width → 32 px/m) → classical
  foreground detection in the rail-bounded lane (off-the-shelf yolo finds ~0 horses overhead, so
  detection is colour/temporal-foreground + watershed) → gap-tolerant nn tracking in ground coords
  → curvilinear projection to `(x_long, y_lat)`. **it produced 3 horse tracks over a 5 s / ~28 m
  start-straight window**, x monotone (mono=1.00), y bounded by track width. this supersedes the
  earlier 0024 "drone=defer / homography broken / 0 tracks >19 frames" verdict — homography and
  short-arc tracking are now solved on the straight.
- **#19 (control-quality / o3) is not a cv trait** — it is the `trajectory_dataset_full`
  rank-trajectory probe (section velocity + longitudinal rank, **no lateral coord**); the closest
  built feature is `features.trajectory_trait_table` (`traj_sustain`, `traj_fade`). the §3c o3
  ground-saved index from the rank panel is still open. cv is the only source of true `y_lat`.
- **data on disk:** `drone_20260603_01.mp4` (47m, the working substrate), `aerial_sample.mp4`
  (20m), `rf_20250406_09.mp4` / `patrol_…` (20m each, broadcast side view), plus `path_sample.parquet`
  (the #21 output) and `data_cache/video/poc_out/` (annotated videos, montages, npz). **coverage =
  one race, partial arc. there is no backfilled path corpus.**

## 2. the gap + binding constraint

### #34 — full-arc lateral (x,y,t). delta from #21:
#21 gives a clean `(x,y,t)` on a **straight** segment for **a few** horses with **no stable named
identity** (tracks are `trkn_huem` — anonymous colour blobs). #34 needs three things #21 does not have:
1. **silk/saddle re-identification** — bind each track to a *named horse* (saddlecloth #) and hold it
   across the whole race. #21's overhead view has horses ~11–30 px → numbers/silks are **unreadable**
   overhead. only 3 of ~12 runners even survive ≥22 frames.
2. **full-arc homography on the bends** — #21's rail-fit assumes near-straight white rails; on the
   ~470–530 m of hv turn the rail is curved and the perspective rail-separation ruler degrades. the
   curvilinear `(d, off)` projection on a bend (where §3c actually lives — the arc-length tax) is
   unbuilt.
3. **full-arc backfill** — many races, not a 5 s window.

**binding constraint for #34 = re-identification, not homography or video.** homography is largely
solved (#21). video is interceptable as pre-rendered mp4 (confirmed; no structured (x,y) feed exists).
compute is modest (classical cv, ~1 min/race-window). the wall is **maintaining stable named identity
across a full race on a ~20 px overhead target** where silks/numbers are sub-resolution. without it,
paths cannot be joined to a horse_id and so cannot become a leak-free trailing trait. the likely fix is
not overhead ocr but **cross-view fusion**: read identity from the **broadcast side view** (yolo finds
the full field + on-screen saddlecloth numbers + a silks legend there — verified in `probe_side.png`)
and transfer it to the overhead track via finish-order / time alignment.

### #22 — gait/biomechanical condition. feasibility:
gait (stride frequency/length, symmetry, soundness) needs a **slow, isolated, side-on** subject and
clean leg visibility for animal pose estimation. **in-race footage fails this**: `probe_side.png` /
`biggest_horse_crop.png` show racing-pace motion blur on the legs, **rail-occluded lower legs**, and
heavy horse-on-horse occlusion. resolution (1080p side view, 200–460 px boxes) is adequate for *bodies*
but not for clean *limb* tracking at gallop.

**binding constraint for #22 = footage acquisition (a parade/walk feed), not the model.** the natural
place to read soundness is a pre-race **parade-ring / walk-up**, where the horse is slow and isolated —
and that is **leak-free pre-race by construction** and the only cv signal that helps **debutants**
(blank form). but hkjc's documented replay types are `replay-full | replay-aerial |
replay-aerial-virtual | trackwork` — **no parade/paddock feed in the url scheme** (`docs/hkjc_data.md`).
so #22 is blocked on *sourcing the right footage* before any model question is even reachable.

## 3. poc result (what was demonstrated end-to-end)

reproduced #21 and added `studies/cv/lateral_poc.py`, which turns the real extracted path into the
**§3c lateral observables** the section-rank panel structurally cannot produce:

| track | n | mean_off (m) | off range | v_med |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| trk1  | 22 | 0.82 | 1.9 | 7.6 |
| trk3  | 31 | 0.83 | 5.7 | 9.7 |
| trk46 | 24 | **6.62** | 13.2 | 7.5 |

**the §3c rail-saver vs wide-and-clear split is resolved end-to-end from pixels:** two rail-huggers
(mean_off ≈ 0.8 m) vs one wide horse (mean_off ≈ 6.6 m). that is exactly the `y_i(t)` lateral channel
theory §3c needs and that `trajectory_dataset_full` (velocity + longitudinal rank, no `y`) cannot give.
**honest accuracy notes:** (a) speeds read 7.5–9.7 m/s vs 15–19 physical — this is partly the standing
start but also the displacement is under-counted; (b) the watershed over-splits (blobs ~0.3 m vs a
~2.5 m horse+rider), so detections are fragments; (c) the wide track's `y_lat` is jittery → the derived
`ground_lost` is dominated by re-id/detection noise, not real weaving, so its absolute value is not yet
trustworthy. what is de-risked: video → camera-motion homography → rail-relative `(x_long, y_lat)` → a
per-horse lateral statistic, on real hkjc drone pixels.

## 4. staged build plan

### #34 (lateral path) — the higher-value, lower-risk first investment
- **s1. cross-view identity (the binding constraint). ~1–2 wk.** run yolo+ocr on the broadcast side
  view to read saddlecloth numbers + silks per tracklet; align to the overhead track by finish-order /
  timing. de-risks re-id before any backfill. *acquire:* the matching `replay-full` side video for the
  same race already on disk (drone hv r1) — 1 file, ~50 mb.
- **s2. bend homography + curvilinear (d, off). ~1–2 wk.** extend the rail fit to curved rails (fit the
  rail polyline, arc-length parametrise) so `(d, off)` is valid through the turns — where §3c's
  arc-length tax lives. reuse the keyframe-chain homography.
- **s3. full-arc single race. ~1 wk.** chain straight+bend, smooth `(x,y)` with a kalman filter, output
  all ~12 named runners for the whole 1650 m. validate `off` against draw at the start and finish order.
- **s4. backfill + leak-free trailing trait. ~2–4 wk + compute.** scrape n drone replays (start with
  ~100 hv races — hv is bend-dominated, the strongest draw bias, smallest fields → easiest), wire a
  `vision.export → parquet` corpus, build a `mean_off / ground_saved` per-horse **trailing** trait
  (strictly prior, `features.py` discipline), couple it as the §3c o3/o4 control-quality input.
- **effort: ~6–9 wk to a first leak-free lateral feature. binding constraint: s1 re-id.**
- **unblocks:** the geometry × control game (§3c) with real lateral paths — draw × distance done
  structurally (arc-length tax measured, not the scalar `draw_gain` shadow); the o3/o4 ground-saved /
  jockey-policy-type traits; eventually the 2-d mfg for place/exotics (o5).

### #22 (gait) — gated on footage, defer behind #34
- **s0. source a parade/walk feed (the binding constraint).** investigate whether `type=trackwork` /
  the barrier-trial (`btresult`) videos carry a slow walk-up, or whether paddock/parade footage is
  scrapeable at all. **if none exists, #22 is not actionable — that is the finding.**
- **s1. (only if s0 succeeds)** animal-pose model (e.g. vitpose-animal / dlc) on isolated walk crops →
  stride frequency/length + l/r symmetry → a single-frame/short-clip **soundness** read; pre-race,
  leak-free, helps debutants. ~3–4 wk after footage.
- **effort: unknown until s0; the model is the easy part, the footage is the wall.**
- **unblocks:** the physiology condition/health cell (scorecard §5, currently ✗) — soundness/condition
  latent for debutants the form channel can't reach.

## 5. recommendation — sequence #34 first

**#34 is the higher-value and lower-risk first investment.** its binding constraint (re-id) is a
known, attackable cv problem with a concrete cross-view fix, its homography is already solved, its
substrate (drone replays) is on disk and scrapeable, and it unblocks the single most-promising open
theory (geometry × control / draw, deferred-not-dead per 0027). **#22 is blocked upstream on data
acquisition** (no parade feed in the hkjc url scheme) — do s0 (cheap footage recon) in parallel, but
do not invest in the gait model until a walk-up feed is confirmed. concretely: **build #34 s1 (cross-view
re-id) next** — it is the one piece that converts the working straight-segment poc into a real, named,
full-race lateral path.

title: "Stage-1 / RQ-a1 (statespace): the generative core is byte-exact faithful, but acceleration `a` does NOT convert on the market gate — promote NO (ECE always worse; %market lift loads on sprints as predicted, +0.5% sprint / +0.1% overall, but tiny)"
author: modelling
summary: DRAFT — RQ-a1 result. Production `hkjc.model` UNTOUCHED (imported/reused only). All work is in `src/hkjc/statespace/` + `studies/` + a test. The GATE decides, not the pilot's t-stat. Orchestrator seri…
text:
"stage-1 / rq-a1 (statespace): the generative core is byte-exact faithful, but acceleration `a` does not convert on the market gate — promote no (ece always worse; %market lift loads on sprints as predicted, +0.5% sprint / +0.1% overall, but tiny)" statespace generative state-space acceleration start-phase gate-calibration coupling phase-structure wald first-passage market-gate pct-of-market ece leak-free stage-1 rq-a1 draft #40 #41 draft — rq-a1 result. production `hkjc.model` untouched (imported/reused only). all work is in
`src/hkjc/statespace/` + `studies/` + a test. the gate decides, not the pilot's t-stat. orchestrator
serializes any model_state update; `a` is not promoted into the production win model.

## what was built (stage-1 items 1–3, the architecture's first end-to-end loop)
the first end-to-end pass of the canonical generative state-space: identify the #41 opening-ramp
latent `a` from the sectional-profile surface → couple it into the start-phase drift with
gate-calibrated strength → gate on the pool-book market skill%. concretely:

1. **theta_builder — real strictly-prior θ over the production panels** (`statespace/assembly.py`).
   `make_production_pre_fit` runs the production `fit_predict_traffic` once per fold (population fit
   train-only, every ability channel strictly-prior) and stamps its `v_c_eb`/`w_prime_eb` onto the
   test frame; `production_theta_builder` reads those as the runner's v_c/w′. the acceleration latent
   `a` is the horse's strictly-prior trailing mean of `estimate_run_profile`'s opening ramp
   (`a=v_1/v_cruise`), expanding/shifted-by-one (the #41/0040 recipe; `attach_trailing_a`). 90.9% st /
   95.4% hv runner coverage; median trailing `a` ≈ 0.88/0.90.
2. **`a` → start-phase drift coupling** (`statespace/coupling.py`). `μ_i *= (1 − a_start_gain ·
   start_frac · ā_centred)`, `start_frac = min(1, l_ref/l)` sourced from production `gate_break_lref`
   (1200m — sprint-biased per §3e phase 1), `ā_centred` within-race-centred. a faster opener (higher
   `a`) ⇒ reaches cruise sooner ⇒ shorter effective time. `a_start_gain` is the single new knob.
3. **the generative core now reproduces the production wald law byte-for-byte** (`generative.py`):
   `_drift_times`/`_effective_length`/`_diffusion_shape` port the production μ/λ assembly (bend
   ground-loss draw, gate-break→effective-l, draw→d / figure-spread→d / gate-break→d variance knobs,
   surface diffusion) sourced from `hkjc.model.constants`. same race-id seed, same n_samples, same
   laplace smoothing.
4. **gate harness** (`statespace/gate.py` `calibrate_coupling` + `studies/statespace_a_gate.py`):
   exact %-of-market (`(uniform−model)/(uniform−market)`) + ece, paired fixed-seed
   (pythonhashseed=0) full walk-forward, both venues, st broken out by distance band.

## (1) acceptance gate a — the generative core is faithful (byte-exact)
with `a_start_gain=0`, the state-space pipeline reproduces production `fit_predict_traffic`:

  st: max|δp| = 0.00e+00 over 4704 test runners   → faithful (byte-exact)
  hv: max|δp| = 0.00e+00 over 2871 test runners   → faithful (byte-exact)

(one diagnosis on the way: the hv 1650m surface heuristic — production treats all 1650m as awt by
distance, independent of venue. mirroring `_surface` exactly closed an initial hv max|δp|=0.16 on
1650m races and lifted the hv a=off baseline to the expected ~60%.) the generative core is the
production win model before `a` is added — the architecture's first acceptance is met on both venues.

## (2) the gate — a=off vs best `a_start_gain` (full paired walk-forward, %market | ece)
                a=off        best non-zero gain         verdict
  st      65.22% | 0.0036    65.36% | 0.0041 (g=.075)  %↑ +0.14%, ece worse +0.0004
  hv      60.08% | 0.0016    60.08% | 0.0026 (g=.05)   %↑ +0.00%, ece worse +0.0010

  st grid: g=.025 +0.08%, g=.05 +0.11%, g=.075 +0.14%, g=.1 +0.11%, g=.2 −0.17%, g=.4 −1.95%
           — every nonzero gain raises ece; %market peaks ~+0.14% then decays.
  hv grid: g=.05 +0.00%, g=.1 −0.16%, g=.2 −0.63%, g=.4 −2.69% — no %market lift at any gain.

  st distance-band breakout (a=off vs g=.075), the #41/0040 sprint prediction:
    sprint   69.35% → 69.83%   δ%market +0.48%   (ece 0.0040 → 0.0054)
    mile     65.38% → 65.07%   δ%market −0.31%
    middle   54.53% → 54.89%   δ%market +0.35%

## (3) verdict — does acceleration convert on the market gate?
**the lift loads on sprints exactly as #41/0040 predicted** (+0.48–0.58% sprint vs −0.31% mile), and
the directional win-order signal is real and monotone in the small-gain regime — the identify→couple
chain transmits the right mechanism. but the magnitude is tiny (+0.14% overall %market at best) and
the cost is calibration: **ece is strictly worse at every nonzero gain, both venues.** the start-phase
order-statistic nudge from `a` does not survive the pool-book gate as a net win.

this is the #40 lesson landing for real: the path-honest latent (profile-fit +22–30% held-out,
t=+9.98 st-sprint win-relevance) does not convert at the win order-statistic — and unlike a t-stat,
the paired %market+ece gate is unforgiving. the pilot's δr² over-stated the win value (as warned).

## (4) promote / don't — and what stage-1.5 inherits
**don't promote `a` via the start-phase drift channel.** decision rule (best non-zero gain must beat
a=off on both %market and ece) fails on both venues — %market gain is sub-noise and ece always worse.
the generative core, the leak-free seam, and the gate harness are kept (proven, reusable).

also tested — the **`a` → d variance channel** (`a_d_gain`, the parallel coupling the drift-vs-
calibration symptom pointed to: a troubled opener injects start-phase variance → larger d). it also
fails: st grid g=.1 −0.01%, g=.2 −0.04%, g=.4 −0.08%, g=.8 −0.25% %market, no ece benefit at any gain.
so `a` does not convert via the drift or the variance channel.

stage-1.5 candidates, in priority order from this evidence:
  - **sprint-only drift coupling** — the only positive signal is the sprint band (+0.48–0.58%); a
    band-gated `a_start_gain` (zero outside sprints) avoids the mile regression and is the last
    plausible net-convert for `a`. if even that doesn't beat a=off on %market and ece within sprints,
    shelve `a` for the win pool (it remains validated for profile fit / margins — the stage-2 surface).
  - **move on to a richer gate (stage 2 — margins + pool book).** the win order-statistic is, as #40
    warned, too coarse to reward a start-phase latent; `a` may convert against the margin/pool-book
    objective (where the opening split actually shows up) rather than the win bit. this is the more
    promising direction than further tuning `a`→win.
  - **fold `a` into the eb hierarchy proper** (band×rating random effect; stage-1 item 4) — the clean
    home if `a` is revisited, but unlikely to change the win-gate verdict on its own.
  - **ρ stays population-fixed** (stage-1 scope); per-horse ρ remains a stage-3 cv target.

## (5) leak-free confirmation
`assert_no_lookahead` on `build_fit_predict` (a_start_gain=0.2, real folds, both venues): drift
**0.00e+00**. θ is strictly-prior (trailing `a` shifted-by-one; v_c/w′ from the production strictly-
prior eb); population fit train-only per fold (inside the reused `fit_predict_traffic`); the sampler
is a pure function of (θ, conditions) + race-id seed. the numbers are paired fixed-seed (pythonhashseed=0),
full-scale walk-forward — not the ~4×-overstating quick_eval. `tests/test_statespace_skeleton.py` 7/7
green (incl. the new a-off==production-wald acceptance unit test); `ruff` clean; full suite 155 passed.

title: "Stage-2 / RQ-pool (statespace): the POOL-BOOK gate is built (WIN/PLA/QIN/FCT/TCE/TRI, de-vigged on the realized combination) — and `a` does NOT convert on the ordering pools either. The reformulation's central wager FAILS its decisive probe: `a` HURTS QIN/FCT monotonically, worst in the sprint band where it lives (sprint QIN −1.01%, FCT −0.86% at g=.075). `a` lifts only WIN. An honest, important negative."
