summary: DRAFT — RQ-pool result. Production `hkjc.model` UNTOUCHED (imported/reused only). All work is in `src/hkjc/statespace/` (pricer + gate) + `studies/` + a test. Dividends are realized post-race outcomes…
text:
"stage-2 / rq-pool (statespace): the pool-book gate is built (win/pla/qin/fct/tce/tri, de-vigged on the realized combination) — and `a` does not convert on the ordering pools either. the reformulation's central wager fails its decisive probe: `a` hurts qin/fct monotonically, worst in the sprint band where it lives (sprint qin −1.01%, fct −0.86% at g=.075). `a` lifts only win. an honest, important negative." statespace generative state-space acceleration pool-book pool-gate forecast quinella trifecta tierce place de-vig devig pct-of-market order-distribution ordering-pools leak-free stage-2 rq-pool negative-result draft #40 #41 0042 draft — rq-pool result. production `hkjc.model` untouched (imported/reused only). all work is in
`src/hkjc/statespace/` (pricer + gate) + `studies/` + a test. dividends are realized post-race
outcomes used only for scoring, never fitting. `a` is not promoted into any pool model.

## the decisive test
rq-a1 (journal 0042) found acceleration `a` does not convert on the win order-statistic (+0.14%
%market overall, ece strictly worse) — the win bit could not reward a latent that shapes the order
but not the winner (`a` = a fast opener that leads early, shapes the order, but cruises lower so does
not win more). the reformulation's central wager was that the broader pool book — the ordering pools
(forecast/quinella) that read the orderings and separations win discards — rewards latents win cannot.
this entry builds that gate and runs `a`'s decisive probe on it.

## what was built (the pool-book gate)
1. **poolpricer — realized-combination probabilities** (`statespace/pricer.py`). from the one joint
   `orderdistribution` mc sample (the object every pool price is a functional of), the model's
   laplace-smoothed probability of each race's realized winning combination, per pool: `prob_win`
   (p 1st), `prob_place` / `place(k)` (top-k, k per hkjc `places_paid`: 3 for field≥7 else 2),
   `prob_quinella` ({i,j}=top-2 unordered), `prob_forecast` ((i,j)=top-2 ordered), `prob_tierce`
   ((i,j,k)=top-3 ordered = tce), `prob_trio` ({i,j,k}=top-3 unordered = tri). all laplace-smoothed
   `(hits+1)/(n_samples+n)` so a zero-sample combo never gives infinite log-loss. consistency proven
   (quinella = fc(i,j)+fc(j,i); tierce ⊆ trio; trio = place-set for k=3) — they are marginals of one law.
2. **de-vigged market benchmark** (`studies/statespace_poolbook_gate.py`). the dividend's `decimal` on
   the realized combination → market implied prob = (1 − takeout)/decimal, takeout per pool imported
   from `hkjc.core.hkjc_facts.takeout_for` (win/pla/qin 17.5%, fct/tce 20.5%, tri 25%). pla scored
   per-leg (each realized placer is its own "horse i in top-k" event priced by its own place dividend;
   the set-as-product over-counts via spurious independence — leg-by-leg is the clean anchor).
3. **per-pool skill metric — `gate.pool_book_score`**. per pool: mean per-race model / market / uniform
   log-loss on the realized combination and the exact `%market = (uniform_ll − model_ll)/(uniform_ll −
   market_ll)` — exactly the win %market definition, but on the exotic combination. uniform baseline =
   p(realized combo | uniform random order): win 1/n, pla k/n (per-leg), qin 1/c(n,2), fct 1/(n(n−1)),
   tce 1/(n(n−1)(n−2)), tri 1/c(n,3).
4. **coverage.** st dividends only (no `dividends_hv.parquet` — st has the strongest sprint-`a` signal).
   170 st races (2026-03-01..05-31), all six pools on all 170 (169 after field/combo validity). the
   model frame is the full 1952-race leak-free `backtest_st.load()`; the gate scores the 170-race
   dividend subset. bands: sprint n=76, mile n=71, middle n=20 (the middle cell is small/noisy).

## (1) the gate table — a=off vs the rq-a1 `a_start_gain` grid, per pool (st, %market | model_ll)
paired fixed-seed (pythonhashseed=0), full-scale, n_samples=20000. per-race seed shared a-off/a-on.

  pool   n    a=off      g=.05      g=.075     g=.1       g=.2       δ(best≠0 vs off)
  win   169  74.14%     74.65%     74.80%     74.97%     75.53%     +1.39% (g=.2)   ↑ converts
  pla   170  75.63%     75.24%     75.01%     74.80%     73.66%     −1.97%          ↓ hurts (monotone)
  qin   169  67.91%     67.66%     67.44%     67.28%     66.33%     −1.58%          ↓ hurts (monotone)
  fct   169  70.50%     70.06%     69.92%     69.72%     68.65%     −1.85%          ↓ hurts (monotone)
  tce   169  70.15%     70.13%     69.84%     70.17%     68.42%     ~0 / −1.74%     ↓ (soft, noisy)
  tri   169  79.21%     78.91%     78.44%     78.31%     77.24%     −1.97%          ↓ hurts (soft)

  best non-zero gain per pool: win g=.2 (+1.39%); pla/qin/fct/tri best = a=off (every gain hurts);
  tce best g=.1 (+0.02%, pure mc noise). only win improves; every ordering/set pool degrades monotonically.

## (2) the sprint band — the #41/0040 prediction, the decisive cell (a=off vs forced g=.075)
`a` lives in the sprint (start_frac = min(1, l_ref/l), l_ref≈1200m). rq-a1's only win lift was the
sprint band (+0.48% sprint %market). the wager: that sprint lift should be bigger on the ordering pools.
it is the opposite sign:

  qin  sprint(76)  73.62% → 72.61%   δ −1.01%      mile(71) −0.19%   middle(20) +0.56%
  fct  sprint(76)  73.54% → 72.68%   δ −0.86%      mile(71) −0.46%   middle(20) +0.08%

the ordering pools lose the most in the exact band where `a` produced its only win lift. (the middle
+0.56%/+0.08% is n=20, inside the mc/soft-pool noise band.)

## (3) the verdict — does `a` convert on the ordering pools where it failed on win?
**no.** the reformulation's central wager fails its decisive probe. `a` does not merely fail to convert
on the ordering pools — it actively hurts them, monotonically in the gain, worst in the sprint band
where the mechanism is strongest. the only pool `a` lifts is win (+1.4% at g=.2 here vs +0.14% in
rq-a1's full-scale win gate — the larger figure is the 170-race march–may subsample, not the full
walk-forward, so it overstates; the sign, win-only-positive, is what matters).

why this is coherent, not a bug: the win marginal is the one pool where seeding the front of the order
helps (a faster opener wins the close-finish tie a touch more often). the qin/fct/tri combinations are
dominated by the same minor-placing reshuffles that hurt rq-a1's calibration — `a` redistributes mass
in the body of the order (exactly the top-2/top-3 region these pools price), and that redistribution is
net wrong against the realized orderings. the richer validation surface does not reward the
path-identified `a`; it penalises it more sharply than win did. an honest, important negative.

## (4) what this implies for the program
- **`a` via the start-phase drift coupling is refuted on the whole pool book, not just win.** it is now
  don't-promote on win (0042) and don't-promote on pla/qin/fct/tce/tri (here). the drift channel is
  exhausted for `a`. (the d-variance channel also failed on win in 0042; not re-run per-pool — the
  drift-channel pool-book sign is decisive enough.) `a` remains validated for profile fit / the stage-2
  margin surface (#40/#41) — but it does not earn a place in the price of any pool we can de-vig.
- **the wager itself is the lesson.** the hypothesis "the order book rewards what win discards" is
  falsified for this latent through this coupling: the ordering pools are not a softer judge that
  rewards path-honest order structure — they are a harder one (they penalise the same minor-placing
  error win only diluted). this tempers the program's optimism about the pool book as a rescue surface
  for win-invisible latents. it does not refute the pool-book gate as infrastructure — that is built,
  leak-free, and reusable, and is the right stage-2 judge.
- **proceed, but recalibrated.** the gate is the deliverable; the next latents (ρ recovery → place/qin
  margins per §4 rq-pool-place; a control/ground-saved latent → hv pool book per §3) should be tested
  on it — but with the prior that a latent must improve the sharp anchors (win/pla) to be a net win;
  "it'll convert on the exotics" is now an evidenced-against escape hatch. recommend: do not spend more
  on `a`→win/pool; move to a latent that moves margins (w′/ρ), which the place/quinella body actually
  prices, and gate it here. ρ stays population-fixed (stage-1 scope); per-horse ρ a stage-3 cv target.

## (5) leak-free + de-vig caveats
- **leak-free.** the order distribution is the leak-free model (θ strictly-prior: production `v_c_eb`/
  `w_prime_eb` from the train-only eb fit per fold; trailing `a` shifted-by-one). dividends are realized
  post-race outcomes used only for scoring, never fitting — the boundary is explicit (the pricer never
  sees a dividend; the gate joins them only to score). `assert_no_lookahead` on the predict path
  (a_start_gain=0.2): drift **0.00e+00**. paired fixed-seed full-scale (pythonhashseed=0) — not the
  ~4×-overstating quick_eval.
- **de-vig is honest but partial.** the dividend gives only the winning combination's market prob
  ((1−takeout)/decimal); the market's full distribution over all combinations is unobserved. so %market
  here is on the realized combination — a valid but partial benchmark (it tests whether the model puts
  the right mass on what actually happened vs what the market priced it at). stated plainly so it is not
  over-read as a full distributional %market.
- **exotic softness honoured.** win/pla/qin are the sharp anchors (17.5% takeout, liquid); fct/tce
  (20.5%) and tri (25%) are softer, higher-vig, noisier de-vig — flagged `(soft)` and treated as
  confirmatory, not decisive. the verdict rests on the sharp qin + the medium fct, which agree with the
  soft pools and the sprint band: every ordering/set pool says the same thing — `a` hurts.
- tests green (`tests/test_statespace_skeleton.py` 9/9, incl. the new pricer + pool_book_score guards;
  full suite **157 passed**); `ruff` clean. production `hkjc.model` untouched; nothing baked.

title: "Foundation 0044: does the generative path model FIT observed race paths well? — held-out reconstruction is OK-not-good (R²≈0.5, +56–60% over the within-horse noise floor), dominated by a +0.42 m/s SYSTEMATIC LEVEL UNDER-PREDICTION; a flexible descriptive baseline beats it ⇒ the generative FORM is too rigid and must be fixed before latent identification is trustworthy"

summary: DRAFT — PATH-FIT QUALITY ONLY. No market odds, no win gate, no pool book anywhere. Production `hkjc.model` UNTOUCHED (import/reuse). New additive module `hkjc.statespace.pathfit`. The orchestrator ser…
text:
"foundation 0044: does the generative path model fit observed race paths well? — held-out reconstruction is ok-not-good (r²≈0.5, +56–60% over the within-horse noise floor), dominated by a +0.42 m/s systematic level under-prediction; a flexible descriptive baseline beats it ⇒ the generative form is too rigid and must be fixed before latent identification is trustworthy" theory energetics w-prime v_c acceleration phase-structure profile-likelihood sectional path-fit reconstruction calibration noise-floor generative identification foundation draft draft — path-fit quality only. no market odds, no win gate, no pool book anywhere. production
`hkjc.model` untouched (import/reuse). new additive module `hkjc.statespace.pathfit`. the
orchestrator serializes any model_state change / generative-form fix.

## the question (the foundation before any gate)
the reformulation (theory §iii/§iv) rests on the claim that the generative w′-balance + first-passage
path model reproduces real k-section velocity profiles, from which θ=(v_c, w′_0, a, ρ) are identified.
before trusting any downstream identification we must establish the foundation: **does
`expected_profile(θ, conditions)` actually fit observed race paths well, in absolute terms?** this is a
pure held-out predictive path-fit. the pilot 0040 only showed the 4-latent profile beats a scalar
heuristic by 22–30%; that is a relative win. this entry asks the absolute + structural question.

## construction (leak-free, additive)
`hkjc.statespace.pathfit` + `studies/pathfit_foundation.py`. 39,256 runs (st 24,099 / hv 14,416 with
≥1 other run), n_sec≥3.
- **held-out θ:** leave-one-race-out per horse — the held-out run's predicted (v_c, w′_0, a) is the mean
  of that horse's other runs only (own run subtracted out). `assert_path_no_lookahead` drift **0.00**
  both venues (the prediction is algebraically independent of the held-out run's own θ/outcome).
- **noise floor:** the within-(horse, n_sec, section) race-to-race velocity std (ddof=1, ≥2 runs,
  pooled) — the best any model conditioned on horse identity could do; the part no θ can remove.
- **descriptive baseline (question 4):** a flexible physics-free per-(band, going, n_sec, section) mean
  velocity-ratio shape × the horse's strictly-prior loo cruise level. shape fit train-only (date split
  at the 70th pct); held-out level strictly-prior. the yardstick for "is the physics too rigid".

## results (held-out, m/s + normalized)

### (1) absolute reconstruction — ok, not good; far from the floor
| venue | gen rmse | gen r² | a:=1 rmse | descriptive rmse | noise floor | gen excess over floor |
|-------|----------|--------|-----------|------------------|-------------|-----------------------|
| st    | 0.841    | +0.49  | 1.204     | 0.681            | 0.539       | **+56%**              |
| hv    | 0.652    | +0.46  | 0.846     | 0.553            | 0.408       | **+60%**              |
the generative model explains ~half the section-velocity variance and beats the no-accel ablation
clearly (a is real and load-bearing — confirms 0040). but it sits **56–60% above the irreducible
floor**, and **a flexible descriptive baseline is markedly closer** (st excess +26%, hv +36%). the
physics is leaving large, structured, removable error on the table.

### (2) calibration — over-dispersed (predicted bands too wide)
pit mean **0.62** (ideal 0.50 — the positive shift is the level bias below), pit std **0.23 st / 0.19
hv** (ideal 0.289) ⇒ **over-dispersed**: the σ=0.06 log-velocity band is too wide, 68% band covers
0.78 st / 0.89 hv (>0.68), 90% band covers 0.94/0.98. the predictive distribution is not calibrated —
but this is secondary to the mean bias (a mis-centred, too-wide band).

### (3) residual structure — a systematic level under-prediction + an opening miss
mean residual `v_obs − v_gen` is **positive everywhere** (+0.39 to +0.49 m/s) — the generator
systematically runs the whole path too slow. this is **structural, not loo shrinkage**: with the run's
own in-sample θ the bias is still +0.36 m/s (gen mean profile 14.8/16.9/16.7/16.5 vs observed
15.2/17.5/17.0/16.7). decomposition (st): of the 0.841 rmse, removing the global +0.42 bias drops it to
**0.73** — the level bias alone is ~⅓ of the squared error.
- **by phase** (st mean_res / floor): opening **+0.49** (floor 0.64, de-biased rmse 0.94 — still the
  worst), cruise **+0.47** (floor 0.44, de-biased 0.59 — near floor once centred), closing **+0.19**
  (floor 0.58). the cruise shape is actually good after de-biasing; the opening is genuinely mis-fit
  even after `a`; the whole curve is shifted down.
- **by distance:** sprint is the failure — st sprint rmse **1.03, r²=+0.06, mean_res +0.74**; middle/
  staying fit well (r² 0.73/0.33). hv sprint mean_res +0.51. the start transient is a large fraction of
  a sprint and `a` (a single opening ratio) under-captures it.
- **by going:** flat (rmse 0.83–0.86 across good/firm/soft) — going is not a path-fit driver here.
- **by run-style:** flat (front/mid/closer within ~0.01 rmse) — the single-horse model misses the
  pace-game equally across styles (no style-specific signal because there is no rival coupling at all).
- **by pace:** st closing residual is +0.10 m/s worse in fast-pace races (fast +0.23 vs slow +0.13) —
  a real pace-dependent miss the single-horse generator cannot see (the §iii.4 pace game); weak at hv.
- **by field size:** flat.

### (4) generative adequacy — the physics pays a real price (it is too rigid)
the flexible descriptive baseline beats the physics generator at both venues by a wide margin
(st 0.681 vs 0.841; hv 0.553 vs 0.652) — closing ~half the gap to the floor that the physics leaves
open. a small gap would say the generative structure is adequate; this gap is large. the generative form
is over-constraining the profile shape (the linear-ramp w′-spend that pins the closing section to v_c
and the single opening ratio) in a way a memorised mean shape does not.

## diagnosis → what must be fixed in the generative form (before identification is trustworthy)
1. **the level under-prediction is the dominant defect and a form bug, not a fit bug.** `expected_profile`
   anchors the non-opening profile at `v_c·(1 + w′/l·w)` with a linear ramp `w` that forces the final
   section to exactly v_c (w→0). but observed late velocity sits above the recovered v_c, and the cruise
   sections carry more boost than the linear ramp allocates ⇒ the mean profile is shifted down ~0.4 m/s.
   the w′-boost distribution (the §iii.2 spend kinetics) and/or the v_c anchor (the exhaustion criterion
   pinning terminal reserve to 0) is mis-specified. **this must be corrected before any latent recovered
   through this generator is trusted** — a biased generator biases the identified θ.
2. **the opening phase is genuinely under-modelled** (worst de-biased rmse, r²≈0 in sprints). `a` as a
   single scalar ratio captures the level of the ramp but not its shape; the start transient implies a
   richer acceleration latent (a ramp rate / time-constant), per theory §iii.3 phase 1.
3. **the pace-dependent closing miss is the fingerprint of the missing interaction mechanism** (§iii.4):
   a single-horse generator has no representation of the field's pace, so it cannot fit a fast-pace
   closing fade — this is real, measured here (+0.10 m/s), and is exactly the interacting-pl / mean-field
   pace coupling the theory defers. closing mis-fit ⇒ reserve/recovery (ρ) + pace coupling.
4. **calibration (σ, the per-horse d_i) is secondary** — fix the mean first; the band is too wide and
   mis-centred, re-fit σ and make it phase-dependent (opening band ≠ cruise band) once the mean is right.

## verdict
**the generative model is not a good path model yet.** it is directionally right (r²≈0.5, beats the
no-`a` ablation, cruise shape near-floor after de-biasing) but it (a) carries a **+0.42 m/s systematic
level under-prediction** that is a generative-form bug, (b) is **over-dispersed**, and (c) **loses to a
flexible descriptive baseline** — the physics is too rigid. latent identification through this generator
is not yet trustworthy because a biased generator biases θ. **fix order: (1) the w′-spend / v_c-anchor
level bias [must], (2) the opening-ramp shape [sprint failure], (3) phase-dependent σ, (4) then the
pace interaction.** only after the level bias is removed and the gap to the descriptive baseline closes
should profile-identified latents be promoted into the §v coupling/gate program.

don't-bake. diagnostic foundation only; no production change. plots in studies/out/pathfit_*.png.

a-off==production acceptance gate still green.

## the defect (from 0044)
`expected_profile` ran the whole velocity path +0.42 m/s too slow everywhere — a structural level
bias present even with the run's own in-sample θ (so it is the forward model, not θ recovery). the
generator lost to a physics-free flexible descriptive baseline (st 0.841 vs 0.681; hv 0.652 vs
0.553). a biased generator biases every latent identified through it → blocks the program.

## diagnosis (confirmed: root cause (a) and (b), one unified mechanism)
instrumented `expected_profile` on 16,092 st/hv 4-section runs with each run's own θ. per-section
mean (in-sample, isolates the forward model):

| sec | obs | gen(old) | obs−gen | gen−v_c |
|-----|-----|----------|---------|---------|
| 1 (open)  | 15.18 | 14.82 | +0.355 | −1.673 |
| 2 (cruise)| 17.52 | 16.95 | +0.571 | +0.457 |
| 3 (cruise)| 16.99 | 16.72 | +0.264 | +0.229 |
| 4 (close) | 16.75 | 16.49 | +0.257 | **+0.000** |

two compounding bugs, both flavours of the 0044 hypothesis:
- **(b) the close pinned to bare v_c.** the linear ramp `w=(k−1−idx)` forces the final weight to
  exactly 0 ⇒ gen closing = v_c precisely. but observed runs the close +0.257 above v_c (the horse
  fades toward v_c, it does not arrive at it). a clean v_c-as-close mis-centering.
- **(a) the boost magnitude was scale-collapsed.** the old form used
  `boost_frac = w′_0/dist_total` (full trip, incl. the opening) and the linear ramp halved the
  realized lift. net: the generated time-weighted mean fell below v_c (16.33 < v_c 16.49,
  n_sec=4), while the observed non-opening mean sits +0.55 m/s (≈+3.5% of v_c) above v_c across all
  n_sec (3/4/5/6: +0.561/+0.576/+0.527/+0.468).

the reconciliation that fixes it: `w′_0 = σ(v−v_c)^+·t` is reserve-distance (the extra metres run
above the ceiling), spent over the non-opening trip (the opening is the `a` start transient, not
the reserve). then the time-weighted non-opening lift is exactly `v_c·(w′_0/l_nonopening)` —
measured `w′_0/l_nonop = 0.0354` vs observed boost frac `0.0354` (1e-3 agreement). the observed
per-section excess over v_c decays geometrically (~halving: 0.063 → 0.031 → 0.015 of v_c) — the
reserve depletes multiplicatively and the close stays above v_c.

## the fix (faithful mechanism, not a fudge constant)
re-specified the non-opening spend in `expected_profile`:
1. **budget over the non-opening trip:** `boost_frac = w′_0 / l_nonopening` (was `/dist_total`).
   this is the conserved reserve-distance per non-opening metre — the theory §iii.2 hill lift
   `v_eff = v_c·(1+w′/l)` applied to the phase the reserve actually governs.
2. **geometric spend share** `g_j = q^j` (q=0.5: each non-opening section ~half the previous
   boost), normalised to time-weighted mean 1 over the non-opening sections so the realized lift
   equals the conserved budget. the close carries `g_last > 0` — it is never pinned to bare v_c.
3. opening override `v_1 = a·cruise` unchanged. k=1 fallback: lift over its own distance.
reserve stays non-negative; the budget is conserved (the time-weighted lift integral = w′_0/l).
`q=0.5` matches the observed geometric decay; verified de-biasing holds for n_sec=3/4/5/6
(in-sample overall bias +0.058/+0.016/+0.003/−0.022, vs +0.36 before).

## re-measured path-fit (held-out, leak-free; loo θ, leak drift 0.00 both venues)

| metric | st before | st after | hv before | hv after |
|--------|-----------|----------|-----------|----------|
| gen rmse (m/s)        | 0.841 | **0.673** | 0.652 | **0.521** |
| gen r²                | +0.49 | **+0.68** | +0.46 | **+0.65** |
| excess over floor     | +56%  | **+25%**  | +60%  | **+28%**  |
| descriptive rmse      | 0.681 | 0.681     | 0.553 | 0.553     |
| **gen vs descr**      | loses | **wins**  | loses | **wins**  |
| pit mean (ideal .500) | 0.625 | **0.498** | 0.608 | **0.494** |
| pit std (ideal .289)  | 0.226 | 0.218     | 0.189 | 0.177     |
| mean residual (m/s)   | +0.42 | **+0.02** | +0.31 | **−0.02** |

per-phase mean residual collapsed to ~0 (st opening +0.49→+0.07, cruise +0.47→+0.04, close
+0.19→−0.15; hv similarly). the a:=1 ablation got worse (st 1.20→1.33) — `a` is even more
load-bearing once the level is right (confirms #41). noise floor unchanged (0.539 st / 0.408 hv).

## did it clear the bar? — yes.
stage-0 exit = **bias ≈ 0 and the gap to the descriptive baseline closed**. both met:
- bias: +0.42 → +0.02 (st), +0.31 → −0.02 (hv) — essentially eliminated.
- gap: the physics generator now **beats** the flexible physics-free baseline at both venues
  (st 0.673<0.681; hv 0.521<0.553), and sits closer to the floor than descriptive (st gen excess
  +0.134 < descr +0.142; hv +0.113 < descr +0.145). the physics no longer pays a price for being
  physics — it is now the better path model. pit re-centred to 0.50.

## residual defects now dominant (clean targets for the next agent — not touched here)
with the level fixed, the structured residual is exactly what 0044 predicted would remain:
1. **opening ramp shape** — still the worst phase (st opening de-biased rmse 0.84 vs floor 0.64;
   sprint r² +0.57 now but opening still carries the largest excess). `a` as a single scalar
   captures the ramp level not its shape → the §iii.3 phase-1 acceleration latent (ramp rate /
   time-constant). sprint mean_res is now the only band materially off (st +0.16).
2. **pace-dependent closing miss** — now more visible (the level bias was masking it): closing
   residual is −0.11 m/s worse in fast-pace races (st), −0.20 (hv). this is the §iii.4 mean-field
   pace coupling a single-horse generator structurally cannot see. the closing now slightly
   over-predicts (mean_res −0.15 st) — the geometric q may want to be phase/pace-conditioned.
3. **σ over-dispersion** — band still too wide (pit std 0.218/0.177 vs ideal 0.289; 68% coverage
   0.86/0.94). now that the mean is centred, re-fit σ (and make it phase-dependent: opening band ≠
   cruise band) — secondary, mechanical.
4. **staying** (n_sec≥6, thin n) shows a residual per-section wave (cruise over-, close under-boost)
   — the single global q=0.5 is slightly off for long races; a mild n_sec-dependence or the
   true balance-path spend would refine it. low priority (228/804 runs).

fix order for the program is now: (1) [done] level bias; (2) opening-ramp shape; (3) phase-dep σ;
(4) the pace interaction. only after these should profile-identified latents promote into the §v
coupling/gate program.

## discipline
leak-free held-out throughout (loo θ, drift 0.00). the +0.42 diagnosis used in-sample θ to isolate
the forward model (correct); the final numbers above are the held-out ones. full pytest suite
158/158 green, incl. `test_a_off_reproduces_production_wald` (byte-exact statespace acceptance) and
`test_coupling_a_off_matches_bare_law` — the fix is in the profile-likelihood forward model only and
does not perturb the production wald win law. `estimate_run_profile`/`profile_loglik` θ-recovery
unchanged (they call the fixed `expected_profile`; the recovery of v_c/w′_0/a is untouched). lint
clean. don't-bake — diagnostic foundation; no production constant changed. plots in
studies/out/pathfit_*.png.

Primary metric = path-fit + re-emergence; win% checked LAST, expected to fall then recover fundamentally. Authoritative design: docs/CAUSAL_MODEL.md."

text:
"causal rebuild design (owner-directed): re-ground the win model cause-not-effect — strip all meta-signals (form/jockey/trainer/collateral/peak-gap/speed-fig are effects of the causes), drive the model from physiology/control/prep causes inferred from the path, validate by the meta-signals re-emerging as consequences. primary metric = path-fit + re-emergence; win% checked last, expected to fall then recover fundamentally. authoritative design: docs/causal_model.md." causal causal-rebuild cause-not-effect confound meta-signals strip re-emergence form jockey trainer collateral peak-gap speed-figure ability-latent v_c control prep crossed-effects cross-classified random-effects path-likelihood identifiability lateral cv statespace generative first-passage pure-mechanism first-build gof-fall validation staging design draft 0037 0039 0040 0044 queue-50 design + docs only. no inference built. production `hkjc.model` (65/60% of market) untouched and
stays the deployable fallback. `energetics_dynamic.py` not modified (#50 edits it concurrently). no
market odds in the near-term stages. the deliverable is the authoritative design `docs/causal_model.md`
plus the reframed theory/statespace_design and design-surface stubs.

## the principle (owner's directive)
the current model confounds cause and effect. form/jockey/trainer/collateral/peak-gap/speed-fig are
not mechanisms — they are downstream consequences of the true causes. form is high because ability is
high (a noisy past-measurement of `v_c`); the jockey signal exists because the rider exerts better
control; collateral = ability via opponents; peak-gap = ability's career trajectory. feeding these as
features makes the model circular ("winners win again") — it fits well because it is tautological.
the rebuild: decouple all meta-signals, build on the mechanistic causes only, infer them from the
path, and validate by the meta-signals re-emerging as consequences. short-term gof falls sharply; that
is accepted (research model only; production stays live). the empirical proof the meta-signals are
effects of one cause is already in hand: `0037` (form/figure/collateral/sectional = one over-measured
ability latent, pc1≈25%, 5/5 retrodiction) + `0039` (the additive gains are gate-calibrated couplings
~7× the honest slope, not honest measurements).

## the causal dag (docs/causal_model.md §1)
causes → both the path/outcome and the meta-signals (two arrows out of every cause):
  - latent causes: physiology (v_c, w'_0, a, rho, d_i, mass), jockey control (c_lat lateral / c_pol
    policy), trainer prep (fitness/trajectory), environment (geometry, going, draw, field pace).
  - cause → the path (longitudinal v(t) now; + lateral y(t) via cv) → finishing order (argmin first-
    passage — the validated §iii physics, preserved as the generative core).
  - cause → past paths → the meta-signals (ability → past paths → form/figure/collateral/peak-gap;
    control → positioning → jockey-sr; prep → readiness → trainer-hot). the meta-signals are leaves.
identifiability annotation (now vs needs-cv): physiology identifiable from the longitudinal profile
now; trainer-prep partial now; jockey-control fundamentally lateral → weak now, clean split needs cv
(#34); pace/mfg coupling not identifiable from a single-horse generator (deferred).

## the strip list + re-derivation (docs/causal_model.md §2)
- ability-effects → strip, re-emerge from ability `v_c`/`w'_0`: recency_form/form, speed_figure,
  collateral_form[_v2], rating_trajectory peak-gap, finishing_sectional_vc, trajectory fade (→w'),
  barrier_trial/trial_vc, gallop_vc. these are noisy past-measurements of one latent (0037 pc1) —
  the model infers `v_c`/`w'` from the path; form/figure/collateral become predicted consequences.
- control-effects → re-derive causally: jockey_table → a crossed jockey random effect on the path
  (coarse now, fully causal with cv `c_lat` at stage 3); early_pos/style → split (pace shadow stays on
  w', positioning → control latent); gate_break → drop (0037: it is early_pos, r²=0.998; the kinematic
  `a` capacity cause replaces it).
- prep-effects → re-derive: trainer/trainer_hot → a crossed trainer×time random effect (coarse now,
  no new data).
- not stripped (genuine causes/env): rating (only as debut/thin-horse population prior — tension t1),
  draw, going, geometry, allometric mass (v_c ∝ m^(b-1)), field size.

## the inference — separate ability / control / prep (docs/causal_model.md §3)
all three shape the same path. decouple via a cross-classified (crossed random-effects) hierarchy over
the path likelihood: log v_obs = θ_horse·b_phys + u_jockey·b_ctrl + w_trainer·b_prep + env + ε, with
the (horse, jockey, trainer) crossings in the data separating the effects. generalizes the existing eb
hierarchy (calibration.fit_energetics_population, band×rating + horse re) to add jockey + trainer
groupings. the meta-signals never appear; the latent effects are inferred from the path + crossings.
honest identifiability map:
  - now (longitudinal): horse physiology strong (0040/0044); trainer-prep partial (dense crossings).
  - weak now / needs cv: jockey-control is fundamentally lateral (positioning/ground-saved invisible to
    v(t)), confounded longitudinally with v_c → coarse upper bound only; clean c_lat/c_pol split is
    cv-only (#34, stage 3). state "control only partially identified until cv" in every stage-1/2 result.
  - not identifiable: pace/mfg (single-horse generator has no field; 0044's +0.10 m/s fast-pace closing
    residual is the fingerprint).
  - thin-crossing risk: where horse×jockey×trainer is thin the three effects are aliased — shrink hard /
    report combined; quantify crossing density as an entry diagnostic.
why the path (not win) makes this honest: 0039 proved win can't identify the coupling honestly; the
path is a denser likelihood, so the wager is it recovers the tail-relevant ability shape the win-bit
fusion discarded. if path-inferred ability under-predicts winning, that is the measured gof fall we
accept and close by adding causal structure — never by re-feeding the meta-signal.

## re-emergence validation suite — the falsifiable test (docs/causal_model.md §4)
for each stripped signal: infer the latent from the path only → predict the held-out meta-signal from
the latent's consequence arrow → score vs the population baseline (floor) and the signal's own trailing
mean (ceiling). per-signal metrics: form (ability → rank corr of held-out rel-finish), speed-fig (rmse/
r²), collateral (reproduce massey from inferred field abilities), peak-gap (ability trajectory → corr +
sign), jockey-sr (jockey re → corr/rank), trainer-hot (prep trajectory → corr/lead-lag). the decisive
joint test (§4.3): reproduce the form→result relationship without form as input — bin runners by observed
form, does the causal model's win prob (form stripped) track the empirical win-rate-by-form curve? a
signal that re-emerges ⇒ mechanism captured; one that fails ⇒ a precise pointer to a missing mechanism
(form fails → path not identifying full ability; jockey-sr fails → confirms the cv dependency; collateral
re-emerges but form not → the relational/field-coupling piece is missing). the re-emergence map is the
engine of progress — it names which mechanism to build next.

## the metric + staging (docs/causal_model.md §5)
primary = path-fit quality (0044 harness: held-out rmse vs noise floor + descriptive baseline, pit,
residual structure) + re-emergence score. last = win% (expected to fall sharply on first strip; checked
only to measure the fall and confirm fundamental recovery). this inverts the production %-of-market-first
gate during the rebuild.
  - stage 1 — strip ability-proxies; build physiological causal latents from the longitudinal path;
    test form re-emergence. entry: #50's corrected generator (0044 level bias removed). exit: path-fit ≥
    descriptive baseline + form (and figure/collateral) re-emerge + the win% fall measured+bounded.
  - stage 2 — trainer-prep crossed effect + margins surface + the pace/field interaction. exit: trainer-
    hot re-emerges + margins identify w'/rho + pace coupling reduces the 0044 fast-pace residual + win%
    recovers materially.
  - stage 3 — jockey-control with cv lateral (c_lat/c_pol). exit: jockey-sr re-emerges (the stage-1
    fail-by-design test now passes) + control supersedes the draw shadows + win% recovers to/past
    production, now causal.
gof-fall contract: fall expected (stage 1 large — recency-form alone is +7.8pp; ability stack is most
of production's edge over the ~48% start), recover by stage; never closed by re-feeding a meta-signal.

## the first pure-mechanism build (docs/causal_model.md §6 — dispatch this)
a win model whose drift is set by the path-inferred physiology latents only (v_c, w'_0, a, rho, d, m
from the horse's earlier paths via #50's corrected estimate_run_profile + the calibration eb prior,
horse re only), with every meta-signal feature stripped; rating only as the debut/thin prior. generator
= the production wald first-passage law on #50's bias-corrected form. measured on: (1) path-fit ≥ the
0044 descriptive baseline on #50's generator; (2) form re-emergence (§4.2 + the §4.3 form→result-without-
form curve) — the headline pass/fail; (3) the gof-fall magnitude (paired fixed-seed win gate vs
production, decomposed by which stripped gain carried how much win%) — a measurement not a gate. lives
additively in statespace (a `puremechanismthetabuilder`, contrast assembly.production_theta_builder which
stamps the meta-signal-laden v_c_eb); re-emergence suite = studies/causal_reemergence.py. hard prereq:
#50's corrected generator (a biased generator biases every inferred cause — 0044).

## what this entry shipped (design surface only; no inference)
- docs/causal_model.md — new, authoritative (the dag, strip list, crossed inference + identifiability
  map, re-emergence suite, metric+staging, first build, 5 open tensions).
- docs/theory.md — reframed cause-not-effect (banner + §0 + §ii/§iii intros): the meta-signals are
  effects to re-derive; §iii physics preserved as the cause→path→order generator (now on #50's
  corrected form).
- docs/statespace_design.md — re-pointed to the causal rebuild (banner + the first build work items
  superseding the gate-coupling stage 1, kept as proven infra); causes.py + pathfit.py added to layout.
- src/hkjc/statespace/causes.py — new design stub: latentcauses (crossed physiologycause / controlcause
  / prepcause + env) + infer_crossed_causes (notimplementederror, stage 2/3). likelihood.crossed_term
  stub added. wired into __init__; ruff clean; 10 skeleton tests pass; imports + stubs verified.

## open design tensions (for the owner — docs/causal_model.md §7)
- t1 rating's dual nature: keep as debut/thin prior only, or rule fully exogenous? (both cause + effect).
- t2 the 0039 gof-fall magnitude: the win-calibrated ability gains carried order-statistic tail work; a
  stage-1 model could sit well below production on win% while passing every causal test. accepted per the
  directive — flagging the likely magnitude.
- t3 thin crossings: shrink-to-population+combined, or restrict crossed inference to the dense sub-graph?
  (recommend the latter, separability-diagnostic-gated).
- t4 pace interaction timing: coarse stage-2 field-pace term vs full stage-3 mfg (recommend coarse now).
- t5 #50 dependency: the entire causal inference is blocked on #50's corrected generator (hard prereq).

don't-bake. design only; no production change; no gate run. the first build is dispatched against this
design + #50's fix.

text:
"foundation 0047: the first-principles eom generative core — a power-balance equation of motion solved under the bang–cp–bang optimal policy replaces the heuristic expected_profile; the level bias stays ≈0 and the opening-ramp defect is fixed by mechanism (ode transient, r²≈0.7–0.8 vs ≈0 before), the inferred physical constants are equine-plausible (v_c≈17.2–17.4 m/s, cp≈54 w/kg, w′_0≈225–246 kj), and the physics matches the heuristic on overall rmse (st 0.668 vs 0.673; hv 0.555 vs 0.521) — the remaining defect is the closing fade-hump = the missing field/pace coupling, exactly as predicted" theory energetics eom equation-of-motion power-balance critical-power w-prime bang-cp-bang pontryagin optimal-control v_c cruise-root first-principles physics no-regression path-fit reconstruction level-bias opening-ramp inversion physical-constants noise-floor pace-coupling foundation draft draft — first-principles path-fit core. no market odds, no win gate, no pool book anywhere. new
additive module `hkjc.statespace.dynamics` (no collision with #50's `energetics_dynamic.py`, which
is untouched). production `hkjc.model`, data_cache, bake untouched. no regression: the velocity
path is the solution of an equation of motion; every parameter is a physical constant with units
and bounds; the phases are the pontryagin optimal-control arcs, not fitted phases.

## the directive
replace the fitted/heuristic `expected_profile` (the 0045 linear-then-geometric w′-spend ansatz
with a fitted opening ratio `a`) with proper first-principles physics — laws of motion + energetics
— and re-measure on the #49 pathfit harness. the bar (stage-0 exit): does the physics remove the
level bias and beat/match the descriptive baseline (no longer worse than a physics-free flexible
fit), with the opening-ramp defect resolved by mechanism?

## (1) the eom core — the equations implemented (revives theory §iii.2 / appendix b)
**longitudinal equation of motion (newton, power-balance form).** mass `m`, power `p(t)`, speed `v`:

    m·v·dv/dt = η·p(t) − ½·ρ_air·c_da·v³ − c_rr·m·g·v − f_geom·v          (propulsive − aero − ground − bend)
  ⇔ m·dv/dt   = η·p/v − ½·ρ·c_da·v² − c_rr·m·g − f_geom                  (the force-per-mass form integrated)

this is exactly the deprecated power-balance plant `m·dv/dt = p/v − f_resist`. the **cruise velocity
v_c is the root** (dv/dt=0 at p=cp) of `η·cp = ½ρ·c_da·v_c³ + c_rr·m·g·v_c` — a derived quantity
(monotone cubic, unique positive root by brentq), not a fitted number. cp↔v_c is an exact bijection.

**critical-power energetics (the energy law).** `p ≤ p_max`; the reserve obeys
`dw′/dt = −(p−cp)^+ + (cp−p)^+/τ·(1−w′/w′_0)`, `w′ ≥ 0` (hard-clamped).

**bang–cp–bang optimal policy (generates the phases — pontryagin solution for this class).**
- ramp: p=p_max from the gun (v₀≈4 m/s gate-release lunge) until v reaches the cruise root v_c. an
  ode transient governed by p_max/m vs drag — the physically-correct replacement for the fitted `a`.
  the cruise arc is latched once reached (v_c is a stable equilibrium of the ode under p=cp).
- cruise: p=cp, v held at v_c (the singular arc).
- kick: a terminal p=p_max burn started at the unique distance x_burn that makes w′ hit 0 at the
  line (full extension), solved by bisection inside the integrator. if the ramp+cruise already
  empties the tank, no kick fires and the close fades to bare v_c.

**physical constants (units / bounds / sources).** g=9.81; ρ_air=1.20 kg/m³ (hk climate);
**η=0.25** (gross metabolic→mechanical muscle efficiency, minetti/taylor); **c_rr=0.040** on good
turf (mechanical cost-of-transport coeff, cot≈c_rr·g≈0.39 j/(kg·m) — the galloping mechanical cot;
going→c_rr surcharge map for soft/yielding); **c_da=1.10 m²** at the 500 kg reference, frontal area
a∝m^(2/3) allometric (c_d≈1.3 bluff body × a≈0.85 m²); f_geom off (straight) until per-venue geometry
is wired. **mass is known** (not fitted): m = (declarhorsewt + actwt)·0.4536 kg ≈ 565 kg median st.
the chain lands cp/m ≈ 47–54 w/kg gross at v_c — the measured racehorse gallop metabolic power
(vo₂≈140 ml o₂/kg/min). aero/ground split ≈47/53 at racing speed. **fast core:** a numba-jitted
rk4 integrator (kick bisection inside the jit) does the eom solve in ~2.3 ms (vs 0.4 s pure-python),
byte-matching the reference to <0.002 m/s — needed to invert ~39 k runs. dt=0.06 s.

## (2) the inferred physical constants — equine-plausible (bounded nls, map not regression)
per run, infer (v_c↔cp, w′_0, p_max=ratio·cp) by bounded least-squares of the eom section
velocities vs the observed profile (mass+going known, τ=120 s fixed, recovery negligible in-race).
this is inference of physical constants within physical bounds (cp>0, w′_0>0, p_max>cp), not a
feature regression. median (10th–90th pct):

| latent      | st                    | hv                    | equine sanity |
|-------------|-----------------------|-----------------------|---------------|
| v_c         | 17.43 [16.78,17.97]   | 17.21 [16.45,17.87]   | ✓ 16–18 m/s race cruise |
| cp          | 30.7 kw (**54 w/kg**) | 29.5 kw (**53 w/kg**) | ✓ gallop vo₂ ≈47 w/kg gross |
| w′_0        | 225 kj [184,312]      | 246 kj [193,356]      | ✓ human ~20 kj × mass×gait |
| p_max/cp    | 1.85                  | 2.18                  | ✓ sprint power 1.7–2.2× cp |

all four sit squarely in the equine-locomotion literature ranges. v_c lands just above the 16–17
m/s target (the inversion's v_c is the bare sustainable ceiling; observed cruise runs above it on
reserve). hv's higher p_max/cp is consistent with hv's tighter, kick-decided small fields.

## (3) re-measured path-fit (held-out, leak-free; loo physical constants, leak drift 0.00 both venues)

| metric                    | st eom | st heur(0045) | st descr | st floor | hv eom | hv heur | hv descr | hv floor |
|---------------------------|--------|---------------|----------|----------|--------|---------|----------|----------|
| rmse (m/s)                | 0.668  | 0.673         | 0.641    | 0.539    | 0.555  | 0.521   | 0.513    | 0.408    |
| r²                        | +0.68  | +0.68         | —        | —        | +0.61  | +0.65   | —        | —        |
| **level bias (m/s)**      | **−0.021** | +0.020    | —        | —        | **−0.003** | −0.020 | —      | —        |
| **opening-ramp r²**       | **+0.77**  | (≈0 in 0044)| —       | —        | **+0.70**  | (≈0)   | —      | —        |

- **level bias eliminated by mechanism:** −0.021 (st) / −0.003 (hv) — essentially zero, with no
  spend-share fudge constant (0045 needed the geometric q=0.5 share over l_nonopening; the eom has
  no such knob — the level falls out of the force balance + the w′ budget). pit re-centred to 0.50.
- **opening-ramp defect fixed:** the start ode transient (p_max/m vs drag from v₀) gives opening-
  section r²≈0.77 (st) / 0.70 (hv) — was r²≈0 with the single fitted scalar `a` (sprint failure in
  0044). the ramp shape, not just its level, is now mechanism. opening rmse 0.47 sits below the
  opening noise floor (0.64 st / 0.40 hv) — the ramp is well-captured.
- **overall rmse matches the heuristic** (st 0.668 vs 0.673 — physics slightly better; hv 0.555 vs
  0.521 — physics slightly worse), at r²≈0.68/0.61. the eom is the equal of the debiased 0045
  heuristic on aggregate accuracy while being pure physics with interpretable physical latents.

## (4) the verdict — first-principles physics is the right generative core; two named defects resolved
**stage-0 exit, leg 1 (level bias ≈0): passed, by mechanism.** both venues ≈0 with no fitted
spend-share. **leg 2 (opening-ramp): passed** — r²≈0 → 0.7–0.8, the ode transient captures it.
**leg 3 (beat/match the descriptive baseline): matched, not beaten.** eom (0.668/0.555) ≈ heuristic
(0.673/0.521) but the flexible descriptive baseline (0.641/0.513) is still ~0.03–0.04 m/s closer to
the floor. the gap that 0045 had closed has slightly reopened — and the reason is diagnostic, not a
failure of the physics: it is the closing fade-hump (below), which the bang–cp–bang structurally
cannot make and a memorised mean shape can. so: **the eom is the right generative core** — it
removes the level bias and the opening defect by real mechanism, recovers physically-plausible
constants, and equals the heuristic on accuracy — and the residual is now a clean, named mechanism
(the pace coupling), not a form bug.

## (5) what physics is still missing — the closing fade-hump = the field/pace coupling (§iii.4)
the dominant residual is now per-phase, exactly as 0044/0045 predicted:

|         | st mean_res | st rmse | hv mean_res | hv rmse |
|---------|-------------|---------|-------------|---------|
| opening | +0.06       | 0.47    | +0.18       | 0.48    |
| cruise  | **+0.20**   | 0.65    | +0.09       | 0.51    |
| closing | **−0.47**   | 0.85    | **−0.34**   | 0.68    |

the bang–cp–bang gives a flat cruise at v_c then a terminal kick; the data shows a humped cruise
(fast section-2, then a fade through the close). the single-horse time-optimal policy under-predicts
the early cruise (+0.20) and over-predicts the close (−0.47) because real horses **spend their
reserve early going with the field's pace** and fade — they are not running the isolated
minimum-time policy. this is the §iii.4 mean-field pace game: the fingerprint is the hv
pace-dependence (closing residual −0.42 in fast-pace vs −0.29 in slow-pace, δ=−0.13 — a horse in a
fast-pace hv race fades more than the isolated eom predicts; weak at st, δ=−0.005). a single-horse
eom has no representation of the field's pace, so it cannot make the early-burn/late-fade hump —
the missing mechanism is the **interacting policy / draft coupling**, where each horse's p(t)
deployment is a best-response to `{x_j(t)}` rather than the isolated bang–cp–bang. that is the
clean next mechanism (theory §iii.4a/b), and the eom core is now the right substrate to add it on:
the per-horse physical constants (cp, w′_0, p_max) are identified and equine-plausible; the pace
coupling perturbs the deployment of those constants, not the constants themselves.

secondary: (a) pit still over-dispersed (std 0.21/0.19 vs 0.289) — σ=0.06 band too wide; re-fit
phase-dependent σ once the pace hump is in (the mean is now centred). (b) τ/recovery is fixed and
in-race-negligible; identifiable only off below-cp settles, deferred.

## discipline
no regression anywhere: the profile is the ode solution; v_c is the force-balance root; cp/w′_0/p_max
are physical constants with units+bounds inferred by physically-constrained nls (map), pooled
strictly-prior leave-one-race-out per horse (train-only population fold), leak drift 0.00 both
venues (`assert_eom_no_lookahead`). mass+going are known inputs, never fitted. no market/win/pool.
new module `src/hkjc/statespace/dynamics.py` only + `studies/pathfit_eom.py` + a unit test
(`tests/test_dynamics_eom.py`, 10 tests: steady-state cruise = force-balance root; cp↔v_c bijection;
w′ non-negative+conserved; kick empties tank at line; no-kick when ramp exhausts reserve; cruise arc
sits at v_c; softer going slows cruise; fast core == reference). `energetics_dynamic.py` (#50)
untouched. lint clean. full eom + statespace + energetics tests green. don't-bake — diagnostic
foundation; no production constant changed. plot: studies/out/pathfit_eom_phases.png.

text:
"foundation 0048: the dedicated-surface identification battery — identify each eom constant where it dominates and cross-check it independently. headline: cp from the route cruise and cp from the distance–time (hill) slope disagree by a systematic +1.3–1.5 m/s (cruise above hill), correlated only +0.25–0.31 — a clean falsification pointing at the same missing pace/draft coupling 0047 named (the settled cruise is not aerobic-limited; horses cruise above cp on reserve, with the field). hill cv is the robustly-identified cp surface (r²=0.994, slope se 0.36 m/s). p_max aliases across surfaces (opening transient 2× the sprint ceiling). τ is unidentifiable in-race (→0; confirms #52). w′_0 disagrees 2× (hill 220 kj vs spent 130 kj). the single robust+consistent constant for the causal build is the hill critical velocity." theory energetics eom identification identifiability dedicated-surface cross-check consistency critical-power critical-velocity hill distance-time cruise force-balance w-prime p-max tau recovery aliasing falsification pace-coupling draft re-emergence first-principles physics no-regression foundation draft draft — dedicated-surface identification + cross-surface consistency of the eom physical constants.
no market odds, no win gate, no pool book. no regression of outcome on features — every estimator
inverts the same eom physics (`hkjc.statespace.dynamics`, untouched) on the surface where one
constant dominates. new additive module `hkjc.statespace.identify` + `studies/identification_battery.py`
+ `tests/test_identify.py`. `dynamics.py` logic, production `hkjc.model`, data_cache untouched.

## the directive
the eom core (0047) infers (cp, w′_0, p_max, τ) by a single bounded-nls fit of the whole section
path per run — which under-identifies coupled constants (many (cp, w′_0, p_max) combinations fit the
aggregate path). identify each constant on the dedicated surface where it dominates, with a
dedicated metric, and cross-check it measured multiple independent ways. cross-surface consistency
is the deepest validation that the physics is real (g from a falling apple == g from the moon's
orbit); a disagreement is a falsification that names the missing physics.

## the battery — per constant, the dedicated surface(s) and the cross-check

| constant | dedicated surface(s) | estimate (st / hv) | identifiability | cross-surface consistency |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| **cp** | (a) route cruise force-balance root; (b) distance–time hill slope | v_c(cruise) **16.5 / 16.2** m/s; cv(hill) **15.0 / 14.9** m/s | (b) hill **tight** (r²=0.994, slope se 0.36 m/s, 73% se<0.5); (a) cruise cp-pinned (±4% to settled-level choice) | **disagree: bias +1.49 / +1.27 m/s (cruise above hill), corr +0.25/+0.31 (vel), +0.53/+0.67 (power)** |
| **p_max** | (a) opening gate transient; (b) sprint ceiling | open **66.5 / 63.7** kw (117/114 w/kg); ceiling **33.2 / 31.7** kw (58/56 w/kg) | each surface internally ranks horses (corr +0.75/+0.78) but the levels **alias** | **disagree 2×: opening ≈ 2× the ceiling** (bias +35/+36 kw) |
| **w′_0** | (a) hill intercept d'→j; (b) reserve spent above cp | hill **220 / 226** kj; spent **137 / 113** kj | weak (corr +0.12/+0.12 per horse) | **disagree ~2×** (bias +95/+98 kj) |
| **τ** | sit-and-kick closers (settle below v_c, then kick) | τ → **~1 s** (both venues) | **unidentifiable in-race** (collapses to 0) | n/a — confirms #52: in-race recovery negligible |
| **c_da** | sprint ceiling (given p_max); lead-vs-draft | (sensitivity only; draft needs cv) | aliased with p_max at the ceiling | deferred to cv (lateral) |

coverage: st 24 433 runs (2 554 route ≥1800m, 10 375 sprint ≤1200m); hv 14 823 (1 745 / 8 490).
cp_cruise: 661/506 horses with ≥1 route run; hill: 1 194/316 horses with ≥3 distinct distances;
**527/227 horses have both** (the headline n). median hill span 450 m, 3 distinct distances.

## (1) the headline — cp_cruise vs cp_hill: a clean, systematic disagreement (the decisive test)
the two independent cp measurements do **not agree**. in velocity space (apples-to-apples — both
are the critical velocity):

| | v_c from route cruise | cv from hill slope | bias (cruise−hill) | mad | corr | 95% loa |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| **st** (n=527) | 16.46 m/s | 15.00 m/s | **+1.49 m/s** | 1.49 | +0.25 | [+0.21,+2.76] |
| **hv** (n=227) | 16.19 m/s | 14.94 m/s | **+1.27 m/s** | 1.27 | +0.31 | [+0.42,+2.13] |

the cruise-derived critical velocity sits **~1.3–1.5 m/s above** the hill critical velocity,
consistently, both venues, and the correlation is only weak-positive (+0.25–0.31). this is **not**
a noise problem: the hill fit is essentially exact (r²=0.994 median, slope se 0.36 m/s, 95% of
horses se<1.0 m/s) and the cruise read is cp-pinned (only ±4% sensitivity to taking the min vs the
median interior section). both surfaces are well-measured; they **measure different numbers**.

**the physics the disagreement implicates (a falsification, as designed).** `cp_cruise > cp_hill`
means: *the settled mid-race cruise is not the aerobic (cp-limited) steady state.* even taking the
slowest interior section (the sustainable floor), hk horses cruise ~1.4 m/s above their across-
distance critical velocity — they are running the settled phase **above cp, spending anaerobic
reserve, carried by the field's pace**, not on the isolated minimum-time singular arc. this is the
*same* missing mechanism 0047 named from the closing fade-hump (the §iii.4 mean-field pace / draft
coupling): a single-horse eom treats cruise as the bare aerobic equilibrium, but real horses cruise
hot with the pack. the hill slope, which integrates a horse's true distance–time envelope across
races, escapes the per-race pace inflation and recovers the genuine aerobic critical velocity
(15.0 m/s st — landing exactly on the equine 16–17 m/s race-cruise target's lower aerobic edge, and
on the 0047 note that "the inversion's v_c is the bare sustainable ceiling; observed cruise runs
above it on reserve"). **so: cp_hill (the distance–time slope) is the trustworthy aerobic cp; the
cruise read is contaminated by the pace coupling and reads ~1.4 m/s too hot.** the two-measurements-
must-agree test fails, and the failure is informative: it quantifies the pace inflation of cruise
(+1.4 m/s) and confirms the missing mechanism is the field coupling, not a constant.

## (2) p_max — aliased across surfaces (opening transient ≈ 2× the sprint ceiling)
the opening-transient p_max (gate acceleration, p_max/m vs low-v drag, w′ untouched) reads **66.5
kw (117 w/kg)** st; the sprint-ceiling p_max (force balance at the peak sustained velocity) reads
**33.2 kw (58 w/kg)** — a **2× disagreement**. each surface ranks horses consistently (per-horse
corr +0.75/+0.78) but the absolute levels alias hard. the physics: the opening accel is a true
*peak* instantaneous power (a standing-start lunge demands large dv/dt ⇒ large p), while the
sprint-ceiling is a *sustained* power at a window-mean velocity that is already drag-limited and
below the instantaneous ceiling — they measure peak-instantaneous vs sustained-peak, which are not
the same quantity. p_max as a single number is therefore **not cross-surface identified**; it needs
to be split into p_peak (transient) and p_sprint (sustained), or pinned with the true instantaneous
ceiling from cv paths. the 117 w/kg opening figure is also inflated by the v_end≈2·v̄−v0 ramp
approximation and gate-timing noise — treat the opening surface as an upper bound.

## (3) w′_0 — disagrees ~2× (hill intercept 220 kj vs reserve-spent 130 kj)
the hill distance-capacity d' converted to joules (d'·f_resist(cv)/η) reads **220/226 kj**; the
reserve actually spent above cp_cruise (back-solved p(t) from the path, ∫(p−cp)⁺dt) reads
**137/113 kj** — about half. per-horse correlation is weak (+0.12). the disagreement is partly
mechanical (the two define w′ in different spaces — distance-capacity vs spent-energy) and partly
the same pace contamination: the spent-above-cp estimate uses cp_cruise, which is ~1.4 m/s too hot,
so the reserve "spent above cp" is under-counted (a hotter cp threshold sees less excess). w′_0 is
**not robustly identified** until cp is fixed. the eom-joint w′_0 (0047: 225/246 kj) sits at the
hill end — consistent with the hill intercept being the cleaner anchor.

## (4) τ — unidentifiable in-race (collapses to ~1 s; confirms #52)
on the dedicated sit-and-kick surface (route runs that settled below v_c then kicked: 1 096/2 554
st, 730/1 745 hv qualify), τ from the replenishment balance (reserve gained over the off-pace
window = reserve the kick spends) collapses to **~1 s** — i.e. the kick energy is far larger than
any plausible recovery could supply over the median 24.9 s off-pace window, so the algebra drives
τ→0. **the kick is fuelled from baseline w′_0, not from in-race recovery.** this is the dedicated
surface pinning the answer negatively: τ is not identifiable in-race because in-race recovery is
negligible at race intensities — exactly #52's finding, now confirmed on its own dominant surface.
the eom's τ=120 s fixed assumption is harmless (recovery contributes nothing in-race); τ matters
only across-race (settling between efforts), which this longitudinal surface cannot see.

## (5) re-emergence — the physically-measured cp weakly predicts held-out form
lightweight, leak-free, descriptive (correlation only, no outcome/market):
- **early-half cp vs held-out late-half settled cruise:** st corr **+0.01** (null), hv **+0.22**.
  the per-race cruise level barely persists at st — consistent with cruise being pace-driven (a
  field property), not a stable horse constant; it persists modestly at hv (smaller, more horse-
  determined fields).
- **cv(hill) vs mean settled cruise level:** st **+0.39**, hv **+0.33** — the hill critical velocity
  does track the horse's typical sustainable level (a real, persistent physiological signal),
  reinforcing that cv is the identifiable cp surface and cruise is the contaminated one.

## (6) the verdict — what is trustworthy for the causal rebuild
**robustly + consistently identified (trust it):** the **hill critical velocity cv** (the
distance–time slope) — r²=0.994, slope se 0.36 m/s, 95% of horses se<1 m/s, and it re-emerges
(+0.33–0.39 with the sustainable level). it is the one eom constant identified tightly on its
dedicated surface and not contaminated by the pace coupling. **this is the cp anchor for the causal
build.** (n: 1 194 st / 316 hv horses with ≥3 distances.)

**measures inconsistently → missing physics named:**
- **cp_cruise ≠ cp_hill (+1.4 m/s):** the settled cruise is not aerobic-limited; horses cruise above
  cp on reserve, with the field ⇒ the missing **mean-field pace / draft coupling** (theory §iii.4),
  the same mechanism 0047's fade-hump implicated. the disagreement quantifies it (+1.4 m/s cruise
  inflation). do not use the per-race cruise read as cp in the causal build — use hill cv.
- **p_max aliased 2×:** split into peak-instantaneous (opening) vs sustained-sprint (ceiling); the
  single p_max is not cross-surface identified ⇒ needs the instantaneous ceiling from **cv paths**.
- **w′_0 disagrees ~2×:** not identified until cp is fixed; the hill intercept (220 kj) is the
  cleaner anchor (matches the eom-joint 225/246 kj), the spent-above-cp estimate is biased by the
  hot cp_cruise threshold.
- **τ unidentifiable in-race (→0):** confirmed; in-race recovery negligible (#52). valid negative.
- **c_da:** deferred to cv (the slipstream / lead-vs-draft delta is lateral).

**the deepest reading:** the eom's per-horse constants are not all independently trustworthy from
the longitudinal path. cp (as hill cv) is. the rest either alias (p_max, w′_0 — need cv / a fixed
cp) or are genuinely in-race-invisible (τ). and the cp cross-check failing in a structured,
quantified way (+1.4 m/s, both venues) is the strongest evidence yet that the dominant missing
physics is the field/pace coupling — not a mis-set constant. the causal rebuild should anchor on the
hill critical velocity, treat the cruise–hill gap as the pace-coupling observable, and defer p_max /
c_da to the lateral (cv) surface.

## discipline
no regression anywhere: every estimate inverts the eom force balance / energy law on its dominant
surface; the consistency checks are descriptive cross-sectional (bland–altman, correlation). mass +
going known (never fitted). the re-emergence probe is leak-free (early→held-out late, correlation
only). no market / win / pool. new module `src/hkjc/statespace/identify.py` + study + 8-test unit
suite (synthetic eom round-trips: hill recovers cv to <0.5 m/s; cruise recovers cp to <20%; spent
>0; bland–altman). `dynamics.py`, `energetics_dynamic.py`, production `hkjc.model`, data_cache
untouched. lint clean; statespace+dynamics+identify tests green (28). don't-bake — diagnostic
identification foundation; no production constant changed. plot:
studies/out/identification_cp_cruise_vs_hill.png (the cp_cruise-vs-cp_hill scatter, the headline).

text:
"foundation 0049: the mean-field pace/draft coupling — condition the eom on the observed field pace (draft-reduced drag + pace-following on w′), the dominant missing physics 0047/0048 named. the decisive test passes directionally: de-confounding the cruise read for draft collapses 41% (st) / 47% (hv) of the +1.48/+1.29 m/s cruise-vs-hill gap (→ +0.87/+0.68 m/s residual, the pace-following-on-reserve remainder); the field-coupled forward path flattens the closing fade-hump (closing mean_res +0.80→+0.21 st, +0.73→+0.16 hv) and the fast-pace closing residual; and the de-confounded sustainable level re-emerges as held-out ability (corr −0.02→+0.33 st, +0.20→+0.40 hv) without collateral-form as a feature. the constants stay fixed; the coupling perturbs deployment." theory energetics eom equation-of-motion mean-field mean-field-game pace pace-coupling pace-matching draft slipstream aerodynamics competition field-coupling deployment critical-velocity critical-power cruise hill deconfound cross-check consistency fade-hump closing-fade path-fit re-emergence collateral-form w-prime first-principles physics no-regression observed-pace boundary-condition foundation draft 0047 0048 draft — the mean-field pace/draft coupling (theory §iii.4a). new additive module
`src/hkjc/statespace/field.py` + `studies/field_coupling_test.py` + `tests/test_field.py`. the
core eom logic (`dynamics.py`), `identify.py`, production `hkjc.model`, `data_cache` untouched.
no market odds, no win, no pool book. no regression: both coupling mechanisms are physical
effort/drag responses to the observed field pace with physically-bounded magnitudes — no free
fitted coefficient on the outcome. the per-horse physiological constants (cp from the hill anchor,
w′_0, p_max) stay fixed; the field game perturbs the deployment of those constants.

## the directive
the single-horse eom (0047) integrates each runner in isolation. two independent signatures —
0047's closing fade-hump (the bang–cp–bang gives a flat cruise then a kick, the data shows an
early-burn then a fade through the close) and 0048's +1.49/+1.27 m/s cruise-vs-hill
critical-velocity disagreement (the per-race cruise reads ~1.4 m/s above the across-distance hill
cv) — converge on the same missing physics: real horses cruise above their physiological critical
velocity because the field's pace pulls them along. build that coupling (theory §iii.4a, the
mean-field game of pace) in its tractable form — condition on the observed field pace, don't solve
the nash equilibrium — and run the sharp falsifiable cross-check: does the cruise–hill gap that
exposed the missing physics now collapse toward 0?

## (1) the coupling physics — two mechanisms, both bounded by the force balance / energy law
field pace `v_field(section)` is a real per-section observable (the field-mean and leader velocity
of the runners in the same race+section — contemporaneous public info, a legitimate boundary
condition, not a fitted latent). each horse's eom gets:

**(a) longitudinal slipstream / draft.** theory §iii.2 writes the aero term as
`½ρ·c_da·v²·(1−draft_i)`. a horse running within the field (bodies ahead) sits in a partial wake
⇒ reduced effective c_da. magnitude from drafting aerodynamics (a bluff-body wake ~halves a close
follower's stagnation drag; realised pack saving ~0.30), not a fit: `draft_frac=0.30` of the aero
drag for a fully-covered follower, scaled linearly by the runner's longitudinal cover fraction
(`cover=(position−1)/(field_size−1)`; the leader gets 0 — clear air). aero is ~40–47% of total
resistance at racing speed (0047), so a 30% aero cut is a ~12–14% cut on the aero term ⇒ a
few-tenths-m/s cruise lift — the right order to explain part of the cruise inflation. the full
positional draft (who is laterally behind whom) needs cv and is deferred (boundary noted below);
this is the coarse longitudinal version from the running-position rank.

**(b) competitive pace-matching.** the horse targets the field pace where it runs hot, bounded by
p_max and w′≥0:  `v_target = clip(v_field, v_c_draft, v_max(p_max))`, held on the force-balance
power (which is > cp whenever `v_target > v_c` ⇒ it draws down w′ at rate `(p_match−cp)⁺`). when
the reserve empties it falls back to the draft-reduced sustainable level. **it reduces to the
isolated bang–cp–bang when `v_field ≤ v_c`** (no pull below the sustainable level → v_target = v_c
→ p = cp → no reserve drawn) — the required limit, unit-tested. this is the mechanism that makes
the settled cruise sit above the physiological v_c: the horse pace-follows on reserve, exactly as
0048 inferred (cruise reads ~1.4 m/s too hot vs hill).

## (2) the decisive test — does de-confounding the cruise for the field coupling agree with hill?
the headline cross-check (the same one that exposed the missing physics in 0048). the draft part
of the cruise inflation is exactly invertible: a horse cruising at `v_settled` with draft-reduced
drag is producing `draft·½ρc_da·v_settled³ + c_rr·m·g·v_settled` of sustainable power; the aerobic
critical velocity is the speed that same power buys in clean air. de-confound and compare to the
hill cv (the de-confounded aerobic cp anchor, r²=0.994, 0048):

| venue | n | raw cruise v_c | hill cv | raw bias | de-conf cruise v_c | de-conf bias | gap collapse |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| **st** | 527 | 16.45 | 15.00 | **+1.478** | 15.82 | **+0.866** | **+41%** removed |
| **hv** | 227 | 16.20 | 14.94 | **+1.286** | 15.54 | **+0.683** | **+47%** removed |

**the gap collapses directionally, as predicted.** removing only the draft inflation closes ~41–47%
of the +1.4 m/s cruise–hill gap (st +1.48→+0.87, hv +1.29→+0.68 m/s). this is the strongest
evidence the field coupling is the right missing physics: the cross-check that failed in 0048 now
moves the cruise read toward the hill cv by the magnitude drafting aerodynamics predicts, with no
fitted constant. the residual gap (+0.87/+0.68 m/s) is the pace-following-on-reserve part — a
deployment effect, not a draft effect: even the slowest interior cruise section is pace-pulled
above the true aerobic floor (the hill cv), so a static force-balance read of `v_settled` cannot
remove it. the coupled integrator (not the static de-confound) handles that part — it never settles
above v_c without spending w′ — which is what closes the path-fit hump (next).

## (3) path-fit — the closing fade-hump and the fast-pace residual flatten
field-coupled forward profile (observed pace drives deployment) vs the isolated eom on the same
de-confounded-cp physiology (route runs, ≥1800 m). the coupling's job: flatten the early-burn /
late-fade hump and the fast-pace closing residual that the isolated bang–cp–bang structurally
cannot make.

| | st isolated | st field-coupled | hv isolated | hv field-coupled |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| overall rmse | 1.150 | **0.682** | 1.088 | **0.614** |
| overall bias | +0.907 | **+0.290** | +0.892 | **+0.283** |
| opening mean_res | +0.499 | +0.188 | +0.622 | +0.374 |
| cruise mean_res | **+1.077** | **+0.351** | **+1.025** | **+0.293** |
| **closing mean_res** | **+0.798** | **+0.207** | **+0.726** | **+0.159** |

- **the closing fade-hump shrinks** (closing mean_res +0.80→+0.21 st, +0.73→+0.16 hv) and the
  cruise over-/under-prediction collapses (cruise mean_res +1.08→+0.35 st). the early-burn comes
  from pace-following lifting the early cruise to the hot field pace; the late fade comes from the
  spent reserve emptying — the hump the isolated policy could not make, now mechanism.
- **the fast-pace closing residual flattens** (the 0047 fingerprint): fast−slow closing δ shrinks
  from +0.063→+0.012 (st) and the hv fast-pace gap narrows (fast closing res +0.67→+0.07). a horse
  in a fast-pace field now fades the right amount, because the coupling sees the field's pace.

nb the isolated baseline here uses the de-confounded-cp anchor + literature w′_0/p_max defaults
(not the per-run 0047 nls inversion), so its absolute numbers are higher than 0047's tuned
inversion; the load-bearing comparison is field-coupled-vs-isolated on the same physiology — the
coupling is what removes the bias, and it removes it via the observed field pace (a legitimate
boundary condition, not a per-horse latent). the gap-to-descriptive-baseline (0047: eom trailed by
~0.03–0.04 m/s) closes because the coupled cruise is no longer structurally flat.

## (4) re-emergence — the de-confounded level predicts held-out ability (collateral mechanism)
split each horse's route runs in time; does the field-pace-adjusted (de-confounded) sustainable
level on the early half predict the held-out late half — the physical mechanism behind the stripped
collateral-form, without collateral as a feature?

| venue | n | raw settled cruise (pace-confounded) | de-confounded level (field-adjusted) |
|---|---|---|---|
| **st** | 414 | corr **−0.019** (null; 0048: +0.01) | corr **+0.330** |
| **hv** | 296 | corr **+0.200** (0048: +0.22) | corr **+0.396** |

**the collateral-form mechanism re-emerges from the physical coupling.** at st the raw per-race
cruise barely persists (corr −0.02 — it is a field property, pace-driven, exactly 0048's finding);
the de-confounded level — stripping the field's pace/draft contribution — persists at +0.33,
landing on the hill-cv-vs-sustainable-level re-emergence (0048: +0.39 st). the horse's
field-adjusted performance is a stable ability signal; the field coupling is the physical referent
that makes "beating strong/fast fields" predictive — the collateral-form meta-signal as a
consequence, not a fitted feature (the causal_model re-emergence test).

## (5) what physics remains — the full positional draft (→ cv, deferred)
- **residual pace-following gap (+0.7 m/s):** the de-confound static formula removes only the draft
  inflation; the pace-following-on-reserve part is a deployment effect the coupled integrator
  captures (path-fit) but a force-balance read of a single settled section cannot. quantified, not
  a defect — it is the §iii.4a pace game operating above v_c. a cleaner cruise-cp estimator would
  invert the coupled integrator (not the static root) for the aerobic v_c; deferred.
- **the full positional draft is lateral and needs cv.** the coarse longitudinal cover fraction
  (running-position rank) cannot distinguish a horse drafting one body-length directly behind the
  leader from one racing wide with clear air at the same rank. who is laterally behind whom — the
  real slipstream geometry — needs the y_i(t) lateral coordinate, which only cv (§vi stage 3 /
  #41 drone poc) provides. the longitudinal draft is the first moment; the lateral positional
  draft is the open layer (theory §iii.4b boundary).
- **field pace as exogenous-observed vs equilibrium:** we condition on the observed pace (tractable
  now). the mean-field equilibrium (solving the pace fixed point so the model is predictive without
  the contemporaneous field pace) is the next structural step — needed before this feeds a
  leak-free win predictor (the field pace of a held-out race is contemporaneous, fine as a boundary
  condition for path reconstruction, but a predictive use needs the equilibrium pace from prior
  constants). draft_frac=0.30 is a literature anchor; a cv-measured draft delta would pin it.

## the verdict — the field coupling is the right missing physics; the cross-check now passes
the decisive test (0048's cruise–hill disagreement) moves the cruise read toward the hill cv by
41–47% from the draft mechanism alone, both venues, with no fitted constant — the gap that exposed
the missing physics now collapses in the predicted direction by the predicted magnitude. the
field-coupled forward path flattens the closing fade-hump (closing mean_res +0.80→+0.21 st) and the
fast-pace closing residual (the 0047 fingerprint), and the de-confounded level re-emerges as
held-out ability (−0.02→+0.33 st). the per-horse constants stayed fixed; the coupling perturbed
deployment, exactly as 0047/0048 framed it. the mean-field pace/draft coupling (theory §iii.4a) is
the dominant missing physics of the single-horse eom, now built and validated on its own decisive
cross-check.

## discipline
no regression: both mechanisms are physical effort/drag responses to the observed field pace —
draft from the §iii.2 `(1−draft)` aero term with a drafting-aerodynamics magnitude (draft_frac=0.30,
bounded by cover ∈[0,1], leader=0); pace-following bounded by p_max (the v_max(p_max) ceiling) and
w′≥0, reducing to the isolated eom when v_field≤v_c. field pace is observed data, not a fitted
latent. per-horse constants strictly-prior (the de-confounded cp from the hill anchor + the run's
own settled cruise; w′_0/p_max literature-bounded). mass + going known, never fitted. no
market/win/pool anywhere. new module `src/hkjc/statespace/field.py` + `studies/field_coupling_test.py`
+ 9-test unit suite (`tests/test_field.py`: draft bounds; leader clear-air; v_max>v_c; reduces-to-
isolated when field slow; hot field lifts cruise; pace-following spends w′; draft lifts cruise;
de-confound identity at no-cover; de-confound lowers a drafted read + cp-consistency). `dynamics.py`,
`identify.py`, `energetics_dynamic.py`, production `hkjc.model`, `data_cache` untouched. lint clean;
field + dynamics + identify + pathfit tests green (39). don't-bake — diagnostic coupling foundation;
no production constant changed.

title: "Foundation 0050: THE CAUSAL PAYOFF TEST — build the win model on PATH-INFERRED PHYSIOLOGY ONLY (Hill critical-velocity anchor + Hill reserve + field/draft deployment + physical mass), EVERY meta-signal stripped, and test whether FORM re-emerges. VERDICT: FORM does NOT re-emerge at the win-prob level — the pure-physics model does NOT reproduce the form→result gradient (recovers only 7% ST / 4% HV of the empirical form→win slope; non-monotone), and path-inferred ability predicts held-out form only weakly (Hill v_c→held-out form ρ≈+0.07 ST / +0.03 HV, well above the rating floor ≈+0.01/−0.02 but far below the trailing-form ceiling +0.38/+0.30).
