text:
"s7b win-wiring of the field/deployment cause (the gated next step after 0063): wire the front-group pace-war w′-burn into the generative win drift as a per-runner reduction of effective anaerobic reserve, guarded behind ``generativeracemodel(field_pace_war=)`` defaulting off (off reproduces the physiology-only model byte-identically — the 181 existing tests stay green). built ``field.pace_war_burn_per_runner`` (the per-runner companion of ``pace_war_gradient``: each contested front-runner held above its own cruise ``base_i`` at the front pace ``l`` spends reserve ``δv_i·t_early`` [m] over the opening window, gated by the front-count pace-war threshold — pure eom force-balance physics, no outcome-fitted knob), carried it leak-free on ``raceconditions.pace_war_burn``, and reduced ``w′_eff = max(w′ − burn, 0)`` where the reserve boost (1+w′/l) enters ``generative._drift_times`` ⇒ a front-runner in a hot, front-heavy field carries less reserve to the finish ⇒ its drift slows. consolidated the forwardness orientation onto the corrected sign (0063): forwardness = 1 − ``trail_early_pos_norm`` (high = closer), retiring the un-inverted feed in ``equilibrium_pace.py`` / ``field_pace_ceiling.py``. measure (``studies/field_win_wiring.py``, paired fixed-seed, leak-free assert_no_lookahead drift=0 both venues): the win-diagnostic %market delta physiology-only (off) vs +field (on). verdict: the field dimension barely moves the win diagnostic — st 7.98%→8.46% (δ+0.48%), hv 9.45%→9.54% (δ+0.10%), ece ~flat both; the pace war fires in 44–49% of test races. honest: a real-but-small causal dimension that barely moves win is a legitimate finding (win is the diagnostic of cumulative causal coverage, 0060, not the target). side-finding: the 0063 orientation fix, applied to 0061's equilibrium-pace study, flips its hv 'beats' to mixed (rmse better, corr flat) — 0061 was on the wrong sign; the 0063 mechanism |ρ| (0.026 st / 0.213 hv) is unchanged (it already used the corrected forwardness). no regression, no win-fitted constant; leak-free / strictly-prior." s7b field-coupling deployment win-wiring win-drift generative-drift win-diagnostic win-as-diagnostic causal-coverage pace-war wprime-burn w-prime effective-reserve reserve-reduction critical-power over-spend front-runner front-count threshold threshold-coupling guarded default-off additive byte-identical acceptance-gate orientation-fix forwardness trail-early-pos-norm consolidate first-principles no-regression no-epicycle no-fitted-constant leak-free strictly-prior paired-seed percent-of-market ece venue-split small-delta honest-null proxy-to-win wave-2 field-cause 0049 0060 0061 0062 0063 s7b — the win-wiring step the field/deployment thread (0061→0063) deferred as the separate, parked
arbiter. 0063 built + validated the front-group pace-war w′-burn gradient mechanism on the pace proxy
(hv recovers the de-confounded composition signal |ρ|=0.213; st a ceiling-checked true null) but did
not wire it into the generative win drift, because pace is a proxy and win is the parked diagnostic of
cumulative causal coverage (0060; philosophy §6). this entry wires it and measures whether adding the
2nd causal dimension (after physiology, 0050–0059) moves the win diagnostic. no win-fitted constant;
guarded; leak-free.

## the wiring (causal, leak-free, guarded / additive)
the pace war makes contesting front-runners spend anaerobic reserve early, so they carry less reserve
into the finish. three pieces:
- **``field.pace_war_burn_per_runner(base, style)``** — the per-runner companion of 0063's
  ``pace_war_gradient``. among genuine front-runners (forwardness ``style ≥ front_style_cutoff``) the
  lead is contested at the front pace ``l`` (the fastest front-runner's own cruise); each front-runner
  held above its own sustainable opening cruise ``base_i`` runs above cp and spends the over-pace
  ``δv_i = δp_i⁺/(dp/dv|_l)`` [m/s] (``δp_i⁺ = [p(l)−p(base_i)]⁺``, the eom force-balance over-spend at
  l, eq.3 — pure resistance physics). the reserve it depletes over the opening window is
  ``burn_i = g(n_front)·δv_i·t_early`` [m], ``t_early = pace_war_early_dist/l`` — the same
  distance-reserve units the model's w′ carries (``σ(v−v_c)·t``, ``energetics.recover_energetics``),
  so it subtracts directly off w′. gated on the front-count pace-war threshold (``front_war_gate``):
  zero for a lone/uncontested leader, a closer, or a single-speed front (all unit-tested).
- **``raceconditions.pace_war_burn``** — the per-runner burn carried as a pre-race composition input
  (known before the race from the field's strictly-prior style/pace ⇒ leak-free), ordered like θ.
- **``generative._effective_w_prime``** — ``w′_eff = max(w′ − burn, 0)`` (floor ``_wprime_floor_frac``
  = 0, no negative reserve), applied where the reserve boost ``v_target = v_c·(1 + w′_eff/l)`` enters
  ``_drift_times``. a burnt front-runner reaches a slower effective target velocity ⇒ a larger μ ⇒ a
  lower win prob.

**guarded / byte-identical baseline (acceptance gate a).** the term is behind
``generativeracemodel(field_pace_war=...)`` defaulting **off**. off returns w′ unchanged even when a
burn is present on conditions ⇒ μ, the sampled orders, and every existing number are byte-identical to
the physiology-only model. the win delta is measured on vs off, paired fixed-seed (the model seeds on
race_id, so off and on share the per-race mc seed and δ is pure mechanism). verified by a focused
guard test: off == baseline (with and without a burn on conditions); on slows exactly the burnt
runners, monotone in the burn, leaving un-burnt runners byte-identical.

## orientation fix consolidated (0063 → here)
``run_policy_dataset.trail_early_pos_norm`` is the strictly-prior trailing position rank, positively
correlated with the section-1 position (1 = leader) ⇒ high = a closer, low = a front-runner — the
inverse of 0061's docstring. 0063 verified this and inverted inside its own study. here the corrected
sign is consolidated: forwardness = ``1 − trail_early_pos_norm`` is applied at the loader in
``equilibrium_pace.py`` and ``field_pace_ceiling.py`` (retiring the un-inverted feed), and
``field_gradient_coupling.py`` is de-double-inverted (the loader now does it once). ``field.py``'s
``equilibrium_pace``/``front_group_pace``/``pace_war_*`` always take the corrected forwardness; the
docstring is repointed.

## measure — the win-diagnostic delta (``studies/field_win_wiring.py``; paired fixed-seed; leak-free)
metric = the exact win %market the gate uses (``gate.gate_score``: (uniform_ll − model_ll)/(uniform_ll
− market_ll)) + ece. θ = path-energetics, strictly-prior, train-only eb population (the same honest
generator as 0053/pool_book_gate); the field term is the only change on vs off. test window = the
latest 30% of dates; ``assert_no_lookahead`` drift = 0 both venues.

| venue | n races | runners | pace war fires | physiology-only %mkt | +field %mkt | **δ%mkt** | δece |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| **st** | 602 | 7745 | 267 (44.4%) | 7.98% | 8.46% | **+0.48%** | +0.0002 |
| **hv** | 403 | 4707 | 196 (48.6%) | 9.45% | 9.54% | **+0.10%** | +0.0005 |

(ece: st 0.0073→0.0074, hv 0.0029→0.0034 — calibration unchanged to 3 dp. win_ll: st
2.5003→2.4977, hv 2.4202→2.4199 — a sliver sharper.)

## the read — honest (win is the diagnostic, not the target)
**the field dimension barely moves the win diagnostic.** both deltas are positive but tiny (st +0.48%,
hv +0.10% of market), calibration is unchanged. this is a legitimate finding under the 0060
re-orientation: win diagnoses cumulative causal coverage, and a single 2nd causal dimension wired on
top of physiology is expected to add a small increment, not a jump — the all-dimension aggregate
(form, ~45–60%) integrates many causes. the mechanism is correct, leak-free, and first-principles; it
simply carries little win information on top of the physiology θ at this stage.

two honest wrinkles:
- **the venue shape inverts vs the pace proxy.** on the pace observable (0063) hv carried the signal
  (|ρ|=0.213) and st was a noise floor (0.026). at the win gate st moves slightly more (+0.48% vs hv
  +0.10%). this is the load-bearing 0062/0063 caveat realised: pace is a proxy, and pace-skill does
  not map cleanly to win-skill. the most likely reading is that the pace-war reserve burn perturbs the
  order more where the physiology θ leaves more win headroom (st's physiology floor 8.0% is lower than
  hv's 9.5%), and hv's tighter, more-congested win outcome already prices the front-crowd effect that
  the burn re-expresses. neither delta is large enough to over-interpret.
- **the increment is within the range a re-seed could wobble.** +0.10–0.48% on 400–600 races is a real
  but marginal lift; the win step does not promote the field dimension as a strong win driver. the
  pace-validated hv gradient signal (0063) does not convert to a hv win lift — the parked arbiter the
  0062/0063 caveats flagged has now answered, and the answer is "small, and not where the pace proxy
  pointed."

## side-finding — 0061's hv 'beats' was on the wrong sign
re-running 0061's equilibrium-pace study with the consolidated correct forwardness: hv flips from
"beats" (0061: corr +0.814→+0.821, rmse 0.558→0.542) to mixed (corr +0.814→+0.814 flat, rmse
0.558→0.550 better, bias −0.130→−0.090). 0061's headline "hv beats the naive baseline" was partly an
artefact of the un-inverted style feed; the corrected equilibrium still improves hv rmse/bias but no
longer lifts correlation. the 0063 mechanism |ρ| is unchanged (0.026 st / 0.213 hv) — it already used
the corrected forwardness (it double-inverted before; now the loader inverts once and it reads
directly), so the de-confounded gradient validation stands exactly. the ceiling-gap targets shifted
slightly (ceil/pace features now use corrected forwardness: st gap 0.030→0.012, hv 0.057→0.046) but
the mechanism still meets/exceeds them.

## discipline / artefacts
added to ``src/hkjc/model/field.py`` (sole editor): ``pace_war_burn_per_runner`` + ``pace_war_early_dist``.
``generative.py``: ``_effective_w_prime`` + the ``field_pace_war`` flag (default off) + ``_wprime_floor_frac``
(the only drift change; gated). ``conditions.py``: ``raceconditions.pace_war_burn`` (optional pre-race
input). new ``studies/field_win_wiring.py``. +3 per-runner burn tests in ``tests/test_field.py``, +2
guard tests in ``tests/test_model_skeleton.py`` (off byte-identical incl. with a burn present; on
slows the burnt runners monotonically, un-burnt byte-identical). consolidated the forwardness
orientation in ``equilibrium_pace.py``/``field_pace_ceiling.py``/``field_gradient_coupling.py``.
``dynamics.py``, the pricer, ``gate.py``, ``pure_mechanism.py``, ``identify.py`` untouched;
``src/hkjc/vision/`` left to its concurrent editor. ``ruff check src/hkjc/model studies/field_win_wiring.py``
clean; ``pythonhashseed=0 pytest -q`` green (186 passed = 181 baseline unchanged + 5 new ⇒ the off
guard is intact). leak-free: ``assert_no_lookahead`` drift = 0 both venues; θ/base/style strictly-prior,
the burn is a pre-race composition input, no outcome enters. no regression, no win/pool-fitted constant
— the burn magnitude is the fixed eom force-balance physics, only on/off + the existing physical
front-count threshold are knobs. ran synchronously in the foreground.

## caveats
- **win is the parked diagnostic, not the fitting target (philosophy §6).** the +0.1–0.5% is a
  measurement of coverage, not a goodness-of-fit win to chase. do not tune the threshold / early window
  / floor against the win delta (that would be the forbidden win-calibrated coupling) — they are
  physical readings; only on/off is the promotion knob.
- **proxy→win is the real lesson.** the pace-validated hv gradient (0063) does not convert to a hv win
  lift; the dimension is real on pace but near-marginal on win. the deeper field/deployment win signal
  likely needs the §iii.4b lateral congestion game (cv / stage 3), where a crowded front actually costs
  ground and trip — not just early reserve — which the longitudinal pace-war burn cannot capture.
- **the increment is small.** it is a positive, leak-free, first-principles 2nd-dimension contribution
  — kept on is defensible, but it is not a step-change. the next causal dimension (control/cv lateral,
  0060's frontier) is where the larger uncaptured win coverage most plausibly sits.

## next
the field/deployment dimension is now wired end-to-end (pace-validated + win-measured) and earns a
small, honest place. the win headroom is in the dimensions still unmodelled (0060): control (cv
lateral path — the §iii.4b congestion game that would give the field cause its ground/trip teeth, not
just the early-reserve burn), prep (training-load → on-the-day physiology), condition (gait). the field
win-wiring confirms the 0060 thesis empirically: adding one causal dimension moves the diagnostic a
little, exactly as a one-dimension probe should.

title: "PREP/FITNESS causal dimension (Wave-2 #72): does training load → an on-the-day FITNESS STATE → modulate the path-read physiological constants (CP/W' on race day)? Banister impulse-response (τ_fit=42d / τ_fat=7d / k_fat=2.0, literature priors) built strictly-prior from the trackwork gallops; identification = does prep predict a RESIDUAL in per-run CP/W' controlling for the horse's OWN career-mean baseline (build_pure_mechanism_panel). VERDICT (§4b ceiling check, both venues, seed-stable): on CP it is a clean TRUE NULL — the prep block adds +0.0003 ST / +0.0001 HV over a no-prep conditions ceiling on the CP residual, and +0.004 / +0.002 on the CP level; fitness and fatigue separately add ~0. The Banister STATE (fitness−fatigue) adds essentially nothing to ANY observable (cond+banister ≈ cond everywhere). The ONE real prep signal is on W' (Hill reserve D'): prep_signal +0.088 ST / +0.087 HV — but it is carried ENTIRELY by raw training VOLUME (cond+volume +0.236/+0.317 ≈ cond+prep), NOT the fitness state (cond+banister +0.159/+0.211 ≈ cond), and volume is partly confounded with career maturity (n_prior_gallops↔hill_n_dist +0.25 ST) so it is NOT cleanly a fitness→W' modulation. RE-EMERGENCE: trainer-hot DOES re-emerge from the prep latent without being fed in — prep-block→held-out trainer-recent-strike OOS ridge ceiling +0.109 ST / +0.148 HV (raw state↔trn_strike +0.087/+0.088), seed-stable. HONEST READ: the specific causal claim (Banister fitness STATE shifts the day's CP/W') is a TRUE NULL on CP; the only prep→physiology signal is a small, maturity-confounded volume→W' link; the genuine prep payoff is the trainer-hot re-emergence (the deleted TRN_HOT axis is a consequence of prep). Study-only; nothing wired into the generative drift; ridge is a DIAGNOSTIC ceiling, never the model, never baked."

text:
"prep/fitness causal dimension (wave-2 #72): does training load → an on-the-day fitness state → modulate the path-read physiological constants (cp/w' on race day)? banister impulse-response (τ_fit=42d / τ_fat=7d / k_fat=2.0, literature priors) built strictly-prior from the trackwork gallops; identification = does prep predict a residual in per-run cp/w' controlling for the horse's own career-mean baseline (build_pure_mechanism_panel). verdict (§4b ceiling check, both venues, seed-stable): on cp it is a clean true null — the prep block adds +0.0003 st / +0.0001 hv over a no-prep conditions ceiling on the cp residual, and +0.004 / +0.002 on the cp level; fitness and fatigue separately add ~0. the banister state (fitness−fatigue) adds essentially nothing to any observable (cond+banister ≈ cond everywhere). the one real prep signal is on w' (hill reserve d'): prep_signal +0.088 st / +0.087 hv — but it is carried entirely by raw training volume (cond+volume +0.236/+0.317 ≈ cond+prep), not the fitness state (cond+banister +0.159/+0.211 ≈ cond), and volume is partly confounded with career maturity (n_prior_gallops↔hill_n_dist +0.25 st) so it is not cleanly a fitness→w' modulation. re-emergence: trainer-hot does re-emerge from the prep latent without being fed in — prep-block→held-out trainer-recent-strike oos ridge ceiling +0.109 st / +0.148 hv (raw state↔trn_strike +0.087/+0.088), seed-stable. honest read: the specific causal claim (banister fitness state shifts the day's cp/w') is a true null on cp; the only prep→physiology signal is a small, maturity-confounded volume→w' link; the genuine prep payoff is the trainer-hot re-emergence (the deleted trn_hot axis is a consequence of prep). study-only; nothing wired into the generative drift; ridge is a diagnostic ceiling, never the model, never baked." prep prep-cause fitness fatigue banister impulse-response training-load trackwork gallop physiology cp wprime w-prime critical-power hill modulation on-the-day identification residual career-baseline ceiling ceiling-check mis-spec-vs-null true-null s4b 0054 0062 de-confound conditions-confound training-volume maturity-confound re-emergence reemergence trainer-hot trn-hot trn-hot-gain deleted-axis wave-2 causal-network out-of-sample ridge leak-free strictly-prior first-principles no-regression no-epicycle no-gallop-fusion diagnostic-only dont-bake 0050 0060 prep/fitness — the wave-2 prep causal dimension (0060, task #72). the cause is upstream and physical:
training impulses → an on-the-day fitness state (fitness − fatigue) → a modulation of the horse's own
physiological constants (its cp / w' on race day shift with fitness). this is causal (prep is an
upstream cause of the physiology the path reveals), distinct from the deleted acausal `gallop-fusion`
regression (which regressed gallop speed-figures onto `v_c` — an epicycle). new study-only
`studies/prep_fitness.py`; src/hkjc read-only (`build_pure_mechanism_panel`, `deconfounded_cruise_velocity`,
`settled_cruise_velocity` imported untouched). not wired into the generative drift (a deliberate later
step, like the field dimension's). lint clean; `pythonhashseed=0`, reproducible. full pytest not run
(per task).

## the banister fitness state (physiological priors — not outcome-fitted)
per training session the impulse is `load = gallop_velocity · worked_distance_m` (m²/s, the kinematic
work proxy of one gallop), summed over the day's gallops. at race day d, over the horse's gallop
sessions s with `sdate < d` (strictly-prior, leak-free — prior gallops only):

    fitness = σ_s load_s · exp(−(d − sdate_s)/τ_fit)
    fatigue = k_fat · σ_s load_s · exp(−(d − sdate_s)/τ_fat)
    state   = fitness − fatigue

with the **literature impulse-response constants fixed before any read**: **τ_fit = 42 d** (slow
positive aerobic-adaptation trace), **τ_fat = 7 d** (fast negative recovery trace), **k_fat = 2.0**
(the canonical banister negative-gain ratio k₂/k₁ ≈ 2 — a hard gallop hurts before it helps). these
are constants of the model, not knobs tuned to cp or to the win outcome. coverage: trackwork has 1090
horses, median 76 prior gallops/horse, all overlapping the trajectory panel; with-prep-history runs
st 10,826 / hv 5,633.

## the identification test — does prep predict a residual in the path-read physiology?
target = the per-run physiology read controlling for the horse's own strictly-prior career baseline:
`cp_resid = vc_run − vc_career` where `vc_run` is the current-run de-confounded cruise cp (the same
estimator `build_pure_mechanism_panel` uses internally, read on the run's own path — leak-free: the
prep predictor is strictly-prior, `vc_run` is the measured target) and `vc_career` is the career-mean
cp. also cp level `vc_run` and w' level `wprime_hill` (hill reserve d' [m]). raw correlations (n):

| prep → observable | st corr | hv corr |
|---|---|---|
| state   → cp_resid (vc_run−career) | −0.028 | −0.033 |
| fitness → cp_resid | −0.039 | −0.025 |
| fatigue → cp_resid | −0.035 | −0.007 |
| state   → cp_level (vc_run) | −0.008 | −0.046 |
| state   → w'_level (d') | **+0.069** | −0.045 |
| fitness → w'_level (d') | +0.051 | −0.049 |

the raw prep→cp correlations are ~0 (and, where non-zero, the wrong sign — fitter horses do not show
a higher day-cp). the only non-trivial raw correlation is state→w' on st (+0.069), inconsistent in
sign across venues. a raw read is not a verdict (phil §4b) — apply the ceiling check.

## §4b ceiling check — mis-specification vs true null (the non-negotiable discipline)
a model-agnostic oos ridge ceiling (cv-tuned λ, pooled out-of-fold, the s1b/0062 pattern — a
diagnostic probe, never the model) of each physiology observable from the full prep block, de-confounded
against a no-prep conditions ceiling (distance, field-size, class, body-weight, days-since-last-gallop).
**prep_signal = (cond+prep) − cond.** components swept separately: fitness-only, fatigue-only,
banister-only (fitness+fatigue+state), and raw volume-only (recent14/recent60/load_total/n_gallops).
seed-stable across seeds 0/1/7 (w' prep_signal st +0.088–0.092, hv +0.082–0.087).

| venue | observable | cond | cond+prep | **prep_signal** | cond+fit | cond+fat | cond+banister | cond+volume |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| st | cp_resid (vc_run−career) | +0.333 | +0.333 | **+0.0003** | +0.333 | +0.333 | +0.333 | +0.334 |
| st | cp_level (vc_run) | +0.583 | +0.586 | **+0.0036** | +0.583 | +0.583 | +0.582 | +0.587 |
| st | w'_level (d') | +0.151 | +0.238 | **+0.0877** | +0.153 | +0.148 | +0.159 | **+0.236** |
| hv | cp_resid (vc_run−career) | +0.133 | +0.133 | **+0.0001** | +0.133 | +0.133 | +0.127 | +0.139 |
| hv | cp_level (vc_run) | +0.333 | +0.335 | **+0.0017** | +0.333 | +0.332 | +0.332 | +0.334 |
| hv | w'_level (d') | +0.223 | +0.310 | **+0.0867** | +0.215 | +0.213 | +0.211 | **+0.317** |

### the reads (per phil §4b: `ceiling ≈ cond ⇒ true null`; `ceiling ≫ our model ⇒ mis-spec`)
- **cp (both the career-residual and the level): a clean true null, both venues.** the full prep block
  adds **+0.0003 / +0.0001** on the cp residual and **+0.004 / +0.002** on the cp level over the
  no-prep conditions ceiling. even a flexible oos predictor extracts essentially nothing from prep
  about the day's cp beyond what conditions already say. this is not a mis-specified fitness model
  missing a real cp effect — there is no cp-modulation signal in the trackwork to miss. **the fitness
  state does not modulate the path-read cp.**
- **the banister state itself is null on every observable.** `cond+banister ≈ cond` everywhere
  (w': +0.159/+0.211 vs cond +0.151/+0.223) — fitness, fatigue and their difference add ~0. the
  specific causal posit (fitness − fatigue shifts the constants) finds no purchase.
- **w' (hill reserve d') is the one real prep signal (+0.088 st / +0.087 hv) — but it is training
  volume, not the fitness state.** `cond+volume` (+0.236 / +0.317) ≈ `cond+prep`, while `cond+banister`
  ≈ `cond`: the entire w' lift is carried by raw training volume (recent load, total load, gallop
  count), not by the impulse-response state. and it is partly a maturity confound: `n_prior_gallops`
  correlates with `hill_n_dist` (+0.25 st), the very data-width that identifies the noisy hill
  intercept d' — more-trained horses are more-established horses with more distinct prior distances,
  so a cleaner/larger d'. the direct `n_gallops→w'` link (+0.18 both venues) survives that, so a
  genuine "more training → bigger anaerobic reserve" component is plausible, but it is not cleanly a
  fitness-state → w' modulation and is confounded enough that it is **not** a clean identification.

**verdict: on the headline claim (prep fitness state modulates the path-read cp/w') the result is a
true null on cp and a small, volume-driven / maturity-confounded effect on w' — not a mis-specified
fitness model.** the de-confounded ceiling is the proof it is a true null and not us using the wrong
observable/coupling: the ceiling itself can read nothing more than conditions from prep on cp.

## re-emergence — does trainer-hot (the deleted trn_hot axis) re-emerge from the prep latent?
held-out test: a strictly-prior trainer recent-strike (exp-weighted win indicator over the trainer's
prior runners, shifted one race back — leak-free, never fed as an input), predicted from the prep
block. **trainer-hot does re-emerge:**

| venue | raw state↔trn_strike | prep-block → trn_strike oos ridge ceiling |
|---|---|---|
| st | +0.087 | **+0.109** (seeds 0/1/7: +0.108–0.110) |
| hv | +0.088 | **+0.148** (seeds 0/1/7: +0.147–0.148) |

the prep latent predicts held-out trainer-recent-strike at ρ≈+0.11 st / +0.15 hv without trainer-hot
as an input — a real, seed-stable re-emergence. this is the genuine prep payoff: the trainer-hot
meta-signal is a downstream consequence of the prep cause (a hot trainer is one whose stable's training
load / gallop programme is currently producing fit, recently-galloped runners), exactly as phil §5 /
the §4.4 re-emergence map predicts. it re-emerges as a trainer-programme signal even though prep does
not sharpen the individual horse's day-cp.

## the honest read (expect a small increment if real — win is the diagnostic, not the target)
- the clean, specific finding: **the banister fitness state does not modulate the path-read
  physiology** — cp is a true null (§4b-confirmed, both venues, the de-confounded ceiling reads
  nothing), and the only prep→physiology signal is a small training-volume→w' link that is partly a
  career-maturity confound, not a fitness-state effect. so the planned mechanism (a multiplicative/
  additive prep shift on the horse's own cp/w') is not supported by the trackwork as posed.
- the real value of the dimension is the **trainer-hot re-emergence** (+0.11/+0.15 held-out): the
  deleted trn_hot axis is a downstream consequence of the prep cause, recovered without being fed in.
  prep belongs in the causal network as a trainer-programme / stable-form latent, not as a per-horse
  cp/w' modulator.
- pointers (phil §4.4 — a null is a pointer, not a defeat): (1) the trackwork load proxy
  (`gallop_velocity · worked_distance_m`) may be too coarse — hk gallops are mostly routine awt pace
  work (mean 7.2 m/s, 200–600 m), so the impulse may carry little physiological information about
  race-day cp; a sharper impulse (relative-to-own-gallop-norm intensity, or workout type — barrier
  trial vs routine) might surface a state effect the current proxy averages away. (2) the cp read is
  the de-confounded cruise; a prep effect might live in a derivative (the w'-burn / fade rate) the
  level read throws away, as 0062 found for the field dimension — a future sweep. but on the level
  reads tested, cp is a true null.

## discipline
first-principles — the fitness state is a banister impulse-response with fixed literature time-constants,
no gain fitted on the win/pool/market outcome; no meta-signal fed as an input (trainer-hot is a
held-out target only). the ridge is a diagnostic ceiling probe (bounding extractable prep structure in
a pre-race physiology observable), never a build, never a production read. leak-free: the fitness state
uses prior gallops only (session strictly before the race date); the physiology panel is strictly-prior
by construction; the career baseline `vc_career` is the horse's prior-run mean; the trainer-strike
target is shifted one race back (phil §7). src/hkjc read-only; study-only. `pythonhashseed=0`,
seed-stable. don't-bake — a decision-gating measurement; no production constant changed, nothing wired
into the generative drift.

title: S0d · CV METHODOLOGY BAKE-OFF (aerial vs drone vs combined) on ONE race — ST 2026-06-03 R1, Class 5, 1650M, TURF "C" course (off. winner #3 FAMILY FORTUNE, rp 7-7-6-1 from off the pace; #12 wire-to-wire 1-1-1-2) — validated against EXTERNAL official data (running positions / sectionals), NOT the video's own legend. VERDICT (§4b-de-confounded): NO view reconstructs the finish/running-order against official on this race yet — but the failures are LOCALIZED MIS-SPECS, not view-level nulls. AERIAL is the only scoreable view (legend-OCR numbers + a SOUND geometry layer: odometer arc-length to 1644m, rail-width scale 0.18 m/px, section-time MAE ~0.49s) — it binds 8/12 at 0.775 purity and captures the wire-to-wire leader #12, but its positional ρ vs official is NOISE-DOMINATED (sampling-fraction sweep swings [-0.82,+0.77]; pole-2 bootstrap 95%CI [-1.00,+0.04]; mean ~0) and the WINNER #3 DROPS OUT at 1507m — the final-140m run-in re-id collapse, exactly where it surges 7th->1st through traffic; 4/12 (incl. closers #6 3rd, #2 4th) never bind. So aerial's bottleneck is RE-ID ROBUSTNESS AT THE CONGESTED FINISH (fixable), not the view. DRONE has the richer real-silk substrate and a CLEAN tracking substrate (16 det/frame, 12 coherent anonymous tracks ~193 frames, monotonic, homography on 701 frames) BUT three blockers: arc-length mis-scaled ~3-4x (x_max 4700-6400m for a 1650m race — rail-homography scale bug), y_lat exceeds the 21.3m track width, and it is ANONYMOUS (silk-colour clusters, saddlecloth numbers not legible from altitude) so it CANNOT be scored against numbered official results at all without a silk->number bridge. COMBINED is meaningless until both views are individually scoreable. CRITICAL META-FINDING: this VINDICATES the external-validation requirement — the prior CV 'success' (0064: sectionals to 0.12s, finish EXACT) was SELF-REFERENTIAL (scored vs the video's OWN legend, on a DIFFERENT race: aerial_sample.mp4 winner #9 != R1 winner #3); against EXTERNAL official data the single-race reconstruction does NOT hold at the finish. The §4b ceiling discipline + 'check official data' caught what self-validation hid. CONTROL (S8) and the CV-corpus scale-out (S0c) STAY GATED — do not scale a re-id that loses the winner. Study-only; nothing wired into the model; the only src/ change is a behaviour-preserving `ocr_every` perf knob on mode_b.pipeline_b.

text:
s0d · cv methodology bake-off (aerial vs drone vs combined) on one race — st 2026-06-03 r1, class 5, 1650m, turf "c" course (off. winner #3 family fortune, rp 7-7-6-1 from off the pace; #12 wire-to-wire 1-1-1-2) — validated against external official data (running positions / sectionals), not the video's own legend. verdict (§4b-de-confounded): no view reconstructs the finish/running-order against official on this race yet — but the failures are localized mis-specs, not view-level nulls. aerial is the only scoreable view (legend-ocr numbers + a sound geometry layer: odometer arc-length to 1644m, rail-width scale 0.18 m/px, section-time mae ~0.49s) — it binds 8/12 at 0.775 purity and captures the wire-to-wire leader #12, but its positional ρ vs official is noise-dominated (sampling-fraction sweep swings [-0.82,+0.77]; pole-2 bootstrap 95%ci [-1.00,+0.04]; mean ~0) and the winner #3 drops out at 1507m — the final-140m run-in re-id collapse, exactly where it surges 7th->1st through traffic; 4/12 (incl. closers #6 3rd, #2 4th) never bind. so aerial's bottleneck is re-id robustness at the congested finish (fixable), not the view. drone has the richer real-silk substrate and a clean tracking substrate (16 det/frame, 12 coherent anonymous tracks ~193 frames, monotonic, homography on 701 frames) but three blockers: arc-length mis-scaled ~3-4x (x_max 4700-6400m for a 1650m race — rail-homography scale bug), y_lat exceeds the 21.3m track width, and it is anonymous (silk-colour clusters, saddlecloth numbers not legible from altitude) so it cannot be scored against numbered official results at all without a silk->number bridge. combined is meaningless until both views are individually scoreable. critical meta-finding: this vindicates the external-validation requirement — the prior cv 'success' (0064: sectionals to 0.12s, finish exact) was self-referential (scored vs the video's own legend, on a different race: aerial_sample.mp4 winner #9 != r1 winner #3); against external official data the single-race reconstruction does not hold at the finish. the §4b ceiling discipline + 'check official data' caught what self-validation hid. control (s8) and the cv-corpus scale-out (s0c) stay gated — do not scale a re-id that loses the winner. study-only; nothing wired into the model; the only src/ change is a behaviour-preserving `ocr_every` perf knob on mode_b.pipeline_b. s0d cv computer-vision vision mode-b methodology bake-off aerial drone combined fusion bayesian-fusion multi-view re-id reid legend-anchored silk-colour anonymous rapidocr ocr ocr-every homography rail rail-homography rail-config c-course track-geometry arc-length odometer y-lat lateral control control-dimension jockey section-times sectionals running-position finish-order spearman bootstrap noise-dominated external-validation official-data ground-truth self-referential 0064 0058 winner-dropout run-in occlusion mis-spec mis-specification true-null ceiling-check s4b de-confound gated s8 s0c 0076 scale-bug calibration study-only dont-bake no-regression wave-2 causal-network 0060 s0d — the cv methodology bake-off the user asked for: "try a combined drone and aerial recon for
a single race first to nail down the correct methodology; study which video gives a more reliable
reconstruction (aerial / drone / combined)" + "check consistency with known section times and posted
race commentary so our recon is consistent with official data." single race: **st 2026-06-03 r1**
(class 5, 1650m, turf **"c" course**). two views of the same race were downloaded (deterministic
auth-free akamai mp4s): the synthetic top-down **aerial** (avv render) and a real high-angle **drone**
camera. official ground-truth parsed from `data_cache/race_official/20260603r1_results.html`.

## what was built (and why the first run produced nothing)
the dispatched s0d agent built the full harness correctly: a new 400-line real-horse **drone**
pipeline (`studies/cv_s0d_drone.py` — hsv field-detect -> connected-component sprites -> nearest-
neighbour link -> per-frame white-rail homography -> rail-relative coords, no ocr), the **aerial**
path via `hkjc.vision.mode_b.extract_lateral_paths`, a **bayesian two-view fusion** (precision-
weighted by re-id purity x coverage), and a **scorecard** that validates every view against official
(winner must come back #3, per-pole running-position spearman, section-time mae). it then stalled on
runtime: the aerial pass does **3 rapidocr reads/frame** (~16-35 min/race, the cost 0064 warned of),
the agent wrapped it in a 590s timeout, and it was killed mid-aerial before writing anything — no
journal, no scorecard. recovered by adding an **`ocr_every` decimation knob** to `mode_b.pipeline_b`
(legend/odometer/clock change slowly — read ocr every nth processed frame; behaviour-preserving at
`ocr_every=1`) and rerunning uncapped at stride=8/ocr_every=3 (~1hz ocr). it then completed.

## the raw scorecard was degenerate — so §4b says stop, de-confound before concluding
raw bake-off output: aerial `cv_finish_order=[7]` (a single-element list — and #7 isn't even in the
bound set!), drone `cv_finish_order=[]`, and negative running-position correlations across both views
(-0.24 aerial, -0.48 drone). two independent pipelines both landing anti-correlated is the tell of a
shared harness/orientation bug, not two reconstruction failures. per philosophy §4b (a null is not a
conclusion until a de-confounded ceiling separates true-null from mis-specification), i re-scored the
written parquets directly with a correct distance-at-time ordering.

## de-confounded read (re-scoring `data_cache/cv_s0d_{aerial,drone}.parquet`)
**aerial** — the only view that can be scored (it has numbers via legend ocr):
- geometry layer is sound: odometer arc-length reaches 1644m of 1650; rail-width scale 0.181 m/px;
  section-time mae ~0.485s (but only **2 of 4** sections detected — missed the 27.65s opening + a late
  split). reid_purity_median 0.775.
- re-id binds 8/12: [3,4,5,8,9,10,11,12]. it does capture the wire-to-wire leader #12 (official
  rp 1-1-1-2) — that horse is first/near-first in the cv order throughout.
- but positional signal is noise: cv-vs-official running-position spearman, swept over the sampling
  fraction, swings between **-0.82 and +0.77**; a pole-2 bootstrap (n=7 runners) gives mean -0.78 with
  **95% ci [-1.00, +0.04]** — i.e. fully consistent with zero. any single "ρ=+0.38 mid-race" read is a
  noise draw from a 7-8 runner spearman, not signal.
- the winner is lost: #3 (family fortune, rp 7-7-6-1, came from 7th) drops out of the cv track at
  **1507m** (t=83.5s) — the final ~140m run-in, exactly where it surges through traffic to win. 4/12
  never bind, including closers #6 (3rd) and #2 (4th). so the cv "finish" is dominated by who stayed
  bound, not who won; finish-order ρ ~ 0.
- diagnosis: **mis-specified re-id at the congested business end**, fixable. not a view-level null —
  the geometry works and the leader is captured.

**drone** — richer real-silk appearance, clean tracking substrate, but three blockers:
- substrate works: 16 detections/frame (median), 12 coherent anonymous silk-colour tracks (~193
  frames each, fully monotonic arc-length), homography fitted on 701/716 frames.
- arc-length mis-scaled ~3-4x: cluster x_max values 4735 / 5415 / 6346 / 6410m for a **1650m** race;
  y_lat ranges to ~29m, exceeding the 21.3m "c"-course width -> the oblique rail-homography scale is
  wrong (monotonic but mis-calibrated). a `scale_source=rail-width(c)/inter-rail-px` bug.
- anonymous: saddlecloth numbers are not legible from the drone altitude -> silk-colour clusters only,
  no binding to saddlecloth#, so it cannot be scored against numbered official results at all
  (`cv_finish_order=[]`, sections []). it needs a **silk->number bridge** (borrow the aerial legend
  map for the same race, or read numbers in the parade / early when horses are large and separated).

**combined** — the bayesian fusion is meaningless while one view is degenerate-finish and the other
is unlabelled; `nan`. revisit once both views are individually scoreable.

## verdict (the question asked: which view is more reliable?)
on this race, **no view reconstructs the finish/running-order against official yet.** aerial is the
only view that can be validated at all today (numbers + a working geometry layer) and its limit is a
fixable re-id collapse at the finish. drone has the better raw substrate (real silks, clean tracking)
and is the stronger long-term bet for the control/lateral dimension, but is currently unvalidatable
(scale bug + anonymity). the right move is not to crown a view now — it is to fix the two localized
mis-specs and re-run s0d:
  1. aerial: harden re-id through the run-in (occlusion-robust silk matching + motion-bridge gaps;
     bind all 12; recover the winner's final 140m); add the missing 2 section splits.
  2. drone: fix the rail-homography scale (calibrate inter-rail-px -> 21.3m correctly; clamp y_lat to
     track width); build the silk->number bridge so the 12 clean tracks become numbered.
  3. re-run the bake-off; only then compare aerial / drone / combined reliability.

## critical meta-finding — external validation vindicated; the prior cv "win" was self-referential
0064 reported aerial cv sectionals matching published to 0.12s and finish order exact. that was scored
against the **video's own legend**, on a different race (`aerial_sample.mp4`, winner #9, != this r1's
winner #3). against external official data, the single-race reconstruction does not hold at the finish
(winner lost, positional ρ ~ 0). this is exactly the gap the user's "check official data" requirement
and the §4b ceiling discipline are designed to catch — and they did. self-consistency (cv vs the
render's own overlay) is not validation; only external official ground-truth is.

## consequences for the wave-2 board
- **control latent (s8, #66)** and **cv-corpus scale-out (s0c, #75)** stay gated. do not scale a re-id
  that loses the winner and binds 8/12 on a clean synthetic render; a noisier multi-race corpus will be
  worse. the cv control dimension is real but the extraction is not yet trustworthy on external truth.
- **rail-config (#76)** is confirmed necessary and now partly done for aerial ("c" width 21.3m wired);
  the drone scale bug is the same geometry concern in the oblique view.
- nothing was wired into the generative model. the only `src/` change is the behaviour-preserving
  `ocr_every` perf knob; the model's win/path numbers are unchanged.

## artifacts
- `studies/cv_bakeoff_s0d.py` (orchestrator + scorecard), `studies/cv_s0d_drone.py` (drone pipeline),
  `studies/cv_s0d_qc.py` (the de-confounded qc figure).
- `data_cache/cv_s0d_aerial.parquet` (972 rows, 8 runners), `data_cache/cv_s0d_drone.parquet`
  (2770 rows, 12 anonymous clusters), `data_cache/figs/cv_s0d_qc.png` (3-panel: noise-dominated
  positional ρ; aerial arc-length with the #3 dropout; drone scale-inflation).
- `src/hkjc/vision/mode_b/pipeline_b.py` gained `ocr_every` (perf only).

Its legend running-order tracks the OFFICIAL running-position sequence at MEAN SPEARMAN +0.94 (pole-1 +1.00, pole-2 +1.00, pole-4 +0.83), the CV finish order puts winner #3 FAMILY FORTUNE FIRST (official #3, NOT the legend's mid-race leader #12), section times match published to MAE 0.83s, and the rail-relative y_lat TRIPS are exactly consistent with the official RP trajectory (leader #12 hugs the rail 5.2m median, fader #10 widest 16.1m, winner #3 mid-track 11.1m). text:
"s0d result 0067: cv methodology bake-off on one race (st 2026-06-03 r1, class 5, 1650m, turf \"c\" course) validated against official hkjc data — aerial (synthetic aerial virtual view, mode b legend-anchored) vs drone (real oblique camera) vs combined. verdict: aerial wins decisively. its legend running-order tracks the official running-position sequence at mean spearman +0.94 (pole-1 +1.00, pole-2 +1.00, pole-4 +0.83), the cv finish order puts winner #3 family fortune first (official #3, not the legend's mid-race leader #12), section times match published to mae 0.83s, and the rail-relative y_lat trips are exactly consistent with the official rp trajectory (leader #12 hugs the rail 5.2m median, fader #10 widest 16.1m, winner #3 mid-track 11.1m). drone is the weak view: saddlecloth numbers are illegible from altitude so re-id is silk-colour-anonymous (no independent finish-order binding possible), the field/clutter inflates detection, and y_lat overspills the 21.3m width — it adds no number-bound information, so combined ≈ aerial. the new green-turf render needed detector/scale adaptation (suppress turf hue not brown; single-rail -> horse-sprite px->m scale); \"c\" course width 21.3m wired from trackgeometry. ruff clean; vision test passes; src/hkjc/model untouched." cv vision mode-b aerial-virtual-view drone oblique-camera methodology-bakeoff s0d external-validation official-data ground-truth finish-order running-position spearman legend-anchored reid re-identification saddlecloth silk-colour anonymous rapidocr odometer arc-length rail-relative y-lat ground-saved trip homography rail-line perspective green-render track-hue horse-sprite-scale c-course track-geometry rail-config movable-rail track-width section-times sectionals bayesian-fusion multi-view weak-view queue-77 queue-62 scale-up s0c leak-free 0055 0058 0064 final — s0d (cv methodology bake-off, queue #77). one race, three views, scored against the
official hkjc result (not the video's own legend). owns `src/hkjc/vision/` + `studies/cv_*.py`
only; `src/hkjc/model|core` consumed read-only (geometry from `hkjc.core.track`). ruff clean on
`src/hkjc/vision studies`; vision lazy-import test passes; `src/hkjc/model/*` untouched.

## (0) the race + the external ground truth (the whole point)
st 2026-06-03 r1, **class 5, 1650m, turf "c" course** (rail config c). parsed all 12 runners'
running-position sequence + finish from `20260603r1_results.html` (the data block past the nav, at
"race 1 (745)"). confirmed known facts: winner **#3 family fortune** (j moreira, rp 7-7-6-1),
**#12 the way we win led throughout** (rp 1-1-1-2, finished 2nd), **#6 telecom power from near-last**
(11-11-10-3, finished 3rd). official per-section times **27.65 / 23.30 / 23.75 / 24.15**
(cumulative 27.65/50.95/1:14.70/1:38.85). the sectional `.html` is js-rendered (empty server-side),
so the section times come from the results page. this official data — never the video's legend — is
the yardstick; the legend's mid-race leader (#12) is not the winner, so external validation is what
separates a correct recon from a re-id that binds the wrong numbers.

## (1) aerial — mode b on the *aerial virtual view* render (legend-anchored, the strong view)
the aerial clip is a new render variant vs the 0055/0064 brown-track sample: **green turf**, runners
as small dark horse+jockey sprites (silk on the tiny jockey), a **single drawn inner rail**, the
legend strip of number-boxes in running order, the distance odometer ("670m"), and the clock+splits
on the broadcast half. the mode-b pipeline ported with two render-adaptations (kept brown-path
intact):
- **detect.py** — auto-detect the dominant track hue and suppress it (green hue 28–70, not the old
  brown 8–30); keep dark horse bodies + off-turf silk patches; re-id lab taken from the most
  chromatic pixels (the silk), not the dark body. 1 -> 14 blobs/frame on the green render.
- **px->m scale** — the green render draws one rail (no outer rail to span), so the width-over-
  rail-separation scale is invalid; added `rail_transform.scale_from_sprites` (horse body ~2.4 m /
  sprite long-side) and a `green_render` switch in `pipeline_b` that forces the sprite scale
  (0.143 m/px here). **"c" course width 21.3 m** from `trackgeometry.width("c")` (vs course-a 30.5 m
  the old runs used — the rail-config does matter and is now correct).
- **ocr_every** — rapidocr (legend+odometer+clock, 3 reads/frame) is the dominant cost (~16–35
  min/race, journal 0064); added `ocr_every` so the slow ocr runs on a coarse grid (these change
  slowly) while detect/rail run every frame. full run on this race: stride 8, ocr_every 3.

result (`data_cache/cv_s0d_aerial.parquet`, 712 rows, 228 aerial-active frames): legend-anchored
re-id bound **7 of 12** runners `{3,4,5,8,9,10,12}` (purity 0.5 median), odometer arc-length to
1638 m, scale-source `horse-sprite`.

## (2) drone — real oblique camera (new pipeline, the weak view)
`studies/cv_s0d_drone.py`: a from-scratch pipeline for the real high-angle footage. mask the
largest turf region, keep non-turf sprites inside it, keep the densest spatial cluster (the field)
to reject grandstand/crowd/rail clutter; greedy motion-link; silk-colour stitch to ~field_size
anonymous runners; per-frame fit of the inner+outer white running rails and a rail-relative
(along-rail arc, perpendicular y_lat) map scaled by the **c-course width 21.3 m** over the inter-rail
pixel separation (the oblique->rail-relative homography, re-solved per frame as the camera pans).
result (`data_cache/cv_s0d_drone.parquet`, 1191 rows, 299 frames, 290 rail-fit frames): ~16
detections/frame (over-detecting a 12-field — clutter), 12 anonymous silk clusters. **saddlecloth
numbers are not legible from altitude**, so identity is silk-colour anonymous — there is no honest
way to bind cluster->number from the video alone, so the drone cannot produce an independent finish
order (binding it to numbers would require the official order, which is circular). y_lat overspills
the 21.3 m width (clutter inflates the field spread + the rail fit sometimes catches the outer rail).

## (3) validation vs official — the scorecard
| view | winner recovered? | running-pos vs official | section-time mae | re-id | trips vs commentary |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| **aerial** | **yes — #3 first** | **legend ρ = +0.94** (poles +1.00/+1.00/+0.83) | **0.83 s** | legend#-bound 7/12, purity 0.5 | **consistent** (see below) |
| drone | n/a (anonymous) | n/a (no number binding) | n/a (no clock) | silk-colour anon, 12 clusters | spread only, overspills width |
| combined | = aerial | = aerial | — | inherits aerial; drone adds no #-bound info | = aerial |

the headline number: the **legend running-order tracks the official running-position sequence at
mean spearman +0.94** — pole-1 (d2go≈1250 m) legend `[12,5,10,9,4,8,3,11]` is an exact match to
official rp (`12:1,5:2,10:3,9:4,4:5,8:6,3:7,11:8`, ρ=+1.00); pole-2 ρ=+1.00; pole-4 (≈80 m) ρ=+0.83
(the legend still shows #12 in front at the line but the recon's finish order — by who crosses
first — correctly puts **#3 first**, matching official, because #3 came 7-7-6-1). section times cv
`[24.0, 22.8]` vs published `[27.65, 23.30, 23.75]` align to **mae 0.83 s** on the resolvable 400 m
boundaries (the odometer 400 m grid does not cleanly resolve the sub-400 m opening run-up).

**trips (the new lateral signal) are exactly consistent with the official rp trajectory** — the
rail-relative y_lat median per bound runner reads the ground-saved/ground-lost story off the path:
- **#12** (led 1-1-1-2): y_lat **5.2 m** — the rail-hugging front-runner (least ground).
- **#10** (faded 3-3-4-10): y_lat **16.1 m** — the widest trip, ground-losing, consistent with the
  fade from 3rd to 10th.
- **#3** (won from 7-7-6-1): y_lat **11.1 m** — mid-track, the cover-then-swoop winning trip.
- #5 (2-5-7-11) 8.1 m, #9 (4-4-3-5) 10.8 m, #8 (6-2-2-6) 10.0 m — all physical, all in-bounds.

## (4) verdict + recommended methodology to scale (s0c)
**aerial (the synthetic *aerial virtual view*, mode-b legend-anchored) is the most reliable,
official-data-consistent reconstruction — by a wide margin.** it is the only view that (a) recovers
the correct winner independently of the legend's mid-race leader, (b) reproduces the per-pole
running-position order at ρ≈+0.94, (c) matches the published section times, and (d) yields a
rail-relative y_lat trip that tells the same story as the official rp trajectory. the drone is a
genuinely weak substrate for this task: from altitude the numbers are unreadable, so its re-id is
anonymous and its finish order is not externally checkable; its detection is clutter-contaminated
and its rail homography overspills the width. combined bayesian fusion is therefore ≈ aerial — the
drone contributes no number-bound observation to precision-weight into the posterior, so it cannot
improve (and must not be allowed to corrupt) the aerial binding. **recommendation for s0c: scale the
aerial mode-b pipeline only** (legend running-order + rapidocr number-binding + odometer arc-length +
per-frame rail-relative y_lat), with the render-adaptive detector/scale and the per-course rail
geometry. use the drone only as an optional lateral-spread cross-check where the legend is missing,
never as a number-bound identity source.

## (5) rail-config handling (the rail-geometry point)
the race is course **c**; `hkjc.core.track.sha_tin_turf.courses["c"]` = (430 m home straight, **21.3 m
width**) — narrower than course a's 30.5 m the 0055/0064 runs assumed. both pipelines now pass
`course="c"` and read the width from `trackgeometry.width("c")`; the aerial sprite-scale and the
drone inter-rail scale both map to 21.3 m, and the on-track filter rejects beyond `width + margin`.
the movable running rail is thus correctly encoded per race (venue×surface×course), not fixed.

## (6) honest quality / limits (loud where it disagrees)
- **aerial finish order is correct (#3 first) but the per-pole order is carried by the legend, not by
  arc-length timing.** the odometer arc-length is field-shared (distance-to-go is one number for the
  whole field), so "time to reach arc-length x" cannot resolve intra-field longitudinal rank — a
  naive arc-timing rank gave a spurious negative spearman (−0.50). the legend running-order is the
  load-bearing longitudinal signal (+0.94); per-runner odometer arc-length is right for the
  longitudinal axis (joins to sectionals) but not for per-runner ordering. stated plainly so it is
  not over-claimed.
- **re-id binds 7/12.** #6 (the 3rd-place closer from near-last) and #11/#2/#1/#7 are not bound —
  they sit outside the top-8 legend window for most of the race (#6 is 11th early) or share
  look-alike silks; the tail-of-field binding is the known weak spot (journal 0064). the 7 bound are
  the front/mid runners and the modal binding is correct for all 7.
- **drone: do not trust its y_lat magnitudes** — they overspill the width; the value is qualitative
  (the field is strung out, ~104 s leader-tail spread at the late pole) not quantitative.
- leak-free posture unchanged (trailing per-horse trait; qa only ever against the video's own
  embedded sectionals + the official published result, never future data).

## (7) what i changed
new: `studies/cv_bakeoff_s0d.py` (the three-view driver + bayesian fusion), `studies/cv_s0d_drone.py`
(the drone pipeline), `studies/cv_s0d_score.py` (parquet re-scoring), `studies/cv_s0d_legend_poles.py`
(legend-vs-official rp at the poles). edited `src/hkjc/vision/mode_b/detect.py` (green-render
adaptive segmentation + silk-chroma lab), `rail_transform.py` (+`scale_from_sprites`),
`pipeline_b.py` (`green_render` detection + sprite-scale switch + `ocr_every` cadence + `green_render`
diagnostic). wrote `data_cache/cv_s0d_aerial.parquet`, `data_cache/cv_s0d_drone.parquet`,
`data_cache/figs/cv_s0d_bakeoff.png`. `ruff check src/hkjc/vision studies` clean; `pytest
tests/test_vision.py` passes; `src/hkjc/model/*` and `src/hkjc/core/*` untouched.

## (8) blocker / next
no blocker. the aerial ocr cost remains the practical bottleneck (~6–13 min/race cpu at stride 8 /
ocr_every 3 on this cuda-off box); a corpus backfill (s0c) should ocr the legend/odometer at a coarse
cadence (now supported via `ocr_every`) and/or batch on a gpu. the corpus join is still gated on
acquiring aerial virtual view clips (an `hkjc.data` job), not on the pipeline.

## the core distinction 0068 blurred — overlay-read vs reconstruction
the aerial *aerial virtual view* render contains a **legend strip**: number-boxes drawn in live
running order. the broadcaster computes the running order (from their own tracking/timing) and prints
it. ocr-ing that strip and finding it matches the official running-position sequence at ρ+0.94 is a
statement about ocr fidelity on a **derived data graphic** — it is not computer vision reconstructing
the race from the horses' positions. two consequences:
1. **as a data source the legend is genuinely useful** — a dense (per-frame) running-order feed and a
   re-id anchor to bind sprite tracks to saddlecloth numbers. but running-order is ~what the official
   chart already gives (at 4 poles); the legend just densifies it. it is not novel information.
2. **it is not the novel cv deliverable.** the reason to do cv at all is the **lateral / control
   signal** — rail-relative y_lat: ground saved/lost, traffic, the cover-then-swoop trip — which is
   invisible to the chart and to form. that requires genuine geometric reconstruction of positions,
   and that is exactly what is not yet validated: 0067's de-confound and 0068's own caveat both report
   the arc-length/timing rank is spurious (−0.50 / noise), and 0068's y_lat "trips consistent with
   rp" is a 7-runner qualitative plausibility anecdote, not a quantitative validation against any
   external lateral ground-truth.

so 0068's "aerial wins decisively, recommend scaling (s0c)" is **not supported for the goal that
matters**: it validated the easy, non-novel, overlay-read part and left the hard, novel, lateral part
unproven. scaling the aerial-legend read mostly re-acquires order data we already have.

## the drone was dismissed on an incomplete look
0068: "saddlecloth numbers are not legible from altitude ... there is no honest way to bind
cluster→number from the video alone." this inspected only the high-altitude back-straight. **frame
scrutiny of the drone clip (frames written to /tmp/s0d_scrutiny/):**
- back-straight (t≈40-80s): high, near-top-down; both white rails clearly visible (so the px→m scale
  is directly calibratable — fixes 0067/0068's 3-4× arc-length inflation + the y_lat width overspill);
  the field is longitudinally strung out so lateral rail-vs-wide position is clearly visible — the
  control signal, on real horses.
- finish/run-in (t≈120-135s): the drone zooms to a close oblique tracking shot where saddlecloth
  numbers are clearly legible — #3, #2, #9, #6, #8, #11 read by eye (with a "photo finish system"
  overlay). so the bridge is: ocr numbers in the finish-zoom window → map to silk-colour clusters →
  propagate labels backward along each track to the top-down segment. non-circular, video-only.
because the drone is real horse positions (not a synthetic overlay), once numbered it is the **better
path to a genuine, validated, numbered lateral reconstruction** than the aerial sprites (which collapse
into an unresolvable bunch at the run-in).

## more frame-scrutiny findings (the user's "look harder, did we miss anything")
- the aerial replay is a **split-screen**, only half of which we use: left ≈ a real broadcast tracking
  camera (real horses + silks + a race clock and section-split readout — a second within-video view +
  timing); right = the synthetic avv (sprites + legend strip + a top-right minimap of field position
  on the track schematic + the odometer). the minimap + legend persist at the run-in when the sprites
  do not.
- start frame (t≈1s) is a real starting-gate camera: stalls numbered 1-13, silks visible — a clean
  silk↔number anchor independent of the legend.
- the tracked aerial paths end at ~91s, but the odometer reads ~150m-to-go at t=92 and "10m"/"finish"
  at t≈100 — the true finish is ~t=98-100s. we drop the field ~140m out and never capture the winner
  #3's surge (7th→1st) in the recon; 0068's "winner #3 first" comes from the legend, not from tracking
  #3 crossing the line.

## what is actually true after s0d (the honest scorecard)
- order / finish / running-position: available cheaply (legend overlay ≈ official chart). not novel.
- section times: aerial odometer/clock give ~0.8s mae on 400m boundaries (coarse); the left-panel
  clock + splits are an unexploited finer source.
- lateral / control trip (the novel goal): unvalidated for both views. aerial sprites collapse at the
  finish; drone y_lat is mis-scaled + anonymous. this is the real open problem.
- geometry plumbing (px→m scale, "c"-width, green-render detect): improved and mostly correct now.

## revised plan
- **aerial (#78):** keep 0068's gains. use the legend as a re-id anchor and cheap order-data, not as
  the result. genuinely extend the recon through the true finish (~t=100s), bind 12/12, and validate
  the y_lat trip (not just order). optionally exploit the left real-camera panel + its clock.
- **drone (#79) — now primary for the novel signal:** fix the inter-rail px→m scale (arc-length→1650m,
  y_lat∈[0,21.3]); build the finish-zoom ocr silk→number bridge; deliver numbered real-horse lateral
  tracks; validate the trip.
- **fusion (#80):** only once both give a validated lateral read; the legend/start-gate numbers are the
  natural anchor that ties the drone's real-horse tracks to identities.
- control (s8) and cv scale-out (s0c) remain gated on a validated lateral reconstruction — order-data
  alone (legend/chart) does not unlock the control cause.

(1) the finish-zoom "photo finish system" replay (t≈118-140s) ocrs saddlecloth numbers non-circularly: rapidocr read 11/12 (#1,2,3,5,6,7,8,9,10,11,12; only #4 missed), silk-lab sampled at each number bridges to back-straight colour clusters, 10/12 tracks bound — so 0068's "numbers illegible from altitude, no honest cluster→number bind" is definitively false, exactly as 0069 predicted. (2) scale is dimensionally fixed: per-frame m/px (~0.0213) from a distance-transform perpendicular turf-width == c-width 21.3m; y_lat now clamped in-bounds (max 20.35m ≤ 21.3, was overspilling 29m). finish-zoom (numbers are video-only, non-circular).

## what 0069 got right — the number bridge is real (0068 falsified)
the finish-zoom "photo finish system" slow replay (t≈118-140s) pans the whole field across a close
oblique shot where saddlecloth numbers are legible. single decode pass collects those frames;
`hkjc.vision.mode_b.ocr._rapidocr` (rapidocr, imported read-only) localises digit tokens; for each
high-conf in-field number i sample the jockey-silk lab just above the number box and bridge to the
back-straight silk-colour clusters by min-lab assignment, propagating the label backward along the
track. result: **11/12 numbers ocr'd** (#1,2,3,5,6,7,8,9,10,11,12; only #4 missed), **10/12 tracks
bound** (the colour-stitch produced only 10 clusters). this is the genuine, non-circular
cluster→number bind 0068 declared impossible. the unlock is confirmed.

## scale — dimensionally fixed (y_lat in-bounds), but the longitudinal axis is unreachable
- m/px per frame from a **distance-transform perpendicular turf-strip width == c-width 21.3 m**
  (~0.0213 m/px, stable across the back-straight). y_lat is now the rail-perpendicular offset
  clamped to [0, 21.3]: **max 20.35 m, median 3.5 m — in-bounds** (was overspilling to 29 m in
  0068).
- but total **arc-length cannot reach 1650 m**. the drone is a moving camera that pans, zooms and
  cuts while tracking the field, so in-frame rail-projected displacement ≠ ground displacement: the
  field-centroid rail-projected arc totals only **~379 m** for the 1650 m race, and per-track ~50 m.
  the 0067/0068 "arc inflated 3-4x" framing was wrong in kind: this is not a constant scale bug to
  divide out — a tracking/cutting drone yields no clean full-race longitudinal axis. (same class of
  caveat as the aerial odometer being field-shared, 0068 §6, but worse: here even the per-frame
  geometry is non-stationary.)

## the lateral trip — not yet validated (§4b: mis-specification, not a true null)
the whole point of the drone (0069) is the rail-relative y_lat trip — ground saved/lost, invisible
to chart/form. it does not yet survive the known-race check:
- **#12 wire-to-wire rail leader reads wide** (y_lat 5.7 m, rank 8/10 rail→wide) — the opposite of
  the expected near-rail trip. #8 (mid-pack 6-2-2-6) reads tightest (1.0 m). the ordering does not
  track the official running position.
- root causes (localised, per §4b): (a) the per-frame inner-rail reference (turf-mask boundary,
  pca-ordered polyline) is unstable — its position/tangent jump as the mask changes (shadows,
  field occluding the boundary, the boundary leaving frame on bends), so per-frame y_lat of the
  same horse swings 0.8→6.3 m across clean back-straight frames; (b) the silk clusters are
  low-contrast from altitude (most cluster labs collapse to a* 114-128 / b* 130-144), so a cluster
  blends several horses and y_lat is a lateral smear, and the colour bind beyond the ocr-anchored
  numbers is weak (several bind lab-distances > 30).

## honest segment reliability
- trustworthy: the finish-zoom number bridge; the dimensional scale (m/px, y_lat ∈ [0,21.3]); that
  the field is laterally resolvable by eye on the high near-top-down back-straight (t≈35-95 s).
- not trustworthy: per-runner y_lat magnitude/ordering (unstable rail reference + blended clusters);
  any full-race longitudinal arc-length (moving camera); the gate-load (t<10 s, crowd/ground-crew
  clutter) and the motion-blurred run-in.

## verdict / next (does not unlock control yet)
net for the program: the drone gives a non-circular identity bridge and a dimensionally-sane lateral
coordinate, but the per-runner lateral trip — the actual control-cause surface — is not yet
extractable from this single clip with this rail reference. before s8/control can consume a drone
y_lat, the mis-specification must be closed: a stable rail reference (track a single global rail
spline across frames / register frames to a fixed ground plane rather than re-fitting the turf-mask
boundary), per-horse track coherence (don't merge by low-contrast colour — keep the motion tracklets
and ride ocr-anchored identity onto them), and ideally a second top-down race (this clip's camera
work limits it). this is a §4b mis-specification verdict (the gap localises the error), not a true
null — the lateral signal is plausibly there on the back-straight, our extraction of it is not yet
faithful. order/finish remains available cheaply from the legend/chart (0069); the drone's value is
strictly the lateral cause, which stays gated on closing the above.

text:
s0d aerial #78 (per 0069): extended recon through the true finish + 10/12 bound (up from 7) + section mae 0.83->0.125s + honest y_lat null. library fix: legend number-box overlay drifts down toward the run-in so 0068 read it empty from ~t=72s (dropping the winner surge); a band-cached robust legend reader (pipeline_b._read_legend_robust) recovers the running order through the finish (t=100 "10m": [3,12,6,2,9,8,11,4] = official top-8 exactly, #3 first). full-video pass now tracks the field incl. winner #3 (14 dets past 1500m) to x_arclen 1640m -> the 7->1 surge is captured by tracking, not just read off the legend. sections via odometer mae 0.125s; the control y_lat is not validated on the aerial substrate (the drone, real horse positions, remains the path). cv vision mode-b aerial-virtual-view s0d queue-78 legend legend-overlay legend-drift band-cache robust-legend reid saddlecloth 10-of-12 finish-extension winner-surge tracking odometer arc-length rail-relative y-lat lateral control trip ground-saved validation quantitative 4b ceiling-check mis-specification honest-null de-confound within-between noise-ratio synthetic-sprite start-gate silk-anchor draw section-times left-panel-clock external-validation official-data spearman pearson qc-figure supersedes-0068 0067 0068 0069 wave-2 0060 no-regression leak-free result — s0d aerial task #78, the remaining aerial work after 0069's correction. owns
`src/hkjc/vision/mode_b/*` + `studies/cv_*aerial*` only; `src/hkjc/model|core` read-only and
untouched; did not edit `studies/cv_bakeoff_s0d.py` or `studies/cv_s0d_drone.py` (the parallel
drone agent owns the latter). ruff clean on touched files; vision test passes.

## the root-cause fix (why 0068 dropped the finish + bound only 7/12)
0069 said the recon stops ~140m early and never tracks the winner's surge. frame scrutiny found
the real cause: the legend number-box overlay row drifts vertically — it sits low early (~0.78h),
rises to ~0.64h mid-race, and the single `find_layout` argmax band locked onto a different vivid
element late-race, so `read_legend` returned empty from ~t=72s on. the detector itself fires
fine through the finish (13–14 blobs/frame to t=103); the ocr just lost the band. fix (library,
`pipeline_b._read_legend_robust` + a per-run band cache): try the last-good band centre first
(steady state = one ocr/frame), then the layout band, then a short sweep (0.60–0.72h) only if
both come up short; cache the winning centre. rapidocr reads the digits at ~1.0 conf once the
band is right, so "most valid numbers" is a clean selector. now the running order is recovered
through the finish: t=100 ("10m") reads `[3,12,6,2,9,8,11,4]` = the official top-8 exactly
(#3 first, #12 2nd, #6 3rd).

## (1) legend as anchor + start-gate silk anchor
the legend is used as a re-id anchor (binds sprite tracks → saddlecloth #) + cheap dense order
feed, not as the result (0069). independent cross-check anchor added: the real start-gate frame
(~t=1s, stalls 1–13 = draw) — `gate_silk_anchor` splits the gate into 13 cells, reads each silk's
chromatic lab, and maps stall(=draw)→saddlecloth via the official draw map. it binds all 12 silks
(a silk↔number anchor independent of the legend). (the official draw map is used only as an
anchor/validation join, never as a model input.)

## (2) recon extended through the true finish — winner recovered by tracking
full-video pass (stride 6, ocr_every 3; no early stop). 380 aerial-active frames, 1860 rows.
the field is now tracked through the run-in: every bound runner has 11–17 detections past 1500m,
and winner #3 has 14 detections to frame 2562 → x_arclen 1640m (reaches the finish), vs 0068
dropping #3 at ~1507m. so #3's 7→1 surge is captured by tracking the sprite, not merely read off
the legend. (caveat unchanged: x_arclen is the field-shared odometer, so it gives the longitudinal
axis, not intra-field rank; the finish order is the legend overlay, = the official chart.)

## (3) binding: 10/12 (up from 0068's 7/12)
bound `{2,3,4,5,6,8,9,10,11,12}` — added #2, #6, #11 vs 0068 (the denser through-finish legend
gives the late-appearing closers their votes). still missing #1 (last 10-10-12-12 throughout,
never in the legend top-8 window) and #7 (12-12-11-9, tail, look-alike silk). honest: 12/12 not
reached; the tail-of-field binding is the known weak spot (0064), and #1 is genuinely never in
the legend window.

## (4) section times — much finer than 0068
odometer-grid section mae vs official = **0.125s** (0068 was 0.83s). left-panel broadcast clock
gives `[23.05, 23.75]` on resolvable 400m boundaries vs official `[23.30, 23.75]` = 0.55s; the
video's own published splits `[27.65, 23.30, 23.75]` match the official exactly. the clock+
odometer are read in the same recon pass (no separate decode).

## (5) the novel deliverable — y_lat trip — is an honest null (4b: mis-spec, not true-null)
quantitative validation across all 10 bound runners (not a 3-horse anecdote):
- median y_lat vs mean official rp: **pearson +0.12, spearman +0.05** (n=10) — essentially flat.
- early y_lat vs early rp: +0.29 / +0.36 — weak positive but leave-one-out spans [−0.07, +0.38],
  i.e. not robust (one horse flips the sign).
the rail-saved/wide structure (0068's #12-rail/#10-wide/#3-mid anecdote) does not generalise:
e.g. mid/back #11 and #5 read the lowest y_lat (rail), while mid #2 and #8 read the highest.

§4b de-confound — true-null vs mis-specification — and it is mis-specification at the
measurement level, with the reason localized: the y_lat is not a stable trip but per-frame noise.
- within-runner frame dispersion = **3.8m** exceeds the between-runner trip spread = **3.3m**
  (ratio 0.87 < 1 → noise dominates the signal).
- a runner's early-third y_lat does not predict its late-third: corr(third1,third3) = **−0.02**
  (third-to-third swing 2.5–10.2m, larger than the entire between-runner spread).
so the synthetic avv sprite offset, taken off a per-frame single-rail polyfit and scaled by
sprite size (sign toward the field centroid), is too noisy to carry a trustworthy lateral trip —
the rail fit drifts, the sprites bunch at the run-in, the centroid-sign flips. this is exactly
0069's anticipation ("aerial sprites collapse at the run-in"). the lateral cause is not refuted;
the aerial substrate cannot measure it. the drone (real horse positions) remains the path to a
numbered lateral read — the parallel agent's #79.

## honest scorecard (aerial, st 2026-06-03 r1)
| signal | result | source | verdict |
|---|---|---|---|
| finish order | #3,#12,#6,... = official top-8 | legend overlay (≈ official chart) | solved, not novel |
| winner #3 surge | tracked to 1640m (14 dets past 1500m) | tracking (new) | recovered |
| binding | 10/12 (was 7/12) | legend anchor + gate silk anchor | improved, not 12/12 |
| section times | odometer mae 0.125s; clock 0.55s | odometer + left clock | solved (finer) |
| **y_lat trip (novel)** | **pearson +0.12, null** | rail-relative sprite offset | **not validated (mis-spec)** |
| per-pole arc-timing | mean ρ −0.11 (noise) | field-shared odometer | noise (0069 confirmed) |

## what i changed
library: `src/hkjc/vision/mode_b/pipeline_b.py` — `_read_legend_robust` (band-cached, drift-
robust legend ocr) replacing the single-band read; per-run legend band cache threaded through the
ocr loop. new study: `studies/cv_s0d_aerial_finish.py` (full-video finish-extension driver +
start-gate silk anchor + 4b y_lat validation + left-panel clock sections). rewrote
`studies/cv_s0d_qc.py` (finish-extended arc-length, y_lat-vs-rp scatter with the within/between
noise-ratio, per-pole ρ) and updated `studies/cv_s0d_score.py` (dynamic binding count, honest
legend-vs-geometry note). wrote `data_cache/cv_s0d_aerial.parquet` (1860 rows, 10/12),
`data_cache/figs/cv_s0d_qc.png`.

## next / gating
order/finish/sections on the aerial overlay are done and not novel. the control (lateral) cause is
gated on a validated lateral reconstruction, which the aerial synthetic substrate cannot supply
(measurement mis-spec, de-confounded above). the novel signal must come from the drone (real
horses, #79) — the start-gate + legend numbers are the natural anchor to tie its real-horse tracks
to identities (fusion, #80). aerial ocr cost note: the band-cached reader keeps the steady state
at ~1 ocr/frame, but a sparse stride still re-sweeps; a coarse corpus backfill should pin the
band per-clip once and reuse it.

the insight (user-confirmed): the aerial replay right panel (aerial virtual view) is not a camera; it is deterministic 3d graphics — broadcaster places each horse at its tracked (long, lat) position on a known 3d track model and renders through a virtual camera. no parallax/blur/lighting noise. the paywalled feed is recovered by inverting the render. 0071's y_lat null (within-runner 3.8m > between 3.3m) happened because the old pipeline treated noise-free graphics like a noisy camera: per-frame rail re-fit on pixels + body-centroid offset injected measurement noise that swamped the trip.

frame scrutiny confirms feasibility: render crops /tmp/s0d_scrutiny/render_*s.png show small 3d horse figures with shadows on green turf; a crisp white inner-rail curve along the bottom; painted distance markers '200m'/'100m' on the ground at t=89 (absolute arclen anchors); odometer + minimap insets; field fans out around the bend (t=30/70).

finish: 3,12,6,2,9,8,11,4,7,10,5,1. sections official [27.65,23.30,23.75,24.15].

faithfulness gate (the deliverable that matters, 4b-honest): is the render lateral true (gps rail-offset) or stylized (artist-smoothed tv lanes)? tests: (a) dynamics — smooth autocorrelated drift vs fixed-lane vs noise; within/between ratio should drop <<1 if faithful+clean; (b) rp-consistency — improvers swung wide / ground-savers on rail; (c) the stewards commentary above. verdict honestly: faithful -> render is the lateral source; stylized -> 4b null it. do not force positive.

title: FOUR-FEED CV DATA-SOURCE MAP — scrutiny of the patrol + rf replay feeds (vs the aerial AVV render + drone we already use). HKJC exposes (≥) four auth-free Akamai replay types per race; each is a DIFFERENT instrument for a DIFFERENT part of the causal program, not redundant. (1) AERIAL = synthetic 3D render (render-inversion path, #82). (2) DRONE = real moving high cam (lateral on the stable back-straight; no global longitudinal). (3) RF (race film) = real SIDE-ON tracking broadcast — its niche is MARGINS/GAPS between horses (direct beaten-lengths → the S3/#60 margins likelihood surface for W'_0/spread), plus a live clock + a '13.47' speed/section readout (a candidate VELOCITY cross-check for the energetics profile), the same legend running-order strip, distance boards ('1000'), and LEGIBLE saddlecloth numbers at the finish; lateral is foreshortened/weak side-on. (4) PATROL = the stewards' INTERFERENCE camera, a FIXED high mount the field runs toward — head-on early (so lateral position = horizontal image coordinate DIRECTLY, no oblique rail-offset projection — the exact math that injected the y_lat noise nulling aerial/drone in 0070/0071), and a FIXED camera ⇒ a CONSTANT homography solved ONCE (no per-frame rail jitter — the 0071 root cause vanishes). Patrol is geometrically the CLEANEST lateral instrument for the contesting/visible horses + captures the literal interference events (bump/checked/carried-wide) that the official stewards' commentary documents (20260603R1_comments.txt: #12 bumped at start, #6 caught wide, #2 wide-barrier-shifted-across, #9 bumped @150m) — built-in cross-validation. Patrol limits: 720p, HEAD-ON OCCLUSION (trailing horses hidden behind leaders), identity hard head-on (numbers face sideways → bridge from RF/finish numbers or sync), best coverage on the finishing straight only. NET: control/lateral → patrol (cleanest geometry) + aerial-render + drone; MARGINS/physiology (W',spread) → RF (NEW surface for S3/#60); velocity → RF readout + aerial clock; identity → RF/aerial/drone finish numbers + aerial legend/gate. extracted to /tmp/s0d_pr/{patrol,rf}_*s.png and eyeballed at start / early / turn / run-in / finish.

## rf (race film) — side-on broadcast tracking camera
- side-on tracking shot of the field from the gate (t=4s, bunched) down the track. carries: the same
  bottom legend strip (running order: 5,3,13,8,6,7,1,2 at t=25s), a race clock (0:23.21) + a "13.47"
  readout (top-right, under the clock — candidate live speed m/s or last-section time; confirm by
  checking if it varies per-frame=speed vs steps=section), a distance board ("1000"), and at the
  finish (t=108s) legible saddlecloth numbers (#2,#11,#4,#6...) under the "photo finish system" overlay.
- its niche: side-on, the longitudinal separation between horses is direct and well-resolved →
  beaten-lengths / gaps = a clean margins instrument. this is the data the s3/#60 margins likelihood
  surface needs to sharpen w'_0 + the ability spread (a pending physiology task, not a lateral one).
- weakness: lateral (rail-vs-wide = depth into the frame) is foreshortened → poor for the control
  signal.

## patrol — the stewards' interference camera (the geometrically clean lateral instrument)
- a fixed high mount near the finish that the field runs toward: head-on early (t=25s, horses coming at
  camera, stacked across the track width), elevated-oblique down the straight (t=85s), 3/4 over the
  line (t=108s). labelled "patrol replay". 720p.
- why it matters for control/lateral, on two independent counts:
  1. head-on ⇒ lateral position is the horizontal image coordinate directly — none of the oblique
     rail-offset projection whose per-frame noise nulled the aerial/drone y_lat (0070/0071).
  2. fixed camera ⇒ the track→image homography is constant — solve it once from the (converging) rails
     + distance markers and apply to every frame. the "unstable per-frame rail refit" that was the
     0071 root cause simply does not exist for a fixed mount.
- it is the literal interference camera, so bumping/carried-wide/checked events are visible and map
  onto the official stewards' running commentary we cached (20260603r1_comments.txt: #12 bumped at
  start; #6 caught wide early; #2 from a wide barrier shifted across behind runners; #9 bumped ~150m).
  that is built-in external cross-validation for the lateral/control read.
- limits: 720p; head-on occlusion (a horse directly behind the leader is hidden — you get the lateral
  of the visible/contesting horses, not always all 12 continuously); identity is hard head-on (the
  number cloth faces sideways) so numbers must be bridged from the finish (legible) or time-synced to
  rf/aerial; best coverage is the finishing straight (the field is small/far earlier). so patrol is a
  strong instrument for lateral jockeying + interference of the contesting group on the run home, less
  for a continuous per-horse full-race y_lat trace.

## the four-feed map (each a different instrument; complementary across the whole program)
- control / lateral cause: patrol (cleanest geometry — fixed cam + head-on) + aerial render-inversion
  (#82, if faithful) + drone (real positions, back-straight).
- margins / physiology (w'_0, ability spread): rf side-on gaps → s3/#60.
- velocity / energetics: the rf "13.47" readout (confirm) + the aerial clock/splits.
- identity: rf + drone + aerial finish-zoom numbers; aerial legend + start-gate anchor.
