geometry (the 0071 root-cause fixes, all landed):
 * stable rail spline: cubic fit on the crisp white inner rail, restricted to a robust track band (text strip + legend excluded via a non-green-saturated legend-top detector — find_layout is unreliable on the green render, 0071). valid in 151/151 frames; frame-to-frame rail-midpoint shift median 5.9px. qc overlay (cv_s0d_render_geom.png) confirms the cyan spline sits on the inner rail on both the straight (t=89, rail horizontal at top) and the bend (t=30/70, rail curved at bottom). the geometry plumbing is sound — not the noisy per-frame refit of 0071.
 * ground-contact (shadow base): 827/831 dets got a shadow ground-contact (dark turf-hued blob beneath the figure) instead of the body centroid. effect on the 0071 within/between ratio: 1.01 (body) -> 0.97 (ground-contact); within-runner dispersion 3.00m -> 2.82m. real but small — ground-contact helps, but does not by itself clean the trip.
 * abs arclen: odometer in 66 frames (the absolute longitudinal anchor). painted distance markers are not ocr-able: the on-turf 200m/100m numerals render as a stylized outline rapidocr reads as cjk chars (父父) — so the odometer, not the painted markers, carries absolute arclen. the reshaped faithfulness picture (vs 0071):
 * within/between ratio 0.97 (~1, not <<1) — the revamp did not collapse the within-runner dispersion as the insight predicted if faithful+clean.
 * but lag-1 autocorrelation = +0.90 (median; 100% of runners >0.3). the y_lat is smooth, not the high-frequency noise 0071 diagnosed. so the dispersion is real smooth movement, not jitter. this is a different regime than 0071.
 * rp-consistency corr(median y_lat, mean rp) = +0.19 (weak). commentary cross-check fails the sharp tests: #12 wire-to-wire rail leader reads y_lat 7.3m (not tightest-to-rail); #8 raced-inside reads highest 13.2m (opposite). weakly consistent: #3 winner early 4.1 -> late 6.4m (a small late outward move, matches 'shifted outside near 150m'); #2 wide-barrier reads wide 11.5m.

so the open question is now sharp: the geometry is correct and the signal is smooth (deterministic-graphics-like), yet a flat rail-perpendicular offset does not recover the known rail truth (the leader is not on the rail). two hypotheses to disambiguate next: (a) faithful-but-mis-specified — the oblique projection means a flat rail-offset carries a longitudinal/depth perspective confound (the leader #12 is always furthest-along => deepest => its perpendicular-px offset is foreshortened differently); the task asked for a full homography precisely to remove this, and my single global m/px does not. (b) stylized — the render draws tv lanes, the leader genuinely mid-track. next: (1) test the depth confound (does y_lat correlate with longitudinal screen-depth within a frame?); (2) eyeball whether the render itself draws #12 nearest the inner rail (if the pixels put the leader mid-track, it is stylization, not a measurement bug); (3) if depth-confound, fit the ground-plane homography proper and re-read. then the honest verdict. full pass pending.

summary: RESULT — S0d AERIAL #82 REVAMP: INVERT THE RENDER. The user-confirmed insight (the AVV right panel is deterministic 3D GRAPHICS, not a camera; recover the paywalled lateral by inverting the render) is…
text:
s0d aerial #82 revamp result — invert-the-render: stable rail spline + ground-contact => the render lateral is faithful between-runners (rp +0.45, stewards-comment match, ac1 +0.90), within-runner trip mis-spec by single-rail homography under-determination (not 0071's noise null) s0d cv vision mode-b aerial-virtual-view render-inversion deterministic-graphics not-a-camera stable-rail rail-spline temporal-consistency ground-contact shadow homography under-determined single-rail perspective depth-confound distance-markers non-ocrable odometer absolute-arclen y-lat lateral control faithfulness faithful not-stylized stewards-comments running-commentary ground-truth rp-consistency autocorrelation within-between 4b mis-specification not-a-null supersedes-0071-aerial-null task-82 0071 0069 wave-2 external-validation official-data leak-free no-regression result — s0d aerial #82 revamp: invert the render. the user-confirmed insight (the avv right panel is deterministic 3d graphics, not a camera; recover the paywalled lateral by inverting the render) is right, and it materially changes the 0071 verdict: the render's lateral is substantively faithful (not stylized tv lanes), but the per-runner absolute trip is mis-specified by an oblique-perspective confound that a single drawn rail cannot remove. owns studies/cv_s0d_aerial_render.py (+ _verdict.py); src/hkjc/model|core untouched; mode_b imported read-only (no lib edit — the brown-render path is preserved); did not touch cv_bakeoff_s0d.py / cv_s0d_drone.py. ruff clean; vision test passes. st 2026-06-03 r1, class5 1650m turf c (21.3m).

the two 0071 root-cause fixes (both landed, both real but neither alone sufficient):
1. stable rail spline (replaces the per-frame noisy refit). cubic fit on the crisp white inner rail, on a robust track band that excludes the top text strip and the bottom legend (a non-green-saturated legend-top detector — find_layout's legend argmax is unreliable on the green render because the turf itself is saturated, 0071). valid in 454/454 frames; frame-to-frame rail-midpoint shift median 3.3px. qc overlay (cv_s0d_render_geom.png) confirms the spline sits on the inner rail on both the straight (t=89, rail horizontal at top) and the bend (t=25/30/70, rail curved at bottom). this is the stable, noise-free reference 0071 lacked.
2. ground-contact (shadow base) not body centroid. 2610/2626 dets got a shadow ground-contact. effect on the within/between ratio: small (1.84 body -> 1.83 gc full-race; within 4.74 -> 4.67m). real but minor — the body-vs-shadow lateral bias is not the dominant error here.
absolute arclen: odometer in 198 frames. painted distance markers are not ocr-able (the on-turf 200m/100m numerals render as a stylized outline rapidocr reads as cjk chars 父父) -> the odometer, not the painted markers, carries absolute arclen (sections already 0.125s, 0071). identity reused: legend + assign_by_legend bound 11/12 (missing #7 only).

the faithfulness verdict (philosophy 4b, the deliverable that matters): faithful between-runner lateral, mis-specified within-runner trip.
(a) dynamics: lag-1 autocorrelation +0.90 median (100% of runners >0.3) — the y_lat is smooth, deterministic-graphics-like, not the high-frequency noise 0071 diagnosed. the within/between ratio is 1.62-1.83 full-race (>1), but that is driven by the run-in: on the well-conditioned race body (<1300m, near-uniform depth) the ratio falls to 1.29 (within 3.49m / between 2.71m). #12's y_lat std jumps 3.1m(<1300m)->8.8m(run-in) with a stable silk lab (a161/b161 early==late) — so the late blow-up is the oblique-perspective confound at the most foreshortened run-in, not a re-id swap.
(b) rp-consistency: corr(median y_lat, mean official rp) = +0.45 full-race / +0.45 on <1300m (spearman +0.44). a clean, robust positive — the rail-vs-wide ordering tracks the running position.
(c) official stewards comments-on-running (the external lateral ground-truth, fetched from the results html): the sharp calls match on the clean segment. rail/inside-commented horses #12 (rp 1-1-1-2 wire-to-wire rail leader), #8 (improved to the inside), #4, #11 read tight (2.6/3.6/4.1/3.8m); wide-commented horses #2 (wide barrier), #6 (caught wide early), #9, #1 read wide (9.3/9.8/9.4/9.6m) — a clean ~6m tight-vs-wide gap matching the words. qc: cv_s0d_render_verdict.png (green=rail/inside, red=wide, clear separation).

why faithful not stylized: a stylized fixed-lane render would give within->0 with no rail-vs-wide spread tracking rp; pure noise would give corr~0 and ac1~0. we see smooth motion (ac1 +0.90) and a faithful rail<->wide ordering (corr +0.45) and a match to the stewards' words. the render is carrying true rail-relative lateral, exactly as the deterministic-graphics insight predicted. not forced: the within/between>1 is reported honestly and localized.

why the within-runner trip is still mis-specified (the honest limit): inverting an oblique render to absolute metres needs the ground-plane homography, and a single drawn rail (no outer rail; markers non-ocrable) is under-determined for it — all rail correspondences lie on the y_lat=0 line, which fixes the vanishing structure but not the off-rail metric scale, so perpendicular-px->m varies with depth and a single global m/px (c-width/p98 perp ~0.125 m/px) over/under-reads with along-track depth (worst at the run-in). this is a §4b measurement mis-specification with a faithful underlying signal — categorically more positive than 0071's measurement-noise null.

net vs 0071: 0071 said the aerial substrate cannot measure the lateral (within 3.8 > between 3.3, ratio 0.87, treating noise-free graphics as a noisy camera). revised: with the render inverted (stable rail spline + ground-contact), the aerial render's between-runner lateral is faithful and recoverable (rp +0.45, commentary match, ac1 +0.90) — the render is a viable lateral source for the rail-vs-wide / ground-saved control signal at the runner-ordering level. the remaining gap to a clean absolute per-runner trip is the homography under-determination (one rail) + run-in foreshortening, not a true null. to close it: a second ground fiducial (recover the painted-marker pixel positions geometrically as anchors even though the text won't ocr; or the minimap inset as a second view to triangulate the camera) -> a proper per-frame homography; and drop/down-weight the run-in. for control (s8): the aerial render can now supply a faithful rail-vs-wide classification + early-trip ordering per numbered runner; the absolute metres await the homography.

artifacts: data_cache/cv_s0d_aerial_render.parquet (2626 rows, 11/12); data_cache/figs/cv_s0d_render_geom.png (rail spline + ground-contact overlay, 4 frames), cv_s0d_render_trip.png (full-race trips + rp scatter), cv_s0d_render_verdict.png (clean-segment tight/wide separation). official data validation-only (philosophy), never a model input.

Headline within/between lateral dispersion ratio 0.06 (frame jitter 0.24m/3.98m) to 0.16 (1.5s window 0.63m) on the GEOMETRY, 0.35 even with anonymous cross-linking contamination -- ALL BEAT aerial 0.87 and drone >1. 12/12 field resolved on the run-in (robust >=20-det tracks). summary: PROTOTYPE (study-only, task #83) — the PATROL feed as a control-lateral instrument on ST 2026-06-03 R1 (Class 5, 1650m, TURF "C", width 21.3m). The thesis from 0073: the patrol replay is the stewards'…
text:
patrol head-on lateral prototype (#83): fixed camera => constant homography (rail slope cv 3.0%, solved once) + head-on => lateral=horizontal image coord, recovers a stable sensible lateral on st 2026-06-03 r1 where aerial/drone nulled. headline within/between lateral dispersion ratio 0.06 (frame jitter 0.24m/3.98m) to 0.16 (1.5s window 0.63m) on the geometry, 0.35 even with anonymous cross-linking contamination -- all beat aerial 0.87 and drone >1. 12/12 field resolved on the run-in (robust >=20-det tracks). lateral fan (rail ~5-7m / mid ~9-11m / wide ~13-15m) matches the visible spread + stewards commentary (#2 shifts in from wide barrier; #6 caught wide). the 0071/0070 null was a substrate mis-spec (moving cam + oblique projection), not a true null of the control cause. honest limits: single race, single visible rail (scale anchored not two-rail-solved; ratio is scale-free), anonymous head-on identity inflates the full-track estimator (bridge from finish-cam numbers next). cv vision video replay patrol head-on fixed-camera constant-homography rail rail-fit slope-cv lateral control control-dimension y-lat trip within-between dispersion-ratio noise-ratio stable sensible ground-contact hoof silk jockey-detection plumb depth-aware-tracking anonymous identity number-bridge occlusion field-fraction 12-of-12 vanishing-point perspective-rectification stewards commentary interference caught-wide shifted-across de-confound mis-specification substrate 4b prototype study-only s0d s8 wave-2 0060-task 0070 0071 0073 beats-aerial no-model-change official-validation-only leak-free prototype (study-only, task #83) — the patrol feed as a control-lateral instrument on st
2026-06-03 r1 (class 5, 1650m, turf "c", width 21.3m). the thesis from 0073: the patrol replay
is the stewards' fixed high mount the field runs head-on toward in the home straight, so (1) the
track->image homography is constant (solve once, the 0071 per-frame rail-refit root cause cannot
occur) and (2) head-on => lateral = ~the horizontal image coordinate after rectification, not the
oblique rail-offset projection whose per-frame noise nulled aerial/drone (0070/0071). verdict: the
thesis holds decisively. all new code in studies/cv_patrol_{lateral,run}.py; src/hkjc/model|core
and vision/mode_b/ untouched; ruff clean; official data validation-only.

## (1) head-on segment
the fixed-camera head-on home-straight window is t=83-96s. verified by eye: before ~83s the camera
still pans off the bend (rail slope flips sign at t<=82); the field runs toward the camera growing
large t=84-100; leaders exit the bottom of frame ~t=101-102, then the feed cuts to a different
finish-line camera at t>=105 (legible saddlecloth numbers #3,#2,#6,#4 there — a potential identity
bridge, distinct camera). native frames are 1920x1080@25fps (not 720p as 0073 guessed).

## (2) fixed homography — stable (the 0071 root cause vanishes)
white left running-rail fit per-frame, taken as the median line once (camera fixed): x=-0.3934*y+393.5.
rail slope cv = 3.0% across the 27-frame window (rock-steady) — the camera is fixed, exactly as the
thesis predicts; the only residual is a +/-80px intercept jitter from horses occluding the rail,
which the solve-once median removes by construction. single visible rail (no clean right outer rail
in the zoomed head-on frame), so the metric scale is anchored to a ~15m field-fan (cross-checked
inside the 21.3m "c" width); the headline ratio is scale-invariant regardless.

## (3) detection + ground contact
per-jockey detection by silk colour (saturated non-turf), dilate+cc to merge each jockey's silk
fragments (raw silk blobs ~40/frame -> ~12-14 jockeys/frame), then a plumb down the silk column
through the dark horse body to the turf boundary = the ground-contact (hoof/shadow base), projected
to lateral offset from the rail. 646 ground-contacts over 65 frames (avg 9.9/frame).

## (4) the headline — within/between lateral dispersion ratio (vs aerial 0.87 / drone >1)
anonymous depth-aware nn tracks (lateral off + along-track depth gate stops the linker hopping
between horses sharing a lateral band). three estimators, all well below the aerial 0.87 null:
  (a) frame-to-frame jitter (raw fixed-cam/head-on measurement noise): within 0.24m / between 3.98m
      = ratio 0.059
  (b) short-window (1.5s) within-horse drift: within 0.63m / between 3.98m = ratio 0.159
  (c) full-window track std: within 1.66m / between 4.70m = ratio 0.352 -- inflated by anonymous
      cross-linking (an identity artifact, not a lateral-geometry one; head-on identity is hard).
=> patrol head-on ratio 0.06-0.35, all beat aerial 0.87 and drone >1. stable. the fixed-camera
head-on geometry recovers a stable lateral where the moving-camera aerial/drone substrates could not.

## (5) fraction of field + sensibility
at the >=20-detection robust cut: 12 long tracks for a 12-horse field = 100% resolved on the run-in
(the contesting/visible field; head-on occlusion is handled by the dense-stride re-detection). the
recovered lateral is sensible: a clean three-way fan -- rail group ~5-7m, midfield ~9-11m, wide
~13-15m -- matching the visible spread. per-track early-vs-late trend matches the stewards' commentary
(20260603r1): two tracks drift in (-1.9m, -3.6m) consistent with #2 setanta 'from a wide barrier
shifted across behind runners'; several drift out consistent with #6 telecom power 'caught wide in
the early stages' and the field fanning for home. finish order 3,12,6,2,9,8,11,4,7,10,5,1 (margins
neck/1.5l/2.25l at the front) used only as validation.

## verdict
yes -- the fixed-camera head-on patrol gives a stable, sensible lateral where aerial/drone could not.
the 0071/0070 null was a substrate mis-specification (moving camera + oblique projection), not a true
null of the control/lateral cause: on the right instrument the lateral signal is clean (within/between
0.06-0.16 on the geometry; 0.35 even with anonymous-linking contamination). honest limits: single race;
single visible rail so the metric scale is anchored not two-rail-solved (ratio is scale-free, the
metric readout is approximate); anonymous head-on identity (numbers face away) inflates the full-track
estimator and is the next thing to close (bridge from the t>=105 finish-camera numbers / time-sync to
rf). this unblocks control (s8) if a numbered per-horse lateral trip can be bridged. artifacts:
studies/cv_patrol_lateral.py, studies/cv_patrol_run.py, data_cache/figs/cv_patrol_qc.png,
data_cache/cv_patrol_lateral.parquet.

title: CV FUSION SPINE #80 STEP 1 — sync+identity built, FIRST cross-feed lateral test is a NULL on the overlap (rho -0.03, cls-agree 56%) and the null LOCALISES cleanly to (a) the bend/run-in FORESHORTENING of the aerial render and (b) the unreliable patrol identity bridge across the camera cut -- NOT a refutation of cross-feed coherence. Both feeds read FAITHFUL on their own clean segments (aerial vs stewards rho +0.9 on the body/home-straight, drops to ~0 on the bend the overlap forces) and their lateral SPREADS agree (~8m aerial / ~10m patrol, identity-free) -- the latent lateral is real and similarly scaled in both instruments; the per-horse ORDERING test fails because the overlap window sits on the worst geometry for the aerial AND the anonymous head-on patrol tracks cannot be bound to numbers across the finish-cam cut. Tells us exactly how to weight + extend: down-weight aerial on the run-in (per 0075), and the fusion needs a continuity-preserving identity anchor (RF time-sync), not the patrol finish-cut img_y bridge.

summary: STEP 1 of the 4-feed fusion (task #80). Study-only: studies/cv_fusion_spine.py. REUSES the two validated per-feed panels as observation models (aerial render #82/0075, patrol #83/0076) -- neither pipe…
text:
cv fusion spine #80 step 1 — sync+identity built, first cross-feed lateral test is a null on the overlap (rho -0.03, cls-agree 56%) and the null localises cleanly to (a) the bend/run-in foreshortening of the aerial render and (b) the unreliable patrol identity bridge across the camera cut -- not a refutation of cross-feed coherence. both feeds read faithful on their own clean segments (aerial vs stewards rho +0.9 on the body/home-straight, drops to ~0 on the bend the overlap forces) and their lateral spreads agree (~8m aerial / ~10m patrol, identity-free) -- the latent lateral is real and similarly scaled in both instruments; the per-horse ordering test fails because the overlap window sits on the worst geometry for the aerial and the anonymous head-on patrol tracks cannot be bound to numbers across the finish-cam cut. tells us exactly how to weight + extend: down-weight aerial on the run-in (per 0075), and the fusion needs a continuity-preserving identity anchor (rf time-sync), not the patrol finish-cut img_y bridge. cv vision fusion four-feed holy-grail task-80 step-1 shared-clock sync race-time odometer arclen official-sections rf-clock identity-bridge saddlecloth ocr rapidocr finish-cam camera-cut back-propagate anonymous head-on patrol aerial render-inversion cross-feed consistency spearman rail-vs-wide classification lateral y-lat off-m control control-dimension overlap-window bend run-in foreshortening mis-specification 4b not-a-null coherence spread stewards comments-on-running validation-only leak-free no-model-change study-only 0075 0076 0073 wave-2 weighting step 1 of the 4-feed fusion (task #80). study-only: studies/cv_fusion_spine.py. reuses the two
validated per-feed panels as observation models (aerial render #82/0075, patrol #83/0076) -- neither
pipeline rebuilt. src/hkjc untouched; the only new video pass is the patrol finish-cam identity ocr.
ruff clean (src/hkjc + studies). official data validation-only (sections, finish order, stewards).

(1) shared clock -- one race_t axis across feeds.
- canonical race_t = official sections [27.65,23.30,23.75,24.15] (sum 98.85 == winner 1:38.85).
- aerial -> race_t: the panel's odometer x_arclen mapped through the official arclen->time curve,
  per row. covers race_t 9.2-98.2s. direct, no anchor needed.
- patrol -> race_t: no odometer/clock; anchored kinematically by the winner (#3) crossing the
  finish line on the photo-finish cut (visually verified vid t=117.5s; auto-detector clamps to it),
  so race_t = patrol_vid_t - 18.65s (residual +-0.4s, single coarse anchor). note the headline run
  reports offset 17.65 from the auto-detector's 116.5s read; the verified visual anchor is 117.5s
  (offset 18.65) -- a 1s clock uncertainty, well within the overlap. patrol head-on window
  vid 83-96s -> race_t ~65-79s.
- rf/full feed cross-check: full_20260603_01.mp4 carries an on-screen race clock (top-right,
  "0:58.65", "670m to finish"). manual reads t_vid 5->0:03.67, 25->0:23.67, 60->0:58.65 give a
  constant offset 1.33-1.35s == race_t -- an independent confirmation of the canonical clock (the
  stylised broadcast clock font does not ocr with rapidocr, same as the painted markers in 0075, so
  it is a manual cross-check not a per-frame source). rf is the natural future sync backbone.
- overlap (aerial cap. and patrol head-on): race_t 65.3-78.3s, width 13.0s. crucial: this maps to
  arclen ~1100-1290m == the bend into the home straight, the single worst region for the aerial
  render (0075 run-in foreshortening), and the patrol head-on fan is the straight-entry. the two
  instruments' coverage only overlaps where the aerial is least reliable.

(2) identity bridge.
- aerial: 11/12 via the legend (reused from the panel's `runner` col; missing #7 only).
- patrol: anonymous head-on (numbers face away). the feed cuts (no pixel continuity) to a finish
  camera at t>=105s. finish-cam saddlecloth ocr (rapidocr, 2-scale, pooled t=105.5-118.5s) reads
  11/12 numbers -- a strong identity count. but binding each number to a head-on track requires its
  rail-relative lateral on the finish cam, and that is the failure: the finish cam is side-on, so
  both image-y and perpendicular-distance-to-rail conflate lateral with along-track depth/stagger
  (leader low/large, trailer high/small). so the rank hand-off (finish-cam rail-order -> head-on
  track rail-order) is unreliable -- 10/12 tracks get a number but the assignment is wrong for
  several (e.g. #2, officially wide + read widest by the aerial, gets bridged to a tight track).
  bridge fraction: aerial 11/12 identity (faithful); patrol 10/12 tracks numbered but low-confidence
  on the lateral binding.

(3) cross-feed consistency test (the deliverable), on the overlap window, per numbered horse.
- headline: spearman rho(aerial y_lat, patrol off_m) = -0.03 (n=9); rail-vs-wide classification
  agreement 56% (~chance). a null.
- diagnosis (the value is in localising it; both contributors are measurement mis-spec, not a
  coherence refutation):
  (a) the overlap window is the bend -- aerial faithfulness vs the stewards' comments-on-running
      (rail #12/#8/#4/#11 vs wide #2/#6/#9/#1, validation-only) is rho +0.93 on the clean body
      (arclen<=1300) and +0.93 on the home straight (>=1300), but collapses to ~0 (+0.14 full-field,
      -0.02 on the bridged subset) on the arclen ~1100-1290m bend the overlap forces. this is exactly
      the 0075 oblique run-in under-determination, now quantified as a window-localised drop.
  (b) the patrol identity bridge is unreliable across the camera cut (above) -- patrol off_m vs
      stewards rho ~0 because the numbers are mis-assigned, not because the patrol metric is bad
      (0076 validated the patrol lateral fan independently at within/between 0.06-0.16).
- coherence positive (identity-free): the two feeds' lateral spreads agree -- aerial 7.8m fan vs
  patrol 9.9m fan (both ~half the 21.3m "c" width) -- so both instruments measure a real,
  similarly-scaled latent lateral. the latent is fuseable; the ordering test just landed on the
  one window + the one missing piece (continuity-preserving identity) that defeat it.

what this tells the fusion design (#80 step 2):
- weight the aerial render down on the run-in/bend (arclen>1300 and the foreshortened transition);
  its faithful regime is the body + home straight, not the bend.
- the patrol identity bridge must not rely on the finish-cam img_y (side-on depth confound) or the
  camera cut (no continuity). use a continuity-preserving anchor: time-sync patrol to the rf feed
  (shared race clock, established here at +-1s) and carry rf/aerial numbered identity into the patrol
  head-on window by race_t + lateral, or find an overlap window on a cleaner aerial segment.
- better overlap: pull a patrol/aerial overlap on the home straight proper (arclen>1300) where both
  are clean -- here the patrol head-on window happens to sit on the bend; a later patrol window (or
  the rf home-straight) would test the feeds where each is strongest.

title: AERIAL MINIMAP probe (#85) — CLEAN NEGATIVE: the AVV top-down inset is a PROGRESS INDICATOR, not a per-horse lateral source. The inset is a tiny ~140x68 px (0.46% of frame) schematic of the FULL TRACK LOOP carrying THREE things and none is per-horse lateral: a '<NNN>M' distance-to-finish caption (yellow, counts 370M->0M), the COVERED arc drawn RED + the REMAINING arc GREEN (red-px strictly monotone 911->700->549->445->368->297->199->101->56->0 across t=20->100s = a textbook progress bar), and a SINGLE yellow dot marking the WHOLE FIELD's along-track position on the loop. There is ONE field-position marker, never the >=12 separable number/colour-coded markers a per-horse lateral would require (dot-count in the loop interior is 0 or 1 every sampled frame, never approaching 12), and there is NO rail-offset/lateral axis at all — the loop is an along-track progress ring shaped like the course, orthographic but DIMENSIONALLY 1-D (arclen only). So the 0077 thesis (a near-orthographic, foreshortening-free, number-identified 2nd view that resolves 12 lateral positions and moots the render-foreshortening problem) is FALSE for this inset: the per-horse lateral data simply does not exist in it. STEP A (scrutinize-first) was decisive and STEPs B/C (extract per-horse minimap lateral; validate vs stewards + render-inversion + per-zone bend/run-in dispersion) are MOOT — there is nothing to extract. This CLOSES the 'minimap as fusion backbone' option flagged unexploited since 0073. It does NOT touch the two validated lateral feeds (aerial render between-runner ordering #82/0075 on the body; patrol fixed-homography #83/0076 on the home straight) nor the >=2-model fusion gate (#80, still MET). aerial minimap probe (#85) — clean negative: the avv top-down inset is a progress indicator, not a per-horse lateral source. the inset is a tiny ~140x68 px (0.46% of frame) schematic of the full track loop carrying three things and none is per-horse lateral: a '<nnn>m' distance-to-finish caption (yellow, counts 370m->0m), the covered arc drawn red + the remaining arc green (red-px strictly monotone 911->700->549->445->368->297->199->101->56->0 across t=20->100s = a textbook progress bar), and a single yellow dot marking the whole field's along-track position on the loop. there is one field-position marker, never the >=12 separable number/colour-coded markers a per-horse lateral would require (dot-count in the loop interior is 0 or 1 every sampled frame, never approaching 12), and there is no rail-offset/lateral axis at all — the loop is an along-track progress ring shaped like the course, orthographic but dimensionally 1-d (arclen only). so the 0077 thesis (a near-orthographic, foreshortening-free, number-identified 2nd view that resolves 12 lateral positions and moots the render-foreshortening problem) is false for this inset: the per-horse lateral data simply does not exist in it. step a (scrutinize-first) was decisive and steps b/c (extract per-horse minimap lateral; validate vs stewards + render-inversion + per-zone bend/run-in dispersion) are moot — there is nothing to extract. this closes the 'minimap as fusion backbone' option flagged unexploited since 0073. it does not touch the two validated lateral feeds (aerial render between-runner ordering #82/0075 on the body; patrol fixed-homography #83/0076 on the home straight) nor the >=2-model fusion gate (#80, still met). the fusion bend/run-in overlap problem (0077) remains open and now has one fewer escape route: of 0077's three next routes, route (i) minimap is refuted; verdict: no. a clean negative — closes the minimap option (flagged unexploited since 0073, never tested).

## step a — scrutinize first (decisive; step b/c never reached because a answered the whole question)

located the inset in the avv split-screen (left=real camera, right=3d render). it sits top-right of
the render panel, full-frame bbox ~x1620-1760, y292-358 => **~140x68 px = 0.46% of the 1920x1080
frame**. stable position; renders once the race is underway (absent at t<=12s, present t>=~15s).

what it actually is (crops saved /tmp/minimap_probe/, qc fig cv_minimap_probe_qc.png):
a schematic of the **full track loop** (the course outline) used as a course-progress widget:
  1. a yellow **'<nnn>m' distance-to-finish caption** (read visually 1330m..670m..140m..0m; the
     stylised numerals are the same family that did not ocr in 0075, but they are legible by eye);
  2. the **covered arc drawn red, the remaining arc green** — red shrinks strictly monotonically
     911->700->549->445->368->297->199->101->56->0 px across t=20->100s (a textbook progress bar);
  3. a **single yellow dot** marking the whole field's current along-track position on the loop,
     advancing around the ring toward the finish.

answers to the step-a questions, concretely:
- minimap present? yes, every frame once racing; ~140x68 px.
- individual horse markers resolvable? no — there is exactly one field-position dot. the dot-count
  inside the loop interior is 0 or 1 on every sampled frame, never approaching the >=12 a per-horse
  read needs. no pack-of-12; the field is rendered as a single point.
- color/number-coded per runner (tie to the legend)? no — the single dot is generic (no number, no
  per-runner colour); identity is not even attempted in the inset.
- full track (lateral=rail-offset readable) or progress bar? progress bar. the loop is an
  along-track ring (arclen/distance-to-finish). it is orthographic but dimensionally 1-d — there is
  no rail-offset axis to read a lateral from.

## why the 0077 thesis fails (honestly)

0077 hoped the inset was a near-orthographic 2nd view that (a) is foreshortening-free and (b) is
number-identified in-frame, so it could resolve 12 per-horse lateral positions and moot the render's
bend/run-in foreshortening. the inset is orthographic and is foreshortening-free — but it carries
only the field's 1-d along-track progress, not per-horse 2-d position. the lateral data is simply
not in it. so step b (extract per-horse minimap lateral) and step c (validate vs stewards / render
agreement / per-zone bend-run-in dispersion) are moot: nothing to extract, nothing to validate.

## what this closes / leaves open

- closed: 'aerial minimap as the clean whole-race lateral / fusion backbone' (0073 flag; 0077 route i).
- unaffected: the two validated lateral feeds (aerial render between-runner ordering #82/0075 on the
  body <1300m; patrol fixed-homography metric #83/0076 on the home straight). the >=2-model fusion
  gate (#80) stays met.
- still open (the 0077 bend/run-in overlap problem, now with one fewer escape route): route (ii)
  bridge patrol identity by rf time-sync continuity (not the side-on finish-cut img_y) so the bend
  overlap becomes usable; route (iii) complementary stitching on the shared clock + the identity-free
  spread match + seam continuity. these remain the live paths to a redundant cross-feed agreement.

drone revisit #87 result — the drone folds in as the 3rd full-race feed (time-anchored on the shared clock, arclen 0->1640m), and delivers the first per-horse cross-feed lateral agreement (drone vs aerial rho +0.88..+0.93, cls 100%, leave-one-out +0.83..+0.91) -- but the per-frame within/between dispersion test still nulls (ratio 1.04 run-in / 2.6 home-straight / 5.2 bend, all >=1), so the new toolkit beats 0070 on between-runner ordering + cross-feed redundancy but not on absolute per-runner trip metres. the strong +0.93 sits on the arclen 773-1000m bend (both feeds order moderately-faithful there: aerial-vs-stew +0.71, drone +0.46); the genuinely clean home-straight overlap (1270-1490m) nulls (-0.58) because the aerial itself degrades there (aerial-vs-stew +0.04, the 0075/0077 foreshortening) -- confirming 0077's structural finding that no arclen band is clean for both at once. honest mixed result: a real 3rd feed + first redundant cross-feed positive (ordering), still a §4b mis-spec on the absolute metric. cv vision drone fusion four-feed holy-grail task-87 third-feed shared-clock race-t arclen time-anchor coverage census straightness bend home-straight run-in stable-rail rail-spline ground-contact shadow y-lat lateral control within-between dispersion-ratio cross-feed redundant coherence spearman leave-one-out rail-vs-wide classification stewards comments-on-running silk-number-bridge reid foreshortening under-determined 4b mis-specification not-a-null null-on-metric positive-on-ordering 0070 0075 0076 0077 wave-2 external-validation validation-only leak-free no-model-change study-only task #87 — fold the drone in as the 3rd lateral feed: census coverage, retry a validated lateral

step 1 — coverage census (the headline structural gain). 0070 said the drone has "no global
longitudinal axis" (the field-relative odometer totals only ~379m). fix: anchor on time, not the
odometer. two frame-verified real-time events -> an affine drone_vid_t -> race_t map:
  gate jump (centroid speed surges 2->12 px/frame, vid ~3.0s) -> race_t 0
  hard cut to the photo-finish replay (centroid jump 350px, vid 113.68s) -> winner crosses 98.85s
=> race_t = (vid_t - 3.0) * 0.8931. then race_t -> arclen via the official-section curve (the same
curve the fusion spine uses, 0077). result: the drone covers race_t -2.7 -> 98s == arclen 0 ->
1640m -- the whole race. per-frame rail-straightness (pca across/along ratio) classifies it:
  * start + accel: arclen 0-450m, mixed straight/turn (vid 3-34)
  * the long bend: arclen ~470-1130m, straightness 0.3-0.6 (vid 36-78) -- the sweeping turn
  * a straight patch arclen ~1150-1190m (vid 80-82)
  * the clean home straight: arclen ~1270-1566m, straightness 0.9-1.0 (vid 88-108) -- overlaps the
    aerial's validated clean home-straight (>=1300m, 0075) and the run-in patrol+aerial both struggle
  * run-in to the line goes oblique (vid 109-113, foreshortened) then cut to the replay.
so the drone is a genuine 3rd full-coverage feed once time-anchored, with a clean straight that
co-locates with the aerial's clean zone -- the redundant overlap 0077 said the aerial+patrol pair
lacked. (#80 holy-grail: this is the 3rd feed folded in, not yet the 4th/rf margins.)

step 2 — validated lateral, new toolkit (stable per-window rail + ground-contact). the 0075 recipe
ported to the panning drone: pool the inner-rail boundary points across a window (camera ~static)
and fit one rail line (not 0070's per-frame turf-boundary refit, the instability root cause); use
each sprite's ground-contact (feet/shadow base, lowest extent) not the body centroid; scale by the
per-frame dt corridor == 21.3m; identity via the 0070 silk->number colour anchors. within/between
y_lat dispersion ratio per clean zone (0070 null was ratio>1):
  mid-bend   (773-1000m): within 2.56 / between 0.49 = 5.19   (rail too curved -> single line poor)
  home-str  (1270-1490m): within 2.44 / between 0.93 = 2.62
  run-in    (1520-1647m): within 2.14 / between 2.06 = 1.04   (best; near the boundary)
honest null on step 2: the ratio still does not beat 1 in any window. the toolkit helps -- the
run-in between-runner spread jumps to 2.06m (vs the bend's 0.49m) and the ratio falls to ~1.04 (vs
0070's >1 and the per-frame swings 0.8->6.3m) -- but a single straight-line per-window rail on a
panning camera is still not a stable enough reference for a clean per-frame absolute trip. this is
the same class of §4b limit as the aerial (0075): the absolute per-runner trip metres are
mis-specified; the between-runner ordering is the recoverable signal.

drone-vs-stewards (rail=0/wide=1) spearman: mid-bend +0.46, home-str -0.07, run-in +0.39 -- positive
where the drone geometry is least degraded, consistent with the ordering (not metric) being real.

step 3 — the back-straight redundant cross-check vs the aerial render (the prize). per numbered
horse, median drone y_lat vs median aerial render y_lat on the overlapping band, spearman + rail/
wide class-agree, with a 0077-style localiser (is the aerial itself faithful vs stewards on that
band?):
  mid-bend  (773-1000m):  rho +0.93, cls 100%  | aerial-vs-stew +0.71, drone-vs-stew +0.68
  home-str (1270-1490m):  rho -0.58, cls  33%  | aerial-vs-stew +0.04, drone-vs-stew +0.11
  run-in   (1520-1647m):  rho +0.32, cls  56%  | aerial-vs-stew +0.39, drone-vs-stew -0.14
the mid-bend +0.93 is robust: leave-one-out rho +0.83..+0.91 (mean +0.88), not driven by one point;
drone rail horses #8/#11/#12 read 3.1-3.8m, wide #9 widest 5.5m. this is the first time two
independent feeds agree per-horse on lateral ordering at rho>0.8 -- the redundant cross-feed
coherence 0077's bend overlap (patrol identity bottleneck, rho -0.03) could not deliver. but the
honest caveat: it sits on arclen 773-1000m, a bend (not the cleanest geometry), where both feeds
order only moderately-faithfully (aerial +0.71). the genuinely clean home-straight overlap
(1270-1490m) nulls (-0.58) -- and the localiser shows why: the aerial itself is unreliable there
(aerial-vs-stew +0.04; e.g. it reads the wire-to-wire rail leader #12 at 19.2m, plainly wrong),
the 0075/0077 home-straight-entry foreshortening. so this confirms 0077's structural finding from
the 3rd feed's side: there is no single arclen band where the aerial is clean and the drone is clean
enough for a strong redundant per-horse test by re-windowing alone.

net / verdict (mixed, honest):
  + the drone is now a 3rd full-race feed on the shared clock (time-anchored, arclen 0-1640m) with a
    clean straight co-located with the aerial's clean zone -- a real structural gain for #80 fusion.
  + first redundant cross-feed per-horse lateral agreement (drone vs aerial rho +0.88..+0.93, cls
    100%, loo-robust) -- on the arclen 773-1000m band. the between-runner ordering signal is real and
    coherent across two independent instruments.
  - the per-frame within/between dispersion test still nulls (ratio >=1 everywhere; best 1.04) -- the
    new toolkit does not recover a clean absolute per-runner trip from the panning drone. same §4b
    metric mis-spec class as the aerial render (single under-determined rail + a moving camera).
  - the cleanest-geometry overlap (home straight) nulls because the aerial degrades there -- so the
    cross-feed prize is earned on a bend, not the clean straight; 0077's "no clean-for-both band"
    structural finding is reaffirmed, now from 3 feeds.
next (for #80): the drone's run-in/home-straight is the real-position fanned finish that patrol+aerial
both lose -- worth a proper per-frame homography (recover the painted-marker pixel anchors or use the
oblique run-in rail as a 2nd fiducial) to convert the drone ordering into a metric there; and the
drone's clean home straight should be fused with the patrol head-on (0076) which is metric-clean on
the straight-entry but loses identity -- the drone's number bridge + the patrol metric are
complementary. rf margins remain the 4th feed to fold.

stage a lut (finish-cam, vid t=102.5-123.0s where the feed cuts to a side-on finish tracking camera with legible saddlecloth numbers): rapidocr dual-scale (1.6x+2.2x), conf>0.45, pooled, >=2-hit gate => 8/12 numbers (#1,2,3,5,6,8,9,12; back-markers #4,7,10,11 exit the finish-cam frame, never ocr'd at any threshold). for each ocr'd number the nearest saturated silk blob above it (jockey torso) contributes a sat-weighted hue histogram (18 bins). key method point: a lab/bgr median collapses every silk to muddy red on these overlapping low-res side-on silks (the partial result 0081); a hue histogram keeps each silk's distinct hues, so blue (#5,#6), yellow (#1,#2-cream) and navy (#3) separate from the red/pink cluster.
stage b head-on signatures: re-sample every detected jockey's silk hue histogram (the same _silk_mask/detect_jockeys machinery as cv_patrol_lateral) per frame, tag by (off_m,depth) from the 0076 homography, bin to each robust track, mean-histogram per track => 12/12 robust tracks signed.
assign: hungarian one-to-one on a circular hue-histogram emd (not rotation-invariant — silks are absolute hues), track<->lut. confidence = margin of the assigned cost to the track's 2nd-best, scaled by the field-median margin; conf<0.35 flagged ambiguous. result: 8 tracks numbered; colour-confident #2,#5,#8,#9 (the distinct yellow/blue/pink-red silks), ambiguous #1,#3,#6,#12 (the red/pink/magenta family that is genuinely degenerate at 1080p side-on — verified by eye: #8 navy+pink, #12 white+pink, #2 cream, #9 red, #6 blue, #3 navy+red).

validation vs stewards' comments-on-running (validation only): field lateral span 8.8-14.9m on the segment; tight<=12.7m / wide>=13.8m percentiles. #12 the way we win (wire-to-wire rail, pos 1-1-1) 10.7m tight ok; #8 manythanks forever (inside) 8.8m tight ok; #2 setanta (wide barrier, shifted across) 14.4m wide ok; #6 telecom power (caught wide) 13.2m mid-but-wide-side ok. 4/4. gap = mean wide(#2,#6) 13.8m - mean rail(#12,#8) 9.8m = +4.1m. the +4.1m gap and the 4/4 rail/wide split are stable across reruns even though the individual pink-vs-pink assignment wobbles (an earlier hue-hist run put #12 at 5.0m rail and #2 at 9.4m; the rail-number<->tight-track and wide-number<->wide-track sets are invariant, the within-set permutation is the ambiguity). so the silk->number->trip chain is correct at the rail-vs-wide classification level; absolute per-runner fine identity needs better silk separation than the side-on finish-cam affords.

deliverable: data_cache/cv_patrol_numbered.parquet (319 rows; cols runner,race_t,arclen,y_lat_m,confidence) over race_t 64.3-77.2s = arclen 1058-1279m (the bend-into-straight head-on window). 8 runners: #1,2,3,5,6,8,9,12. this banks the per-segment floor deliverable (a confident, numbered, high-res lateral segment) and unlocks the bend cross-feed test (#80 step 2) with a proper continuity-free identity (replacing 0077's unreliable side-on img_y bridge that nulled the first cross-feed test). honest limits: single race; 8/12 numbered (lut-capped by ocr at the finish-cam, 4 back-markers never legible); 4 of the 8 colour-ambiguous within the red/pink silk family; #6's 13.2m reads mid not hard-wide (its 'caught wide' was earlier in the race; by this late head-on segment the field has fanned). next: (a) push more lut numbers / cleaner silks via the rf finish saddlecloths or time-sync continuity for #4,7,10,11; (b) feed this numbered segment into #80 fusion step 2 as the patrol observation model with a per-runner confidence weight.

text: fusion smoother #80 step 2 partial — rts state-space runs end-to-end on all 12 horses, first reconstructed-race trajectories produced  partial (anti-stall): studies/cv_fusion_smoother.py — a per-horse numpy kalman forward-filter + rts backward-smoother on the shared race_t grid (5hz, 448 nodes, race_t 9.2-98.6s) — runs end-to-end fusing all 3 validated feeds. state z=[s,s_dot,l,l_dot]; physics motion prior = bounded longitudinal accel (sigma_a 0.8 m/s^2) + bounded lateral accel (0.35 m/s^2 -> slow sideways drift), applied jointly in the smoother, no per-feed pre-filter. obs models: aerial odometer arclen (field-shared, sd 3m) + y_lat (sd 6m, inflated to 12m >1300m foreshortening); drone arclen (sd 8m) + y_lat (sd 7m); patrol = metric anchor y_lat (sd 1.2m/conf). ingest: aerial 2626 obs/11 runners, drone 4957/10, patrol 319/8 -> union 12/12 identity. first numbers: tight/wide gap survives fusion +3.85m (rail #4/8/11/12 mean 5.36m vs wide #1/2/6/9 mean 9.21m) vs stewards/patrol +4.1m, now covering 8/8 commented horses (patrol alone was 4/8). full result + figure + per-band uncertainty census to follow after a prior-strength pass (the run-in band must show the honest widening). artifacts: cv_fusion_trajectories.parquet (5193 rows), figs/cv_fusion_recon.png.

title: FUSION smoother #80 step 2 RESULT — 3-feed RTS state-space reconstructs ALL 12 horses' (arclen,lateral,t) trajectory full-race; the +4.1m rail-wide gap SURVIVES fusion (+3.84m) and EXTENDS to 8/8 commented horses; run-in y_lat uncertainty inflates honestly 0.98m(patrol anchor)->1.72m(line); longitudinal is field-shared (per-horse order awaits RF margins)
author: modelling
summary: RESULT — #80 STEP 2, the FUSION STATE-SPACE SMOOTHER + first reconstructed-race trajectories. studies/cv_fusion_smoother.py (study-only; src/hkjc untouched; the 3 input parquets read-only/not mutated;…
text:
fusion smoother #80 step 2 result — 3-feed rts state-space reconstructs all 12 horses' (arclen,lateral,t) trajectory full-race; the +4.1m rail-wide gap survives fusion (+3.84m) and extends to 8/8 commented horses; run-in y_lat uncertainty inflates honestly 0.98m(patrol anchor)->1.72m(line); longitudinal is field-shared (per-horse order awaits rf margins)  result — #80 step 2, the fusion state-space smoother + first reconstructed-race trajectories. studies/cv_fusion_smoother.py (study-only; src/hkjc untouched; the 3 input parquets read-only/not mutated; official sections/rp/stewards validation-only). ruff clean (src/hkjc + studies). st 2026-06-03 r1, class5 1650m turf c (21.3m).

the model (faithful to the #80 design). per-horse independent numpy kalman forward-filter + rts backward-smoother on one shared race_t grid (5hz, 448 nodes, race_t 9.2-98.6s). latent z=[s,s_dot,l,l_dot]. physics motion prior applied jointly in the smoother (not a per-feed pre-filter): bounded longitudinal accel (white-accel sigma 0.8 m/s^2, near-constant cruise) + bounded lateral accel (sigma 0.35 m/s^2 -> slow sideways drift) — this smoothness prior is the principled home of the no-teleport/jitter concern. each feed enters only over its coverage window with its own noise: aerial odometer arclen (field-shared, sd 3m) + y_lat (sd 6m, inflated 14m on >1300m foreshortening, 0075); drone time-anchored arclen (sd 8m) + y_lat (sd 7m, inflated 11m on the run-in where its metric §4b-nulls, 0080); patrol = the metric anchor y_lat (sd 1.2m / confidence, 0082/0076) pinning absolute scale on its 1058-1279m window. state covariance propagated -> uncertainty bands.

shared clock (0077 reused): aerial t->field-odometer arclen->race_t (official-section curve); drone race_t=(vid-3.0)*0.8931 (0080) -> arclen; patrol already on race_t/arclen/y_lat_m. identity union: aerial 11/12 (legend) + drone 10/12 (silk->number) + patrol 8/12 (silk lut) => union 12/12.

results (the first real reconstruct-the-race output):
- 12/12 horses reconstructed over the whole race (race_t 9.2-98.6s == arclen ~150-1647m). per-horse feed mix: 6 horses see all 3 feeds (#1,2,5,6,8,9,12), #3 aerial+patrol, #4 aerial-only, #10/#11 aerial+drone, #7 drone-only (a 771-1646m partial). output cv_fusion_trajectories.parquet (5193 rows; runner,race_t,arclen,y_lat_m,sd_arclen,sd_ylat).
- fused tight-vs-wide gap survives fusion and extends: rail #4/8/11/12 mean 5.39m vs wide #1/2/6/9 mean 9.23m => gap +3.84m (stewards/patrol ref +4.1m), now covering 8/8 stewards-commented horses (patrol-alone covered 4/8 — fusion roughly doubles the validated coverage). all 4 rail horses read <=6.7m, all 4 wide horses >=9.5m: a clean rail/wide split with no mis-class. the +4.1m gap survives and extends to more horses — the deliverable's headline question answered yes.
- per-band y_lat uncertainty (the segment-quality census — what each segment is worth): start/accel(150-450m) 1.44m; backstr/bend(450-850m) 2.03m (thin: drone window starts ~770m, so 450-770m is aerial-only); bend->straight(850-1300m) 1.00m (the best — co-located with the patrol anchor + the cross-validated <1300m aerial/drone ordering zone); run-in(>1300m) 1.41m mean. the honest gap is visible in the fine profile: sd is tightest ~0.96-0.98m at 1200-1300m (the patrol metric anchor) and inflates monotonically through the run-in: 1.18(1300-1350) -> 1.50(1450) -> 1.72m at the line (1600-1650m). i.e. as soon as we leave the patrol metric anchor and only foreshortened ordering feeds remain, the absolute-metric band widens ~75% — exactly the honest run-in gap the recon figure must show.

the recon figure (cv_fusion_recon.png, 2 panels): top = arclen vs race_t, all 12 horses + 2-sigma bands on the shared clock; bottom = y_lat vs arclen, the lateral/control trip, 12 horses + 2-sigma bands, with the gold patrol metric-anchor window (visibly tightest bands there) and the crimson >1300m run-in divider where the bands visibly fan out. feed-coverage strip annotated.

honest limits (no overclaim — this is a first fusion):
1. the lateral is the real fused product and it is validated at the rail-vs-wide classification / ordering level (+3.84m gap, clean split), not a clean whole-race absolute metric — the metric is anchored only where patrol sees it (1058-1279m); elsewhere the scale rides on the prior + the §4b-null ordering feeds, hence the honestly-widening run-in bands. this matches the per-feed verdicts (all 3 feeds §4b-null on the absolute metric; patrol the only within/between<1).
2. the longitudinal recon is the field odometer (frame-shared distance-run common to all horses) + coarse drone arclen — per-horse stagger is essentially unobserved (field arclen std ~1.2m at a pole). so the fused lead-order vs official rp is not meaningful (rho -0.57/-0.56/+0.31/+0.03 at the 450/850/1250/1640m poles — dominated by sub-metre smoother artifacts, reported with the caveat). a real per-horse longitudinal order needs the rf margins feed — the un-built 4th feed. fused y_lat(<1300m) vs official mean-rp spearman is only +0.10 because mean-rp conflates lead/back with rail/wide; the rail-vs-wide gap is the cleaner validated axis (and 0075's +0.45 was that conflated corr on aerial-alone).
3. single race; per-horse independent (field interactions = future work); 4 of the patrol-anchored horses are in the ambiguous pink-silk family (down-weighted by confidence).

net: the 4-feed-design fusion (3 feeds folded; rf margins pending) now produces a single per-horse latent (arclen, lateral, t) trajectory for all 12 horses on the shared clock under a first-principles physics motion prior, with propagated uncertainty that correctly tightens at the patrol metric anchor and widens on the run-in. the validated deliverable is the rail-vs-wide control classification (s8-ready: who saved ground / went wide), with absolute metres pinned only on the patrol window — solid where solid, honestly-wide where thin. builds directly on 0083 (partial).

artifacts: studies/cv_fusion_smoother.py; data_cache/cv_fusion_trajectories.parquet (5193 rows, 12 runners); data_cache/figs/cv_fusion_recon.png. inputs reused read-only: cv_s0d_aerial_render.parquet (#82/0075), cv_drone_numbered.parquet (#87/0080), cv_patrol_numbered.parquet (#86/0082).

official chart = validation only). ruff clean. st 2026-06-03 r1, class5 1650m turf c, 12 runners.
shared clock (0077): race_t = rf_vid_t - 1.34; winner #3 crosses race_t 98.85 (1:38.85) == rf_vid ~100.19.

rf is real side-on broadcast footage (1920x1080, 25fps, 143s). unlike the from-behind mid-race body
and unlike the stylised avv, near the finish the camera is side-on at ~real scale and saddlecloth
numbers ocr on the horses themselves (rapidocr dual-scale on the track-band crop).

step 1 — identity. finish-window (vid 96.5-100.5) ocr binds 8/12 saddlecloths on the horses
themselves: {3,4,5,6,7,8,9,12} (the lead+mid group). the 5 deep back-markers {1,2,10,11 + #4/7 fall
out of the margin set} are too distant/blurred side-on to ocr reliably in this window. backup/whole-race
identity comes from the bottom legend strip (step 3): its english names ocr cleanly and bridge 1:1 to
runner numbers via the fixed pre-race name->number lut.

step 2 — finish margins (the priority deliverable; the s3 likelihood surface, #60). photo-finish
geometry: a horse's horizontal pixel position is its along-track position; the within-frame pixel gap
to the winner / a per-frame body-length px scale (2.4m) is the margin in lengths -- pan-robust because
it is relative within a single frame. aggregated open-gap (75th-pct) per horse, n>=2.
  headline vs the official chart lbw (lengths-behind-winner): margin mae = 0.41 lengths;
  margin spearman rho = +0.90; order spearman rho = +0.90; pairwise order 9/10; fit rf=0.70*official+0.23.
  per-horse (rf len vs official lbw): #3 0.00/0 (winner ref); #12 0.28 / 0.3 (neck -- nailed);
  #9 1.82 / 2.25; #6 1.87 / 1.5; #8 3.02 / 4.25. 5 horses co-framed with the winner near the line.
  honest residual: slope 0.70 (not 1.0) -- back-markers leave the (leader-tracking) frame before the
  gap fully opens, so the deeper the horse the more its line-margin is under-read (#8 the worst). this
  is a real sampling/geometry limit, not a fit knob; the lead-group close finish is excellent.

s3 implication (#60): the rf margins are a per-horse finishing-gap observation the 3-feed fusion (0084)
entirely lacked (its only longitudinal obs was the field-shared aerial odometer, per-horse stagger
~1.2m unobserved, order-vs-rp rho~0 at the poles). the margins distribution is the s3 likelihood
surface that sharpens w'_0 + the spread: a tight close finish (here #3/#12 within a neck = ~0.3 len ~0.7m,
then a 1.5-len step to #6) constrains the front-group w'-burn / kick dispersion to be small near the line
(low diffusion d in the run-in), i.e. it pins the upper tail of the finishing-time spread; the longer
4-5+ len tail to the back-markers sets the lower tail. validated at mae 0.41 len, this is a usable
per-race s3 constraint on the spread (w'_0 sharpening) for the lead group -- the first per-horse
longitudinal observable in the fusion.

step 3 (per-horse longitudinal backbone over the whole race) is computing now (legend-name order +
finish gaps); full entry to follow. artifacts so far: studies/cv_rf_longitudinal.py;
data_cache/cv_rf_longitudinal.parquet; data_cache/figs/cv_rf_qc.png.

the only long. obs was the aerial field-shared odometer (one distance-run for the whole field;
per-horse stagger ~1.2m unresolved), so fused order-vs-official-rp rho~0 at the poles. rf is the fix

-> 8-deep numbered order at 42 timepoints. so the per-horse identity for the longitudinal backbone is

  headline vs official chart lbw: margin mae = 0.41 lengths; margin spearman rho = +0.90; order

running-order data overlay (~ official chart), lead group left->back, 42 timepoints race_t 8.7-90.7s.

fusion's gap: a per-horse longitudinal order that is rp-faithful (rho +0.98..+1.00) over the whole
race -- exactly what the field-shared odometer could not give (0084 rho~0). plus metric finishing
gaps at the line (mae 0.41 len). so rf resolves the longitudinal order everywhere and the metric
gap at the finish; the per-horse absolute metric stagger mid-race remains unresolved by any feed
(consistent with the §4b-metric nulls of the other 3) -- but order + finish-margins is what the
generative finishing-order model and the s3 spread actually consume.

the lower tail. at mae 0.41 len this is a usable per-race s3 likelihood term on the spread (w'_0
sharpening) for the lead group -- the first per-horse longitudinal observable available to the
fusion/generative pipeline. next: enter rf into the fusion smoother (0084) as the 4th observation
model -- the legend order as a per-horse rank/ordering constraint over the whole race + the finish
margins as metric longitudinal gaps at the line -- to give the fused trajectory the per-horse
longitudinal order it currently lacks.
