author: modelling
summary: ## Horse detection reworked — rail-bounded, count-aware, k-means dropped (promoted) Promoted `detect_avatars` to hkjc.vision.feeds.aerial_detect (replaces the `_kmeans_field_both` forces-the-count app…
text:
horse detection reworked: rail-bounded count-aware watershed (k-means dropped); longitudinal next cv aerial detection reconstruction handoff ## horse detection reworked — rail-bounded, count-aware, k-means dropped (promoted)
promoted `detect_avatars` to hkjc.vision.feeds.aerial_detect (replaces the `_kmeans_field_both`
forces-the-count approach). pipeline: turf/bright suppress -> canny+fill ∩ colour -> close to
reconnect each avatar's split body/silk pieces -> rail-bound the roi (track region between the two
main rails, from rail candidates = field-independent, drops grandstand/apron false-positives) ->
rail-parallel close -> split only over-large blobs (genuine front-to-back merges) into
round(area/single) centres via distance-transform nms, with the single-horse area solved from the
known field/legend count (the user's "iterate until we get the number of horses", as a global
constraint). count-aware, not count-forced.

tried + judged visually (studies/cv_avatar_detect2.py): iterative rail-parallel blur alone (good on
spread, fails on bunched=under-segmented); naive distance-peaks (over-counts, one peak per fragment);
the field-anchored watershed split = winner (f1080/f2200/f2440 -> exactly 11 with dots on the horses;
f1760 -> 14, a few avatars stay split). bidirectional blur-down-then-split regressed; reverted.

whole-race: median 11 in-lane (honest variance 5-20 vs the old fake-forced 11); 4 clean long
tracklets. good enough to drive longitudinal reconstruction (user: losing 1-2 frames is fine).

## nn research (background subagent, orthogonal)
keep the rail classical (sam2/segmentation are weak on thin structures; the rail problem is geometric
disambiguation). the only nn worth a small experiment is a fine-tuned yolo11-n detector (cpu-feasible
~16fps; auto-labelable from the classical detector + legend; ~1-2 days) for the residual bunched/faint
cases. zero-shot/sam2-video re-create the merge problem and need gpu. deferred.

## next (in progress): longitudinal / metric reconstruction
goal: per-horse (arclen, y_lat, t) 2d paths. use the on-screen odometer widget (m to finish;
aerial_ocr.read_odometer; pre-extracted in cv_joint_aerial_r08_obs.npz, ~148 finite frames) as the
key-frame absolute-arclen calibration to convert per-frame pixel s along the rail -> metric arclen,
and to set the px->m scale (its rate of change). then assemble high-quality 2d paths.

## open
- (c) a-config single-rail fragment coalescing (still pending).
- f1760-type detection over-segment residual (a few frames); per-frame count variance.

title: 2D reconstruction: resolution root cause + SOTA backbone blueprint (BHITK camera-pose tracker)
author: modelling
summary: ## 2D reconstruction: resolution diagnosis + the backbone revamp blueprint (SOTA-informed) ### Where we are (committed thru 8bc8bfc + WIP) detect_avatars (rail-bounded, count-aware) -> per-frame rail …
text:
2d reconstruction: resolution root cause + sota backbone blueprint (bhitk camera-pose tracker) cv aerial reconstruction homography handoff ## 2d reconstruction: resolution diagnosis + the backbone revamp blueprint (sota-informed)

### where we are (committed thru 8bc8bfc + wip)
detect_avatars (rail-bounded, count-aware) -> per-frame rail (select_running_rail) -> project to s,perp
-> odometer-anchored arclen (odo = head m-to-finish, confirmed at the finish: f2735 shows "20m" + the
finish line, field ~20m back; ocr verified: precision 100%, recall ~88%, interp-covered) -> metric-
space tracklet association with the odometer as the motion prior (longest track 1216 frames, top
304/290/237; 538->202 fragments). y_lat is positive distance from the rail.

### resolution root cause (studies/cv_aerial_track_id.py pass4 cv_recon_res.png)
within stable straights resolution is good (smooth perp/s). damage is at: (1) steep-oblique bends /
the home turn f2196-2316 (f2256 = 340m: low oblique on a sharp bend, rail barely visible, heavy
foreshortening) -> per-frame rail fit unstable + single global px->m scale wrong -> tens-of-px jumps;
(2) head-reference jitter (anchoring to max(s), a single jittery lead detection -> offset baseline
snaps to 0); (3) isolated outlier spikes.

### the revamp (sota literature, all cpu) — bhitk-style camera-pose tracker over the rigid track plane
per-frame map is not a free 8-dof homography (degenerate on straights, our 0099 finding) but a
constrained camera pose+focal (cv2.solvepnp, z=0 track plane). layers:
  (a) per-frame constrained pose from rail lines (inner + outer at the known 22.5 m offset) + odometer
      + distance poles;
  (b) dense-relative init: lk optical flow on background -> estimateaffinepartial2d similarity
      (pan/rotate/zoom) carries the previous pose as the init -> the temporal init 0099 said was
      missing (fixes the oblique-bend local minima);
  (c) temporal smoothing of the camera trajectory via ekf/rts -> reuse reconstruction/fusion.py
      kalman+rts (same forward/backward pattern, on the camera not the horses). gtsam factor graph +
      oval loop-closure (railgeometry closure gap) only if it drifts over a lap.
why it fixes everything: positions read off the fixed metric track frame (no per-frame origin -> no
max(s) jitter, no bend level-shifts); homography gives a perspective-correct local px->m scale with
the 22.5 m rail separation as the metric ruler (resolves cv_recon §7 under-determination); pose-graph
is globally consistent; dynamics carry the pose through holes. render is true perspective (confirmed:
near horses larger than far on f2256), so pnp applies. avv is synthetic (no lens distortion) -> pose
model even cleaner.

### plan (proceeding with all)
- quick wins on the current pipeline (interim, low-risk): robust head reference (smoothed/percentile,
  not max), per-track outlier rejection + light smoothing. [local two-rail scale deferred -> subsumed
  by the backbone.]
- backbone: new studies/cv_pose_backbone.py: solvepnp pose + optical-flow init + ekf/rts over the
  camera, validated f1080 (straight) then f2256 (home turn), then promote to hkjc.reconstruction.

### key sota refs
bhitk arxiv:2311.10361 (sequential bayesian homography, sparse-absolute + dense-relative kalman) — the
direct analogue. pnlcalib arxiv:2404.08401 (points+lines, 3d model). tvcalib arxiv:2207.11709
(camera-model vs free homography). gtsam (factor graph, cpu). line-vs-point dlt (dubrofsky/woodham).

title: Pose backbone: core validated; free-homography smoothing fails -> solvePnP pose + EKF is the path
author: modelling
summary: ## Pose backbone (task #101): core validated, but FREE-homography smoothing fails -> need solvePnP Built studies/cv_pose_backbone.py: per-frame two-rail homography (track-plane inner b=0 + outer b=22.…
text:
pose backbone: core validated; free-homography smoothing fails -> solvepnp pose + ekf is the path cv aerial reconstruction homography handoff ## pose backbone (task #101): core validated, but free-homography smoothing fails -> need solvepnp

built studies/cv_pose_backbone.py: per-frame two-rail homography (track-plane inner b=0 + outer
b=22.5 m -> image), read each horse's metric lateral b via h^-1. the known 22.5 m rail separation is
the metric ruler; positions read off the fixed track plane (no per-frame s-origin, no s_head jitter,
perspective-correct scale).

### what works (core validated)
per-frame fit is clean where both rails are well-detected: f2440 resid 3.4 px (y_lat 3-14 m), f2200
15.8 px. across the race the lateral band is clean + physical in the dense-anchor regions
(f1800-2780: median ~4-9 m, tight). 1312 two-rail anchors over 2162 frames.

### what fails (the wall)
1. temporal carry freezes: on long one-rail stretches (outer rail undetected, ~845 frames) carrying
   prev_h froze -> a constant 22.5 m plateau (f1500-1620).
2. smoothing the raw 8 homography params + interpolating across anchors does not clean it: a
   homography is not a flat vector space (perspective terms h20/h21 tiny+sensitive, h02 ~hundreds), so
   median-smoothing breaks the geometry and interpolation across sparse anchors gives ramps. f600-1500
   stays jittery (median swinging 3-25 m).
3. root cause: the free 8-dof homography is too unstructured + the along-axis is degenerate on
   straights (two parallel rails don't fix along-position), so the icp correspondence slides and
   perturbs even the (over-determined) lateral.

### conclusion / next (per the sota, bhitk/pnlcalib/tvcalib — journal 0102)
must parametrize and smooth the camera pose, not the free homography: cv2.solvepnp for
rotation+translation+focal against the z=0 track plane (well-conditioned on straights because the
camera model removes the unconstrained dofs), then ekf/rts smoothing of the pose state (reuse
reconstruction/fusion.py kalman+rts), with optical-flow dense-relative as the pose dynamics. that is
the focused next build.

### meanwhile
the best current 2d recon is the main tracker (studies/cv_aerial_track_id.py): detect_avatars +
field-median running rail + odometer-anchored arclen + two-rail per-frame sep-scale y_lat + the
spike-audit validity gate. decent (bulk physical) but not production-clean; the solvepnp pose backbone
is what makes it good.
